ĐÁNH GIÁ CỦA HỘI ĐỒNG QUẢN TRỊ VỀ HOẠT ĐỘNG CỦA CÔNG 
TY 
1) Đánh giá của Hội đồng quản trị về các mặt hoạt động của Công ty, trong đó có 
đánh giá liên quan đến trách nhiệm môi trường và xã hội 
Năm 2023, một năm chịu nhiều khó khăn do tình trạng lạm phát vẫn còn cao khiến chi phí nguyên vật 
liệu đầu vào, làm gia tăng chi phí hoạt động và ảnh hưởng đến biên lợi nhuận của DORUCO. Với nỗ 
lực phấn đấu của Ban Lãnh đạo cùng toàn bộ công nhân viên và sự hỗ trợ từ Tập đoàn Công nghiệp 
Cao su Việt Nam cùng các cấp, ban, ngành tại địa phương đã giúp Công ty triển khai tốt các mục tiêu, 
kế hoạch đề ra và hướng tới năm 2024 được kỳ vọng sẽ giá cao su tự nhiên sẽ phục hồi, tăng giá giúp 
tình hình kinh doanh của DPR tích cực. Cụ thể:  
- 
Sản lượng khai thác vượt kế hoạch 4,91%; năng suất đạt 2,07 tấn/ha, giữ vững vị trí ở Top đầu 
trong Tập đoàn Công nghiệp cao su Việt Nam.  
- 
Tổng lợi nhuận sau thuế đạt 76,54% so với kế hoạch đề ra.  
- 
Thu nhập của cán bộ công nhân viên ổn định. 
- 
Vốn và tài sản của các cổ đông được sử dụng một cách hiệu quả, bảo toàn qua các năm. Đồng 
thời, Công ty cũng cân đối được nguồn đầu tư, bảo đảm hài hòa lợi ích của các cổ đông và có 
phần phân phối cho người lao động thông qua chính sách tiền lương và việc sử dụng quỹ khen 
thưởng, phúc lợi. Ngoài ra, Công ty luôn hoàn thành các nghĩa vụ thuế, nộp ngân sách đối với 
Nhà nước. 
HĐQT DORUCO luôn giữ vững tinh thần đoàn kết, tâm huyết với công ty và nhạy bén trước những 
biến động của thị trường. HĐQT dành nhiều thời gian nghiên cứu, thảo luận để đưa ra các chủ trương, 
nghị quyết phù hợp, góp phần định hướng phát triển cho công ty. Nhờ sự phối hợp nhịp nhàng giữa 
HĐQT và bộ máy chuyên môn, công tác điều hành được thực hiện hiệu quả, đảm bảo hoạt động công 
ty diễn ra suôn sẻ. 
Đối mặt với những khó khăn trong năm qua, HĐQT đã thể hiện sự đoàn kết, đồng lòng, cùng Ban điều 
hành kịp thời xử lý các vấn đề phát sinh. HĐQT cũng đóng góp ý kiến quan trọng trong việc định hướng 
chiến lược ngắn hạn và trung hạn cho sự phát triển bền vững của Công ty. 
2) Đánh giá của Hội đồng quản trị về hoạt động của Ban Tổng Giám đốc công ty 
- 
Căn cứ Điều lệ Công ty, Hội đồng Quản trị thực hiện giám sát Ban Tổng Giám đốc và các cán 
bộ quản lý khác trong điều hành công việc hằng ngày của Công ty. 
- 
Hội đồng Quản trị và Ban Tổng Giám đốc phối hợp hoạt động hiệu quả theo quy định của Điều 
lệ Công ty và Quy chế Quản trị Công ty. HĐQT đánh giá cao khả năng điều hành linh hoạt, 
quyết liệt và kịp thời của BĐT, góp phần đạt được kết quả kinh doanh tốt. BĐT đã hoàn thành 
xuất sắc các nhiệm vụ, Nghị quyết của HĐQT và kế hoạch sản xuất kinh doanh do Đại hội đồng 
cổ đông đề ra. Hoạt động điều hành kinh doanh của BĐT không gặp cản trở, đồng thời việc giám 
sát của HĐQT và Ban Kiểm soát được thực hiện thường xuyên, chặt chẽ, đảm bảo hoạt động 
của Công ty tuân thủ Nghị quyết của ĐHĐCĐ và HĐQT. Các thành viên HĐQT, BĐT và Ban 
Kiểm soát thực hiện quản trị Công ty theo chuẩn mực hiện đại, đề cao đạo đức nghề nghiệp và 
luôn hành động vì lợi ích của các cổ đông.

47 
 
- 
Hằng quý, Ban Tổng Giám đốc phải báo cáo Hội đồng quản trị về kết quả sản xuất kinh doanh, 
tiến độ thực hiện Nghị quyết HĐQT và những khó khăn, thuận lợi trong quá trình điều hành. 
Dựa vào báo cáo và tình hình thực tế, HĐQT sẽ tổ chức họp để đánh giá kết quả điều hành trong 
quý và đưa ra yêu cầu triển khai công việc mới theo Nghị quyết Đại hội đồng cổ đông. 
- 
Trong suốt năm vừa qua, Ban Tổng Giám đốc đã thực hiện đầy đủ trách nhiệm báo cáo, giải 
trình, công bố thông tin về tình hình hoạt động sản xuất kinh doanh một cách đầy đủ, minh bạch. 
Ban Tổng Giám đốc đã tuân thủ các yêu cầu về trình và xin ý kiến các nội dung thuộc thẩm 
quyền phê duyệt của Hội đồng quản trị tại các cuộc họp Hội đồng quản trị định kỳ và đột xuất. 
- 
Các hoạt động kinh doanh, nghiệp vụ hàng ngày đều được tuân thủ theo quy tắc tác nghiệp và 
quản lý. Trong năm 2023, tất cả các hoạt động sản xuất kinh doanh đều đảm bảo tuân thủ theo 
các quy định của pháp luật hiện hành. 
3) Các kế hoạch, định hướng của Hội đồng quản trị  
Năm 2024 sẽ là một năm đầy thử thách của Công ty trong tình hình chính trị và kinh tế thế giới có nhiều 
diễn biến phức tạp, trong bối cảnh kinh tế vi mô, vĩ mô có nhiều thay đổi. Công ty đã đề ra những biện 
pháp quyết liệt để ứng phó, xây dựng nhiều kịch bản trong sản xuất kinh doanh để thích nghi với tình 
hình mới. Chiến lược dài hạn ngoài mảng sản xuất cao su vẫn không thay đổi, công ty còn tập trung 
phát triển ngành sản xuất chế biến gỗ và đầu tư khu công nghiệp để tận dụng lợi thế về nguồn nguyên 
liệu và quỹ đất nông nghiệp khi được phép chuyển đổi. Về trung và ngắn hạn, Công ty sẽ tập trung vào 
những sản phẩm có giá bán tốt, nhu cầu của thị trường lớn. Đồng thời cải tiến dây chuyền công nghệ để 
giảm giá thành sản phẩm. Công ty tin tưởng sẽ vượt qua mọi khó khăn trở ngại để hoàn thành kế hoạch, 
tiến đến mục tiêu đã định. 
Nguồn lực chính của Công ty chủ yếu tập trung vào đội ngũ, nhân viên và người lao động cũng như quỹ 
đất hiện có. Trên nền tảng quỹ đất và diện tích khai thác có sẵn, Công ty sẽ tiếp tục phát triển mở rộng 
diện tích, tăng năng suất, tăng sản lượng mủ. Nguồn vốn của Công ty để hướng đến các chiến lược kinh 
doanh chủ yếu dựa vào nguồn vốn chủ sở hữu và các nguồn quỹ được hình thành từ lợi nhuận kinh 
doanh. Vì vậy năm 2024 là năm thách thức nhưng cũng có nhiều cơ hội đặt ra đối với HĐQT.  
Các biện pháp hoàn thành kế hoạch: 
Hội đồng Quản trị thực hiện nghiêm túc công việc quản trị Công ty theo đúng các quy định về Quản trị 
Công ty áp dụng cho các công ty đại chúng và Điều lệ, quy chế Quản trị của Công ty CPCS Đồng Phú. 
Các thành viên HĐQT thực hiện nhiệm vụ và quyền hạn của một thành viên HĐQT theo đúng Điều lệ, 
quy chế Quản trị của Công ty và sự phân công của Chủ tịch HĐQT một cách trung thực; tuân thủ các 
chuẩn mực hành vi, đạo đức nghề nghiệp của thành viên HĐQT; luôn hành động vì quyền lợi của công 
ty và các cổ đông công ty. 
Hội đồng Quản trị lãnh đạo và giám sát mọi hoạt động của Ban Tổng Giám đốc trên cơ sở tạo mọi điều 
kiện tốt nhất về cơ chế, chính sách, nguồn nhân lực, cơ sở vật chất để giúp Ban Tổng Giám đốc hoàn 
thành nhiệm vụ được giao. Hội đồng Quản trị hợp tác chặt chẽ với Ban Kiểm soát, đảm bảo cung cấp 
tất cả các tài liệu và thông tin cần thiết cho Ban Kiểm soát, tôn trọng tư cách khách quan độc lập của 
Ban Kiểm soát. Hội đồng Quản trị tạo điều kiện tốt nhất cho các thành viên Ban Kiểm soát trong việc 
thực hiện chức năng và nhiệm vụ của Ban Kiểm soát và chỉ đạo, giám sát việc chấn chỉnh, xử lý các sai 
phạm theo đề xuất của Ban Kiểm soát.

48 
 
Hội đồng quản trị, Ban Kiểm soát và Ban Tổng Giám đốc phối hợp chặt chẽ trong quan hệ công tác 
theo các nguyên tắc sau: 
- 
Luôn vì lợi ích của Công ty và các cổ đông; 
- 
Tuân thủ nghiêm túc các quy định có liên quan đến Pháp luật, Điều lệ, Quy chế Quản trị Công 
ty; 
- 
Thực hiện nguyên tắc tập trung, dân chủ, công khai, minh bạch; 
- 
Phối hợp công tác với tinh thần trách nhiệm cao nhất, trung thực, hợp tác và thường xuyên chủ 
động phối hợp tháo gỡ các vướng mắc, khó khăn.

Hàng tháng và quý, các thành viên Hội đồng Quản trị Công ty được báo cáo về tiến độ sản xuất kinh

Hoạt động của thành viên HĐQT độc lập: 
Là thành viên độc lập của HĐQT, bà Nguyễn Ngọc Thanh luôn thể hiện tinh thần trách nhiệm cao khi 
tham gia đầy đủ các cuộc họp và đóng góp tích cực vào hoạt động của HĐQT. Với kiến thức và kinh 
nghiệm uyên thâm, bà đã hoàn thành xuất sắc nhiệm vụ được giao, đồng thời đóng vai trò quan trọng 
trong việc giám sát và điều hành hoạt động của Công ty theo đúng định hướng phát triển. Trong quá 
trình công tác, bà luôn giữ vững tinh thần độc lập, đưa ra những ý kiến chuyên môn cao và chính xác, 
góp phần quan trọng vào hoạt động của HĐQT.

c) Hoạt động của Ban Kiểm soát 
Năm 2023 Ban Kiểm soát đã tổ chức triển khai hoạt động giám sát theo kế hoạch đã được đại hội đồng 
cổ đông 2023 thông qua. Ban Kiểm soát thực hiện giám sát Hội đồng Quản trị, Ban Tổng Giám đốc 
trong việc quản lý và điều hành công ty; kiểm tra tính hợp lý, hợp pháp, tính trung thực và mức độ cẩn 
trọng trong quản lý, điều hành hoạt động sản xuất kinh doanh, trong tổ chức công tác tài chính - kế toán; 
thực hiện thẩm định báo cáo tình hình kinh doanh, báo cáo tài chính bán niên và báo cáo tài chính năm 
của công ty, báo cáo của Hội đồng Quản trị và Tổng Giám đốc.  
Ban Kiểm soát giám sát và đánh giá tình hình thực hiện các chỉ tiêu kế hoạch sản xuất kinh doanh 2023, 
các chỉ tiêu tài chính, bảo toàn và phát triển vốn; giám sát việc xây dựng và thực hiện các định mức 
kinh tế kỹ thuật, các giải pháp nhằm đạt mục tiêu nghị quyết ĐH cổ đông.

d) Đánh giá việc thực hiện các quy định về quản trị Công ty 
Công ty Cổ phần Cao su Đồng Phú luôn đề cao công tác quản trị, tuân thủ nghiêm ngặt quy định pháp 
luật và nội bộ. Công ty thường xuyên cập nhật thông lệ quốc tế, áp dụng phù hợp để tối ưu hiệu quả 
hoạt động. Các quy định của Ủy ban Chứng khoán Nhà nước và Sở Giao dịch Chứng khoán TP.HCM 
được cập nhật và triển khai nghiêm túc. HĐQT quan tâm và khuyến khích cán bộ tham gia tập huấn 
nâng cao năng lực quản trị do các tổ chức uy tín tổ chức.

MWG được vinh danh tại AGM Awards 2026 với hai hạng mục quan trọng về quản trị doanh nghiệp
Công ty Cổ phần Đầu tư Thế Giới Di Động (MWG) vừa được vinh danh
tại AGM Awards 2026 với hai hạng mục gồm “Đại hội đồng cổ đông của năm” và “Top 10 Đại hội đồng cổ đông thường niên tiêu biểu 2026 – Nhóm vốn hóa
lớn”.
AGM Awards là chương trình đánh giá
thường niên do CafeF phối hợp cùng VIOD – Viện Thành
viên Hội đồng Quản trị Việt Nam tổ chức nhằm ghi nhận các doanh nghiệp niêm yết có chất
lượng tổ chức Đại hội đồng cổ đông (ĐHĐCĐ) nổi bật, hướng đến các chuẩn mực
quản trị hiện đại, minh bạch và nâng cao trải nghiệm cổ đông trên thị trường
vốn Việt Nam.
K ết
quả AGM Awards 2026 được xây dựng dựa trên quá trình đánh giá độc lập đối với
công tác tổ chức đại hội thực tế, chất lượng tài liệu đại hội, mức độ minh bạch
trong công bố thông tin cũng như hiệu quả tương tác với cổ đông và nhà đầu tư.
Việc được ghi nhận đồng thời ở hai hạng
mục quan trọng cho thấy những nỗ lực liên tục của MWG trong việc nâng cao chất
lượng quản trị doanh nghiệp và hoạt động quan hệ nhà đầu tư. Trong những năm
gần đây, MWG tập trung đẩy mạnh tính minh bạch, chuẩn hóa hoạt động công bố
thông tin, ứng dụng công nghệ trong tổ chức đại hội và nâng cao trải nghiệm
tham dự dành cho cổ đông.
Đặc biệt, hạng mục “Đại hội đồng cổ
đông của năm” ghi nhận những đổi mới của MWG trong cách thức tổ chức ĐHĐCĐ
theo hướng chuyên nghiệp, hiệu quả và tăng cường kết nối với cộng đồng nhà đầu
tư. Đại hội không chỉ là hoạt động quản trị thường niên mà còn trở thành diễn
đàn đối thoại cởi mở, nơi doanh nghiệp chia sẻ định hướng chiến lược, kế hoạch
phát triển và cam kết tạo dựng giá trị dài hạn cho cổ đông.
Trong bối cảnh thị trường chứng khoán
Việt Nam đang hướng tới mục tiêu nâng hạng, AGM Awards được kỳ vọng sẽ tiếp tục
thúc đẩy cộng đồng doanh nghiệp nâng cao chuẩn mực quản trị, minh bạch hóa hoạt
động và củng cố niềm tin của nhà đầu tư đối với thị trường vốn Việt Nam.
Đối với MWG, các giải thưởng lần này là
sự ghi nhận đáng trân trọng, đồng thời là động lực để doanh nghiệp tiếp tục
hoàn thiện năng lực quản trị, nâng cao chất lượng hoạt động IR và phát triển
bền vững trong dài hạn.

MWG Honored At AGM Awards 2026 With Two Major Corporate Governance Achievements
Mobile World Investment Corporation (MWG) has recently been
honored at the AGM Awards 2026 with two prestigious recognitions: “Shareholders’ Meeting of the Year” and “ Top 10 Outstanding Annual General
Shareholders Meetings 2026 – Large Capitalization Group ”.
AGM Awards is an annual evaluation program jointly organized
by CafeF and VIOD – Vietnam Institute of Directors to recognize listed
companies that demonstrate excellence in organizing General Meetings of
Shareholders (GMS), while promoting modern governance standards, transparency,
and enhanced shareholder experience in Vietnam’s capital market.
The results of AGM Awards 2026 were developed through an
independent assessment process covering the actual organization of shareholder
meetings, the quality of meeting materials, the level of transparency in
information disclosure, as well as the effectiveness of engagement with
shareholders and investors.
Receiving recognition in two major categories highlights
MWG’s continuous efforts to improve its corporate governance practices and
investor relations activities. In recent years, MWG has focused on
strengthening transparency, standardizing information disclosure practices,
applying technology in shareholder meeting organization, and enhancing the
participation experience for shareholders.
In particular, the “Shareholders’ Meeting of the Year” award
recognizes MWG’s innovations in organizing General Meetings of Shareholders in
a more professional, efficient, and investor-oriented manner. The meeting has
evolved beyond a routine corporate governance activity into an open dialogue
platform where the company shares its strategic direction, development plans,
and commitment to creating long-term value for shareholders.
As Vietnam’s stock market continues progressing toward
market upgrade goals, AGM Awards is expected to further encourage the business
community to enhance governance standards, improve transparency, and strengthen
investor confidence in Vietnam’s capital market.
For MWG, these awards represent both a meaningful
recognition and a strong motivation for the company to continue enhancing its
governance capabilities, improving the quality of investor relations (IR)
activities, and pursuing sustainable long-term development.

MWG was recognized among the "Top 10 Large-Cap Best Corporate Governance Companies 2023" and "Best Annual General Meeting (AGM) Organizing Enterprise."
Home
News
MWG was recognized among the "Top 10 Large-Cap Best Corporate Governance Companies 2023" and "Best Annual General Meeting (AGM) Organizing Enterprise."
Mobile World Investment Corporation (HOSE: MWG) proudly secured a place in the "Top 10 Best Corporate Governance Companies" (large capitalization group) and "Best Annual General Meeting (AGM) Organizing Enterprise" categories at the 2023 Listed Company Voting organized by HoSE.
On December 15, 2023, the event was integrated with the Annual Listed Company Conference 2023, featuring the participation of key figures from the State Securities Commission, Stock Exchanges, the Vietnam Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation, as well as representatives from nearly 300 listed enterprises, securities firms, fund management companies, and other financial institutions in the market.
The judging panel emphasized that the corporate governance scores reflected progress and an increasing focus on practical governance activities. Currently, companies show differences in the level of compliance with standard criteria. Specifically, 66% of companies meet compliance criteria, while nearly 26% meet standard criteria.
Additionally, the evaluation results show that the compliance rate with governance criteria ranges from 62.9% to 72.3%, depending on the capitalization group (larger capitalized companies tend to comply better with legal standards), and the compliance with standard criteria ranges from 21.1% to 42.1% (smaller capitalized companies tend to comply less with standard criteria).
In 2023, MWG was honored in the "Top 100 Most Valuable Brands in Vietnam 2023," "Top 10 Strongest Brands in Vietnam 2023," "Top 10 Largest Private Enterprises in Vietnam," "Top 10 Reputable Retail Companies in 2023," "Top 100 Best Places to Work in Vietnam 2023," and for the second consecutive year in the Top 50 Most Sustainable Development Companies in Vietnam and Top 20 Companies with the Highest VNSI Sustainable Development Index in Vietnam. This recognition affirms and acknowledges the state and market's recognition of MWG's business management model as it increasingly aligns with the highest standards, becomes more transparent, modern, and aims for sustainable development, balancing economic interests with social and environmental responsibilities, and committing to a sustainable future.
The criteria for evaluating corporate governance were developed based on Vietnamese legal regulations on corporate governance and good governance practices based on G20/OECD corporate governance principles, the Vietnam Corporate Governance Code (VCGS), and the ASEAN Corporate Governance Scorecard.
The evaluation criteria for corporate governance items were developed separately based on the OECD corporate governance principles, focusing on five principles: shareholder rights, fair treatment of shareholders, disclosure of information and transparency, the responsibility of the board of directors, and sustainable development and resilience.
This year, the OECD has added new rules on corporate governance, emphasizing the integration of the 3 ESG aspects (environment, social, and governance). This is seen as the first step for new requirements on corporate governance in the context of the government's strong commitments to reducing emissions, dealing with climate change, and sustainable development over the past two years following the COP26 conference. The aspect of sustainability and resilience is an essential content in the G20/OECD Corporate Governance Principles issued in 2023.

CHAIRMAN’S MESSAGE
Dear Valued Shareholders, Customers
and Partners,
In 2019, the world economy experienced the lowest 
growth in the decade. The US-China economic conflict 
was the major reason as it damaged the prospects of 
global investment, production, and trade. In addition, 
the increase of geopolitical tensions in the Middle 
East and Asia, policy instability in Europe and the US 
and continuous decline in some emerging markets 
also reduced overall growth.   
In that context, Vietnam still sustained its growth 
momentum with a GDP increase of 7.03% while 
maintaining low inflation. However, in 2019, the 
Agriculture, Forestry, and Aquaculture sectors 
sharply declined as of 2018 reaching a growth of only 
2.2% compared to 3.76% in previous years. The main 
reasons were the African swine fever, the drought in 
the Central Highlands, and the decline in the export 
price of key products.
Predicting the situation, from the beginning of the 
year, the Board of Directors focused on investment 
in the Group’s internal production capacity to 
create a platform that is able to adapt to difficulties 
generated from climate change and the pressures 
of competition. As a result, a series of production 
facilities were built and put into operation in this 
year such as a vegetable and flower seed center in 
Lam Dong, a confectionery factory in Long An, an 
industrial center for seeds and agricultural products 
processing in Dong Thap and an expanded high-
tech shrimp farming area in Soc Trang. Ending 
2019, although the consolidated earnings after tax 
decreased compared to that of the same period last 
year, the earnings after tax from core business still 
increased by 15%. The consolidated gross profit 
margin increased to 21% in 2019 compared to 18% 
in 2018. 
In particular, 2019 was the year marking our 
completion of the value chain platform “Farm-Food-
Family” through the establishment of PAN Consumer 
Goods Distribution JSC (PAN CG). This was an 
important initiative that sent the PAN’s agricultural 
and food products to domestic and world consumers. 
Furthermore, we also officially participated in the 
coffee business segment by the acquisition of 80% 
shares of Golden Beans Coffee JSC (owns Shin 
Cà Phê brand), at the same time increasing our 
ownership of 584 Nha Trang Seafood JSC to make it 
one of the Group’s subsidiaries. 
With the strategy of sustainable development 
based on full value chains to improve Vietnamese 
agriculture, the PAN’s products have confirmed 
their quality and have conquered not only domestic 
consumers but also highly demanding markets 
such as the US, Europe, and Japan, etc. Clear 
evidence of the effectiveness of this strategy was the 
restructuring of the cashew business which created 
branded and high added value products and 
attained quarterly profit growth in 2019. The 
quality of the PAN’s products was further 
confirmed when the PAN group was the only 
agricultural corporation chosen to be “The 
Special Sponsor of conferences and events in 
the ASEAN VIETNAM 2020” by the Government.
Stepping into 2020, the whole world was faced 
with the Covid-19 pandemic which negatively 
and heavily affected the socio-economic life 
of most countries as well as all corporations. 
Therefore, the Group’s strengthening of 
core competencies and implementation of a 
thorough sustainable development strategy 
was our significant preparation against 
difficulties. The Board of Directors will work 
closely with the Board of Management to 
adapt to disease situations and proactively 
make contingency plans. We believe that all 
members of the Group will work together to 
overcome such difficulties, continue to invest 
in production and business activities and 
create more value reservations for the benefit 
of shareholders, employees, and the whole 
community. 
Respectfully,
Chairman
Nguyen Duy Hung
WE BELIEVE THAT ALL MEMBERS OF THE GROUP WILL WORK TOGETHER TO

2019 Journey
Don Duong Young Plant Center in Don 
Duong district, Lam Dong is the result of 
the cooperation between PAN-HULIC and 
its Japanese partner Jadin – one of the top 
seed companies in Japan. The objective 
of the project is to produce high-quality 
agricultural products, to boost exports and 
to serve the domestic market. This will be 
the place to produce more than 100 kinds 
of copyrighted flowers and vegetables, 
which meet the strict quality standards of 
the export markets.
With the advantage of a closed fish breeding 
circuit, the Group can meet the strict 
standards of demanding markets. In 2019, 
Aquatex Ben Tre - a member company 
of the group became one of the largest 
catfish exporters to the Japanese market. 
The company’s export value to this market 
increased by more than 80%, bringing the 
proportion of exports to Japan from 18% in 
2017 to 37.3% in 2019. Value-added products 
accounted for more than 20% of the export 
value.
In 2018, in the business of raw cashew 
products, 
the 
Group 
made 
a 
bold 
transformation: focusing on developing 
branded products with high added value 
and organic materials to move towards a 
long-lasting business model. After a period 
of transformation, business efficiency has 
improved markedly, profits returned, and 
increased gradually each quarter instead 
of losses, while risks in production and 
business activities were minimized.
In the 3rd quarter of 2019, the Group 
officially made 584 Nha Trang a subsidiary. 
This contributed to the preservation of 
the traditional fish sauce industry and 
the expansion and development of a 
business under the common strategy. The 
PAN Group has helped 584 Nha Trang to 
develop raw material areas for traditional 
fish sauce in Nha Trang, Ca Na, and Phan 
Ri, focusing on promoting investment in 
developing production capacity at these 
facilities.
Golden Beans with the brand of Shin Cà 
Phe is considered as a suitable candidate 
for a development plan focused on 
quality products and the closed value 
chain business of the Group. With our 
advantages, PAN will help Shin Cà Phê 
further expand its material areas and 
develop its products. In addition, Shin Cà 
Phê also benefits from a network of over 
150,000 domestic sales points and export 
markets to dozens of countries.
Inaugurated by Vinaseed in December 
2019 after 8 months of construction, this 
is the largest and most modern center in 
the field of seed and rice in Vietnam as 
well as Southeast Asia with an area of 5 
hectares, a processing capacity of 30,000 
tons of seeds and 60,000 tons of rice per 
year, and a total investment of over VND 
300 billion. The project is an important 
element in the Group’s strategy to build 
quality rice chains, with greater scale and 
sustainability.
PAN Consumer Goods Distribution Joint 
Stock Company (PAN CG) was established 
in June 2019 with the first goal of 
distributing PAN Group’s agricultural and 
food products, then expand to products of 
equivalent quality from its partners. 
PAN CG owns a distribution network 
covering nearly 100% of modern selling 
points across 63 provinces and cities, has 
800 employees, and partner with more 
than 145,000 retail stores.
Opened in October 2019, Western Bibica is 
the fourth Bibica factory with an area of over 
50,000 m2, and a total investment of VND 
1,000 billion. This is a milestone marking 
the energetic development of Bibica in 
the coming time and making further 
development possible. It will contribute 
to the diversification of the confectionery 
supply, which will help maintain the 
domestic market and enable Bibica’s 
products to compete directly with imported 
goods. Besides, the factory is expected to 
provide new high-quality products for both 
domestic and export markets.
In 2019, Sao Ta Foods Joint Stock Company joined and won a project 
which had an investment in shrimp farming of the People’s Committee 
of Soc Trang Province. The project has an area of 90 hectares, is situated 
near the existing shrimp farm. It takes advantage of a simplified 
management system and the available process of the same farming 
infrastructure. With this project, Sao Ta will harvest an additional 2,000 
tons of shrimp annually. This helps the company reach a raw materials 
self-supply level of 30% which is internationally certified.

1. KEY AGRICULTURAL 
PRODUCTS
THE GROUP’S PRODUCTS 
ARE CHARACTERIZED BY

Key products and services
1.1. Crop seed
RICE SEEDS
Conventional varieties: popular varieties, currently dominating 
the domestic market, include Thien Uu 8, RVT, Dai thom 8, VS1, 
Du Huong, and Tran Trau Huong.
Hybrid varieties:  these varieties are quality-certified and 
include TH3-4, Thuy Huong, Bac Uu 64, Bac Uu 903, Nhi Uu 63, 
Nhị Uu 86B, and PAC 807.
CORN SEEDS
In 2018, Vinaseed focused on developing fresh glutinous and 
sweet corn varieties for the domestic market. These varieties 
currently enjoy market dominance due to the high productivity 
and adaptability of the seed and the attractive and flavorful end 
product. Popular corn varieties include purple glutinous corn 
(HN66), hybrid glutinous corn (HN88), HN68, single hybrid 
glutinous corn (MX10), and MX6.
VEGETABLE SEEDS
Although Vinaseed’s vegetable seed varieties are still limited, 
they have been well-received by the market. The company has 
recently helped diversify the produce available in Vietnam by 
contributing a number of melon varieties. Popular vegetable 
seeds include heat-tolerant cucumber Sakura, Red Pumpkin 
(Pum1664, Pum1628m, and Pum1631); hybrid gourd (F1), Bog 
16 Watermelon (WAM 14123 annd WAM 14127), and hybrid bitter 
melon (F1: Big 6131).
FLOWER SEED AND YOUNG PLANTS  
In 2019, PAN invested in a research and production center 
for seed and young plants in Don Duong, Lam Dong. This is a 
project of cooperation with Jardin (Japan) through copyright 
transfer contracts to produce flower seeds for Vietnam and Asia 
markets. Specifically, the 1 ha greenhouse area with Japanese 
technology will be the place to test over 100 flower varieties and 
perform the initial phase of the cooperation plan. According to 
the group’s trategy, in the next 5 years, it is possible to produce 
seeds to create 20-30 million export flower branches.
1.2. Agricultural products
FRESH CUT FLOWERS
PAN-Saladbowl produces and exports over 40 varieties of 
chrysanthemums (Kindly, Silvia, Celebrate, Olive, Lenior, 
Matissie, Colonge, Dante, Pinky rock, Copa, Muse, etc.) and 
20 varieties of carnation (Borja, Babylon, Apolo, Americano, 
etc.) to Japan. The flowers have beautiful colors and can be 
kept fresh for up to 20 days.
STRAWBERRY
After research and experimental cultivation since mid-
2018, the first strawberries were officially harvested 
in the fourth quarter of 2019 in Lam Dong. In order to 
get these strawberries, the product development and 
research process is conducted rigorously and thoroughly 
from selecting seeds, planting trials to verifying product 
quality. The project is supported by the Japan International 
Cooperation Agency (JICA).
CUCUMIS MELON
Taking advantage of technology transfers from Japan, our 
melons are cultivated under a strictly controlled conditions. 
PAN-Saladbowl offers Global GAP Standard products  for 
domestic consumption and export to international markets 
including Japan, Singapore, and Dubai.
PACKAGED RICE  
Ban Mai Rice: Ban Mai rice is produced from purebred rice, 
which is a clean fresh rice product produced in a closed 
manner from the selection of good varieties, under strict 
management. Immediately after harvesting, the rice is 
transferred to the modern drying and processing system of 
VinaRice (in Dong Thap), ensuring 100% freshness. Ban Mai 
rice meets the VietGap standards, on a completely closed, 
modern Japanese processing line.
VJ Pearl, VJ Japonica: these varieties are grown from a 
strictly controlled seed stock and are cultivated, harvested, 
and processed using technologies developed for the 
Japanese market. These processing techniques ensure the 
maintenance of nutritional value and natural aroma.
RVT rice: Vinaseed has identifed the most viable agricultural 
areas for mass production of RVT rice. In these areas, 
seed selection, soil preparation, and irrigation are strictly 
controlled. Postharvest processing is done using German 
and Japanese equipment to yield a product that meets the 
most stringent market requirements. 
Special rice (red rice, black rice): these products are rich in 
bioactive substances, fiber, protein, vitamins, minerals, and 
micronutrients. These products protect the body’s ability to 
regulate blood pressure, control cardiovascular functions, 
and stabilize blood sugar levels.
1.3. Agrochemicals
Since 1996 Vietnam Fumigation Company (VFC) has provided 
farmers with high-quality agrochemical products. These are 
processed and distributed from companies in the US, Japan, 
Switzerland, and Israel. 
1.4. Fumigation and pest control

I. THE AGRICULTURAL SEGMENT
In seed segment, demand risk refers to the possibility of lower than expected 
consumer demand for a firm’s products or services. This risk is realized 
whenever the Group loses access to, share within, or fail to penetrate, a target 
market. The market is small and split between 260 companies. Each province has 
its own seeds, with no truly dominant varieties, and the product quality is uneven. 
Domestic producers have to compete with standardized, high-quality imports 
sold by larger and more organized agribusinesses. All of these factors lead to 
low  competitiveness and low price – both embodiments of realized demand risk. 
For agrochemicals segment, realization of demand risk also tends to result 
from competition. Aside from this, there are reputational threats that menace 
the industry generally. Over the past few years, the agrochemicals market has 
been scandalized by the sale of fake and/or counterfeit goods. The scandals have 
created hesitation in the minds of potential customers, leading to lower revenue.
In export flowers segment, faces less imminent demand risks because Group 
has signed a contract to import their entire crop. In addition, Group’s flower 
production will likely only meet half of the Japanese partner’s demand. 
Operational risk is the possibility that a firm will suffer losses greater than forecast from 
insufficient internal processes or external events beyond its control.  Adverse weather is an 
important operational risk that directly threatens the core production activities of Group. When 
such risk is realized, it reduces crop yield, crop quality, and tends to result in increased seed 
consumption. Vietnam’s central highlands are ideal for certain kinds of cultivation; however, 
they are also home to frequent damaging rainstorms and periodic droughts, both of which 
have a negative impact on agricultural operations. 
Solutions to minimize risk: 
To minimize operational risks, especially those posed by adverse weather events, Group has 
expanded, and will continue to expand, its production areas into different ecological zones. It 
has also maintained warehouses in Dong Van and Ba Vi since 2015, where it stockpiles goods 
to ensure continuity of production in case of supply disruption. Finally, Group is researching 
and developing products with cold, drought, pest and disease resistance properties to reduce 
the impact of natural disasters and climate change on crop yields.
In export flowers, conducts most of its planting and growing operations in Belgian and 
Dutch greenhouses, complemented by Israeli irrigation and dike systems. This makes their 
operations less likely to be affected by adverse weather.

II. FOOD SEGMENT
Supply risk is the possibility that a firm will be unable to 
source the raw materials it requires for its basic activities. 
The most fundamental and troubling source of supply 
risk in Vietnam’s agricultural sector is the increasing 
scarcity and fragmentation of land. We cannot grow crops 
if we do not have adequate amounts or concentrations of 
land on which to grow them. Vietnam’s agricultural land 
is highly fragmented due to the nature of the terrain, 
high population density, land allocations, culture, and 
history. The area available for cultivation shrinks gradually 
every year due to urbanization and industrialization. The 
reduction of available hectarage has had consequences 
for all Vietnamese agriculture, but especially for rice 
production.
This segment is primarily exposed to demand risk and 
supply risk, the former from ever-changing consumer 
preferences, and the latter from unpredictable changes in 
the prices of production inputs. Competitive pressure from 
large market entrants is also an important consideration. 
In cashew processing, the Vietnamese cashew nut harvest 
runs from February to May every year and coincides with 
the beginning of the rainy season. If the harvest goes 
poorly, or if the crop is poorly handled post-harvest, the 
cashew nuts will not dry properly, lowering their quality. 
The quality of imported cashew nuts, mainly from African 
countries, is also affected by less-than-ideal weather and 
transport conditions. 
Regarding the coffee segment, business activities are also 
exposed to risks from fluctuating prices of raw coffee. 
Although Vietnam is the second largest coffee exporter in 
the world in terms of output, the price of raw materials is 
unstable but fluctuates erratically, depending on the world 
coffee price.
In confectionery segment, production is highly dependent 
on raw materials like starch, sugar and butter. However, 
the price of these raw materials has been, and is forecast 
to remain, low and stable.

III. MARKET RISKS
Market risks arise from the possibility of loss caused by 
adverse moves in interest rates, exchange rates, market 
liquidity, and stock prices. Market risk management aims to 
keep those risks within acceptable bounds while maximizing 
profits. The main market risks managed by The PAN Group 
include:
Price Risk: Stock Price Risk
Price risk is the chance of loss resulting from a negative 
change in the value of a portfolio. 
Since pivoting to focus on the agriculture and food sectors, 
The PAN Group’s investments are all long-term and 
strategic. For The PAN Group’s holdings, therefore, the risk 
of meaningful negative stock price fluctuations is not very 
high.
Solutions to minimize risk
The PAN Group manages price risk using Value at Risk 
(VAR), establishing conservative investment limits, and 
diversifying the investment portfolio. The PAN Group’s 
investment sub-committee is responsible for considering 
and approving investment decisions in stocks. They focus 
on buying the stock of companies that have good internal 
operations, reasonable price-to-earnings ratios, and other 
metrics indicating stability. 
Stock price risk is regularly reviewed by the Finance-
Accounting department and the Chief Finance Officer.
Commodity price risks
The PAN Group and its subsidiaries operate in many 
different fields that are sensitive to the price of commodities: 
agriculture, seafoods. Adverse commodity price fluctuations 
are a realization of supply risk when member companies 
require these commodities as inputs. They are realizations 
of demand risk whenever a member needs to sell materials 
it produces to a third party. Rapid changes in commodity 
prices can damage The PAN Group’s business and 
operations.
Solutions to minimize risk
The PAN Group manages commodity price risks through 
carefully monitoring domestic and foreign markets, 
ensuring timely commodity purchases, production planning, 
and prudent stockpiling. 
Risks related to commodity price fluctuations are monitored 
by the purchasing department, the production departments 
of subsidiaries, and reported to Director of Production and 
Chief Executive Officer on a weekly basis.
Exchange rate risk
Exchange rate risk is the risk of loss due to adverse changes in exchange 
rates and it arises whenever The PAN Group or affiliates engage in 
transactions denominated in currencies other than the Vietnamese 
Dong. The PAN Group is exposed to this risk through its subsidiaries and 
affiliates engaged in import and export and whenever they raise foreign 
capital.
Solutions to minimize risks
The PAN Group estimates exchange rate risk through the issuance of 
shares for capital increase and has adjustment policies for incomes with 
foreign currency elements, export mechanisms, and trade credit. Import 
and export plans are carefully developed to limit exchange rate risk.

A. AGRICULTURAL SEGMENT
Market highlights
Vietnam’s GDP increased 7.02% in 2019. However, the GDP 
of agriculture sector grew only 0.61%, the lowest level in 
the last 10 years (2011-2019) due to the severe impacts of 
climate change and unfavorable market conditions.
Weather in 2019 was unfavorable for agricultural production 
because of the El Nino phenomenon. Some negative impacts 
were higher temperatures during the year (0.5 - 2°C higher 
than the normal annual average), prolonged and extreme 
heat, one-month late arrival of rainy season, and significant 
decline of rainfall, especially in Central Vietnam and the 
Central Highlands (50% less than the typical annual average). 
These conditions, together with saltwater intrusion in the 
South, has led to a decrease in the cultivatable area and 
productivity to the lowest level in 5 years. According to the 
General Statistics Office, the total cultivated area of rice was 
estimated at 7.47 million hectares, down 1.4% compared to 
2018. In addition, the winter cultivated area of corn reduced 
to 500 thousand hectares, down 50% compared to the same 
period.  Total rice production reached 43.45 million tons, 
which had declined by 596 thousand tons. Corn production 
also decreased by about 3%, equivalent to 117 thousand 
tons.
Meanwhile, the market for agricultural exports was negative 
and the prices stayed low. The total value of Vietnam’s 
agricultural exports in 2019 is estimated at US $ 18.5 
billion, down 5.3% compared to last year. Export value of 
main commodities such as rice, coffee, pepper and cashew 
all decreased. According to the Ministry of Agriculture and 
Rural Development, rice exports in the first 10 months of 
2019 were estimated at 5.56 million tons and US $ 2.43 
billion, up 6.1% in volume but down 9.1% in value compared 
to the same period in 2018. The average export price in 
the first 10 months declined by 13.4% to 435.6 USD/ton, 
mainly because our main markets like China, Indonesia and 
Bangladesh have been oversupplied. 
The unfavorable weather and the market conditions have 
caused great difficulties for farmers. The uncultivated land 
is increasing, especially in the Northern provinces, where 
agricultural production is not economically efficient. This 
trend has affected seed demands in 2019.

In December 2019, in the Truong Xuan commune, Thap Muoi district, the Industrial 
center for seeds and agricultural products processing was officially inaugurated 
and put into production after only 7 months of construction. The center is located 
in ab area of 5,2 hectares and has a total investment of VND 342 billion. The project 
aims to build a sustainable rice value chain from research – breeding- producing 
- harvesting - processing and product distribution. The center has 2 factories: 
an agricultural seed processing factory with an annual capacity of 50,000 tons 
(equivalent to 40% of current capacity); and a rice processing factory with an 
annual capacity of 100,000 tons (which meets the FSSC22000 standard qualified). 
The project includes 25,000 m2 of factory and warehouse, and a drying system 
with a capacity of 300 tons/batch equipped with with modern and fully automated

In addition, the sustainable rice value chain from seed research to distributing 
final products with high quality to consumers will bring more added value for the 
company.

By the end of 2019, the net revenue from pangasius and 
clam reached VND 361 billion, down 8.8% YoY, mainly 
because the PAN group continued to reduce the clam 
production and focus on pangasius export (accounting for 
75.5% of the revenue). According to VASEP, the company’s 
revenue reduction was lower than the general industry fall. 
Net profit decreased by 27.1% YoY to VND 48.6 billion due 
to low export prices and raw materials price increase over 
a long period of time. In addition, the company had to make 
a provision for breeding fishes.
Given the difficulties in consumption, though the company 
continues to pursue a sustainable development strategy to 
limit the impacts. Accordingly, it is focusing on high value-
added products in order to maintain stable profit margins 
and build long-term relationships with existing as well as 
new customers. As a result, the revenue of the products 
grew by 9% over the same period.
The PAN group identified that Japan is still a key market 
because of its higher demand due to the 2020 Olympics. 
Export to Japan increased by 6% YoY. Regarding the EU 
market, it aimed to maintain stable partnerships with long-
term customers and only focus on orders with suitable 
prices and payment conditions.
In addition, the company also concentrated on developing 
the closed production chain as set out in its sustainable 
development strategy. Its pangasius harvest volumes 
increased 14% YoY thanks to the successful application of 
R&D which has continued to improve output.
Vietnam’s shrimp and pangasius segment had been 
through many difficulties in 2019. It is expected that 
the situation will not improve quickly in 2020 due to the 
Covid-19 outbreak which will negatively affect the economy 
and consumer buying behaviors. However, demand for 
seafood might be higher  as pork and poultry supply is 
affected by African swine fever and bird flu in China. 
High-price inventories of 2018 are gradually being sold in 
2019 and the beginning of 2020. The EVFTA Agreement is 
expected to be approved by the European Parliament and 
Vietnam National Assembly in the first half of the year and 
will be effective from 2020. It will support the export to the 
EU market and bring great opportunities for Vietnam’s 
seafood products, especially processed products.
In 2019, shrimp exports reach USD 3.4 billion (-5.4% YoY). Export to the biggest 
markets such as EU and Japan were down 9.2% and 15.9%, respectively. However, 
the US market has recovered after the 2018 slump, with a slight increase of 2.5% 
to USD 654 million, of which the largest contribution to this growth is breaded 
shrimp products. Demand for shrimp in the Chinese market continued to increase 
with exports up 17.1%, especially in Q4/2019 due to Tet holiday. 
The average export price of Vietnam’s shrimp is still relatively low due to competition 
from cheap frozen shrimp suppliers such as India, Ecuador while inventories in 
importing countries are still high. The unfavorable weather in the last months of 
2019 and the shrimp outbreaks resulted in a sharp decrease in the qualified output 
and push up the price of raw shrimp. In December 2019 and early January 2020, 
there was a temporary slowdown in shrimp input demand of processing factories 
because they finished their production in Q4/2019 and prepared to close for Tet 
Holiday. Therefore, the price of raw white shrimp declined. 
Given the industry is expected to face more challenges in 
2020, the PAN Group strategy is to focus on improving its 
internal resources and completing the closed value chain. 
The success of its aquafarming activities in 2019 is the 
foundation to strengthen its self-supply of high quality, 
traceable and sustainable raw materials. Therefore, the 
company plans to invest more in facilities to improve the 
density and quality of the farming environment which helps 
to increase production output and reduce cost of goods 
sold. 
Regarding the processing, a modern cold storage is 
expected to be put into operation in the first quarter of 
2020, which will help to improve warehouse management 
efficiency. It also expands its production capacity of deep 
processing goods to meet the increasing demand.
In terms of product distribution, the PAN group is actively 
approaching new customers. It has signed some long term 
contracts and is negotiating with some supermarkets to 
supply deep-processed or ASC-certified products. The 
company plans to participate in major seafood expo in the 
EU, China, Japan, ... to introduce its key products and find 
new customers.

In 2019, despite a slight decrease of 2.5% in revenue, net profit from the shrimp segment still grew 
strongly by 27.7% YoY. Net profit margin increased by 1.5% to 6.2%. Amid the slowdown of the EU market 
and the drop of average selling price, the company’s managers promptly shifted to the US market (+ 
44% YoY) and Japan (+ 42% YoY), and focused on deep-processed products which its competitors such 
as India and Ecuador are unable to provide. The strategies effectively increased the company’s profit 
margin in the shrimp segment. In addition, instead of signing new contracts when raw material prices 
tended to rise, the company concentrated on orders from long-term customers with good prices and 
payment terms. 
2019 was a successful year for shrimp farming of the PAN Group as its harvest increased by 71% over 
the same period. The Board of Directors promptly took advantage of favorable weather to breed at 
high density, and applied R&D results. Thus, shrimp grew well, had fewer diseases and resulted in a 
better yield. As the farming cost was lower than the purchase price of external raw materials the profit 
margin of the segment increased.
With the success of the shrimp farming this year, the Group is confident to continue pursuing the closed 
production chain. It invested in a new shrimp farming area of 90 ha; therefore, the output is expected 
to double in the near future. The farming area is going to be completed in Q2/2020. In addition, a new 
cold storage will be put into operation in Q1/2020, so its storage capacity will double. This will help 
to reduce rental costs, improve warehouse management and make good impressions on customers. 
The company also plans to attend seafood fairs to approach new customers and technologies in the 
industry.

The cashew market has experienced a difficult year as 
the cashew export price remained at a low level. The 
average export price of cashew in 2019 reached US $ 
7,219 / ton, decreasing by 20% over the same period in 
2018. The cashew export value in 2019 was only US $

increasing by 22.1% over the same period. The demand 
for cashew nuts in the world has remained positive, and 
the level of consumption has continued to grow steadily 
over the years. China and Germany which are two of 
the largest export markets for cashews saw impressive 
growth in value at 30.4% and 21% respectively, while 
other markets including the US, the Netherlands and 
the UK all witnessed significant declines of 15.1%, 16% 
and 14% respectively due to a sharp fall in cashew 
import price.
Despite the difficult market conditions, the Group’s 
cashew business had a very positive business result, 
both in the fourth quarter and the whole year of 2019. 
The Group’s direction of promoting high value-added 
products has proved its effectiveness. Other value-added 
types of nuts also witnessed a strong growth. The sales 
of value-added products contributed 64% of the Group’s 
total nut revenue in 2019 and grew by 18.4% over the 
same period in 2018.
The Group attended the Food Expo event in the fourth 
quarter of 2019. In addition to reaching and introducing 
products to potential importers, the Group also 
introduced a new product of dried fruits in order to 
diversify its product portfolio beside its main product of 
cashew nut and to improve its revenue in the low demand 
time of cashew nuts (quarter 1 and quarter 2 every year).
In 2019, the revenue of the Nut segment decreased by 
18.3% over the same period in 2018, and fulfilled 87% of 
the plan, which mainly results from the Group’s control 
and limit of cashew business in the context of cashew 
kernel prices continuing to decline. The cashew kernel 
segment contributed only 33% of the total revenue of 
the Nut segment and decreased by 50% compared to 
the same period in 2018. The after-tax profit of the Nut 
business was VND 17.9 billion, exceeding the target 
by 42.4 % , which was completely contrasting to the 
negative business result of 2018 (VND -63.6 billion).

In November 2019, the Group officially entered the coffee industry by acquiring an 80% stake in Golden

The domestic market for roasted coffee is worth more than VND 7,700 billion with annual growth

industry are expected to be very positive.
SHIN Coffee is one of the famous specialty coffee brands in Vietnam market and owns a distinguishing 
business value chain in which there is strict control from managing raw materials to producing roasted 
coffee with a completely distinguished quality. The Group’s coffee plantations are stretching from the 
North to the South, including Son La, Khe Sanh, A Luoi, Pleiku, Da Lat and so on as the Group’s coffee 
flavours will vary depending on the growing region.
By capitalizing on the existing distribution network in the domestic and export markets as well as 
the distribution system of the Group’s existing partners, the Group can create a great momentum to 
increase sales of the coffee segment. In January 2020, the Group was the only agricultural business

scheme to distribute products to new or ineffective sales territories. Regarding the “clean” rice product

and consumers. Moreover, the sales force is divided by product group of cake, nutrition, agricultural 
products, dry cake and candy for the purpose of product knowledge specialization.
Given the ambition of reaching the revenue of 3,000 billion VND in 2020, the Group will diversify its 
products and distribution channels. In addition to the mainstream sales channel GT, the Group continues 
to expand its sales force for MT channels, export, key accounts, B2B channels and online channels. 
Since the fourth quarter of 2019, besides confectionery, the Group has promoted the distribution of other 
products such as cashew nut, rice and fish sauce. Agricultural products are the Group’s strength in the 
context that consumers are more conscious of quality and traceability of staple goods. In addition, the

Investing in a new modern industrial center of processing seed and agricultural products. 
Reason for 
implementation
- According to the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, in recent years, the rice sector in 
the Mekong Delta (MD) has strongly transformed and achieved remarkable results. However, there 
have still been challenges and limitations affecting the efficiency, sustainability and competitiveness 
of this important sector, especially the quality of seed and rice. In order to overcome these 
difficulties, in addition to the efforts of localities and farmers, the increased involvement and 
attention of enterprises especially enterprises which have rich potential and experience in this 
sector is called for.     
- The investment of Vinaseed in the project of industrial center for processing seed and agricultural 
products in Dong Thap province – a key province of producing rice for the whole country will 
contribute to complete the rice value chain which applied 4.0 technology from seed to production, 
harvest, processing and product consumption. It also will be a basis for forming large scale 
specialized production areas associated with processing and preserving seed and producing and 
trading in branded rice that is reserved for domestic consumption and export to the largest rice 
production areas of the whole country. Eventually, it contributes to exercise the Master program on 
sustainable agriculture development adapting to climate change in the Mekong Delta. 
Method and 
schedule of 
implementation
- In April 2019, Vinaseed officially started building the Industrial Center for processing seed and 
agricultural products at Truong Xuan industrial cluster, Thap Muoi District, Dong Thap province. 
This is a key project of Vinassed which was approved by the Dong Thap People’s Committee 
for the investment in the Decision No. 1068/QĐ-UBND-HC and was credited with the Investment 
Certificate No. 7407342160 by the Dong Thap Ministry of Planning and Investment. 
- On the 14 of December 2019, in Thap Muoi District (Dong Thap province), Vinaseed held the 
inauguration ceremony for the industrial center for processing seed and agricultural products 
and on the same day put it into operation.
The investment 
result
- After 8 months of construction, the industrial center for processing seed and agricultural 
products was established and put into operation with a capacity of one hundred thousand tons of 
rice and fifty thousand tons of seed per year. The center is expected to contribute to revenue of 
about VND 300 billion in 2020 and gradually increase to VND 700 billion in 2024 and is also a factor 
boosting PAN’s agricultural business in the near future.

Business Situations: In 2019, BBC reached VND 1,503 billion in revenue and VND 95 billion in earnings 
after tax, respectively equivalent to 94% and 86% of plans. Earnings per share for the whole year were 
VND 5,832 per share. On average for the whole period of 2015-2019, its revenue achieved an average 
growth of 6.4% per year and earnings after tax increased by 2.6% per year. 
In 2019, the Company’s earnings after tax of confectionery segment decreased due to high selling 
expenses including advertising expense, displaying expense, commission and sales bonus and 
a record of other income in 2018. In quarter four of 2019, the Company developed the new product 
lines: Lucrich and Roppy that are low calorie and low-fat aiming to provide a full-energy snack without 
gaining weight and meet consumers’s tastes. As a result, the company focused on building the market 
and introducing products to customers.   
Profit ratio: Thanks to good control in expenses and promoting R&D to develop and distribute new 
products with high profit margins, on average for the period of 2015-2019, gross profit margin and net 
profit margin of the company still continue on a trend of sustainable development. 
Asset situations and solvency: BBC’s total assets as of the 31st of December 2019 were VND 1,570 
billion, up 25% over the same period in 2018. For the whole period of 2015-2019, its total assets reached 
an average growth of 11% per year. In which cash and deposits were VND 403 billion (equal to 26% of 
total assets), thereby maintaining high solvency (short-term solvency was 1.55 times and inventories 
was VND 116 billion). The debt/total assets ratio was relatively low, at a rate of 35% higher than 27% 
in 2018. 
Some outstanding activities of the Company in 2019:
Production activities and cost management: the Company’s business efficiency in 2019 was effectively 
maintained thanks to its good forecast of buying price and raw material import policy.
Development of new products: thanks to promoting the R&D, in 2019, BBC continued to successfully 
send some new products to the market, especially new product lines Lurich and Roppy.

Business performance compared to year plans
Business situations: In 2019, Aquatex Bentre’s revenue was VND 361 billion reaching 90% 
of plan and earnings before tax was VND 48 billion reaching 96% of plan, a decrease of 27% 
over the same period. 
The main reason for this decline of Aquatex Bentre came from common difficulties of the 
Pangasius export industry in 2019. In particular, the export price and raw material price 
were the lowest they’d been in a long time so the Company had to make a provision for 
inventories of farming fish as raw materials. However, the decline of Aquatex Bentre was 
considered to be lower than the industry average.  
The Company built a chain of farming and processing pangasius with good technology 
that improved the survivability of fish breeding and improved the quality and efficiency of 
pangasius raw material, thereby minimizing risks of fluctuations of input materials. 
Profit ratio: In 2019, Aquatex Bentre’s gross profit margin and net profit margin remained 
at 15%, a sharp decrease compared to 2018 (one of the best years in history) but they 
were higher than the industry average because Aquatex Bentre was self-sufficient in 
raw material under a closed value chain from farm to finished product. Its EPS as at 31st 
December 2019 was VND 4,235 per share, decreased 26% over the same period. Aquatex 
Bentre retained its net profit margin at 13% mainly due to good management of admin and 
selling costs by the Board of Governors (retained at a reasonable rate against incurring 
revenue) in the context of difficult business. 
In addition, Aquatex Bentre had an abundant source of cash so loan demand was at a low 
level, leading to an interest expense that was insignificant, thereby profitability ratios of 
the Company were higher than most listed fishery enterprises.   
On average in the period of 2015-2019, the gross profit ratios and net profit ratios reached 
18% and 12% respectively because the Company focused on high-class customer segments 
with higher gross profit margins and managed costs in the chain of farming and processing 
pangasius.    
Asset structure and solvency: In the period of 2014-2019, Aquatex Bentre still retained its 
good solvency and healthy financial status, limited loan and interest expenses. This was 
a special advantage of Aquatex Bentre in its business process as well as in the process of 
expanding production or investing in a new business model.  
Some outstanding activities of the Company in 2019:
Farming activities: In 2019, the Company continued to build and complete facilities of its 
farms for the implementation of its farming policy in the direction of industry and technical 
innovations.  
Processing activities: Aquatex Bentre executed many innovations in clam and pangasius 
processing activities including: 
Clam: continuing to improve the clam immersion process, increase product competitiveness 
and maintain the quality of products. 
Pangasius: implementing improvements in the quality of microbiological, organoleptic and 
products. 
Sales activities: In 2019, the Company focused on boosting pangasius consumption 
markets through offering its products to some new markets and the project of development 
of value-added goods in the next period to utilize of market’s advantages. For clam 
products, Aquatex Bentre decreased the sales proportion of this product. Clams are mainly 
consumed in Japan, EU, USA, Australia and Canada.

Business situation:
Ending in 2019, although revenue slightly declined 2.5%, Fimex VN still achieved positive growth 
in profit with an increase of 30% in net profit. Gross profit margin slightly increased to 11%. 
In the context of the EU market slowing down, the average selling price tended to decrease, the 
management promptly shifted its focus on the US market (+44% YoY) and Japanese market (+42% 
YoY) while improving the capacity of intensive processed products (which India and Ecuador etc. do 
not have the same processing level) to meet the demand of these markets and improve profit margin 
of processing segment. 
2019 was a successful year of shrimp farming of Fimex VN with the harvest output increased 71% 
over the same period. The management promptly took advantage of favorable weather to breed at 
a high density and at the same time applying R&D results to help shrimp grow well, contract less 
diseases and gain high yield. Thanks to the lower cost of farming compared to the purchase price of 
external raw materials, profit margins of the shrimp sector increased and contributed to high profit 
growth.

2019 Business operation report 
1. OVERVIEW
2. INVESTMENT AND M&A IN 2019
In 2019, using raised capital, The PAN Group focused on building a solid 
foundational system in Agriculture and Food by purchasing shares 
that controlled companies in the industry with good foundations and 
great growth potential, as well as investing in new projects in member 
companies in key areas. At the end of 2019, in the context of and entire 
industry beset with difficulties, the Group has made many efforts to 
maintain a high level of revenue and profit growth.
In 2019, within the framework of the Group-based operating 
model in which the Parent Company plays the role of capital 
management company and coordinates the production, business 
and distribution coordination among member companies, PAN 
continued to implement its development strategy through M&A 
and increased the ownership ratio of member companies.
In the food sector, new project investment and M&A activities 
to increase ownership in food companies continued to be 
implemented. Specifically, PAN continued to increase its 
ownership in Fimex VN to 64.5%. In addition, in 2019, the Group 
also increased its ownership in 584 Nha Trang Fisheries JSC to 
73.4%, thereby making 584 Nha Trang a member company of 
the Group.
In the agricultural sector, in early 2019, the Group completed 
the process of increasing its ownership in VFC to 41.88% 
through a tender offer.
Additionally, in June 2019, PAN Consumer Goods Distribution 
JSC, abbreviated as PAN CG, was officially established with the 
goal of quickly attaining a monthly revenue of 150 billion VND 
through the first distribution of The PAN Group’s agricultural 
products and foodstuffs, followed by similar products from 
partners.

In the context of extremely difficult agricultural markets 
in 2019, the business results in 2019 clearly demonstrated 
the efforts of the whole group. These efforts became the 
most apparent when the revenue and profit scale achieved 
in the year was equivalent to the same period from the year 
before. Net revenue in 2019 reached VND 7,784 billion, 
down slightly by 0.57%. Revenue from export activities 
reached VND 4,302 billion, down 10.1% while domestic 
revenue increased sharply by 14.5% to VND 3,481 billion. 
The main reason for this is the general decline in export 
prices of seafood products and the Group’s focus on 
developing domestic sales.
As at 31 December 2019, total consolidated asset value was VND 10,764 billion, an increase of 14% 
compared to the same figure at the end of 2018. The growth rate of total assets in 2019 was lower than 
that of the period of 2013-2018 because the Company entered into a new development period in which it 
focused on enhancing and promoting its internal strengths from the ecosystem of its existing member 
companies and slowing down the pace of M&A implementation.  
The M&A strategy of consolidating subsidiaries continued to be carried out in the period of 2015 - 2019. 
Most of these subsidiaries had good financial potential and stable financial structures in the field of 
agriculture and food, of which their cash and cash equivalents, receivables, inventories and fixed assets 
made a significant proportion of the Company’s total asset structure.

agricultural products: In December 2019, after 8 
months of construction and installation, Vinaseed 
completed the project of building an industry center 
for processing seed and agricultural products in Dong 
Thap province. This is a modern, synchronous and 
automatic center of producing and processing seed 
and agricultural products using Japanese technology 
which was established with a capacity of 100,000 tons

drying system with a capacity of 450 tons per batch

new cold storage facility in Quarter 1 of 2020 which

2019 was a year in which the agriculture sector faced lots of difficulties such 
as: prolonged hot weather, drought and severe saltwater intrusion across the 
country and the key region of the Mekong Delta. The export market of agricultural 
products also faced many barriers when export prices remained perpetually low. 
Thus, the achievement of profit growth from the PAN’s core business is evidence 
of the effectiveness of the model of sustainable business development that The 
PAN group has been pursuing. 
For revenue: The Group’s consolidated net revenue in 2019 reached VND 7,813 
billion, a slight drop of 0.2%. In which, the agriculture sector contributed VND 
1,535 billion, equivalent to 20% and the food segment contributed VND 6,277 
billion equal to 80%. Export sales achieved VND 4,302 billion, down 10.1%, while 
domestic revenue sharply increased 14.5% as of VND 3,481 billion. The main 
reason was the decline in the export price of aquatic products and that the Group 
focused on developing domestic sales.
For profit: The Group’s consolidated earnings after tax in 2019 reached VND 
452 billion, a downturn of 20% as of same previous period. However, if the Group 
separated net profit from reasonable M&A transaction of FMC in 2018, the EAT 
from its core business in 2019 grew 15%. Its consolidated gross profit margin 
in 2019 improved by 21% compared with 18% of 2018. This result was achieved 
thanks to the improvement of FMC’s gross profit margin and especially the 
dramatic movement of LAF’s product structure from raw cashews to processed 
ones in 2019. 
In regards to carrying out business plans in 2019, the plan of increasing ownership 
of the Vietnam Fumigation Joint Stock Company (HOSE: VFG) over 50% has not 
been completed due to market conditions and VFG’s 
business performance has not been consolidated 
into the Group’s financial statements. As a result, its 
consolidated net revenue achieved 74.3% of the year’s 
plan. However, the Group has still proactively expanded 
value chains by successfully raising its ownership 
proportion of 73.45% at Nha Trang 584 Fishery Joint 
Stock Company, acquiring 80% stock shares of Golden 
Beans (Shin Coffee) and especially establishing the PAN 
Consumer Goods Distribution Joint Stock Company 
(PAN CG). 
In 2019, the Group strongly promoted the investment of 
big projects and focused more on organic growth based 
on its existing platform. Typically, that was the expansion 
by and additional 90 ha of shrimp farming in Soc Trang 
Province, the completion of the Seed Center in Don 
dương, Lam Dong Province, the inauguration of Western 
Bibica Factory with its capacity of 10,000 tons per year 
and the opening of the Industry Center for processing of

with its capacity of 30,000 tons of seed and 85,000 tons

2. SUBCOMMITTEES OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS
On July 15, 2013, the Board of Directors issued Resolution No. 16-07 / 2013 / NQ-HĐQT to establish 
four subcommittees to support the Board’s activities: The Investment Subcommittee, the Human 
Resources Subcommittee, the Social Responsibility Subcommittee, and the Independent Management 
Subcommittee. The Investment Subcommittee was obviated by establishment of the Investment Council 
at the 2014 Annual General Meeting of Shareholders, as stipulated in Clause 3, Article 29 of the Charter 
of the PAN Pacific Joint Stock Company, issued on October 28, 2014. Accordingly, Resolution No. 15-06 
/ 2014 / NQ-HĐQT dismissed the Investment Subcommittee and cancelled all pertinent documents. 
On April 6, 2015, the Board established the Subcommittee for the Environment and Sustainable 
Development to promote the Company’s sustainable development activities. This subcommittee 
reflects the Company’s commitment to professionalizing its supervision of its social and environmental 
impacts, good corporate citizenship, and regulating its future expansion according to sustainability 
protocols. Members who contribute to the committee possess a comprehensive understanding of the 
Company’s activities, are experienced in social, environmental, and safety issues, and have received 
international training in these areas at corporations such as Sumitomo, Yamaha, CJ Vina, Palffiger, and 
Levi Strauss. The Environment and Sustainable Development Subcommittee was established under 
Resolution No. 04-04 / 2015 / NQ-HĐQT on April 6, 2015.
The AGM subsequently approved cancellation of the Investment Council and its regulatory provisions. 
The rights and obligations of the Investment Council were transferred in accordance with the current 
Charter for the Board, under Resolution No. 01-04 / 2015 / NQ-DHDCD, Article 7, Clause B, issued on 
April 24, 2015. 
On November 18, 2018, the Board of Directors issued a resolution to restructure their subcommittees 
according to the corporate governance provisions of Decree 71/2017 / ND-CP and Internal Regulations 
adopted by the General Meeting of Shareholders on October 27, 2018.  The Board of Directors 
approved renaming the Environment and Sustainable Development Subcommittee as the Sustainable 
Development Subcommittee.
As of December 31, 2019, the Company has three subcommittees under the Board, including the 
Personnel Subcommittee, the Sustainable Development Subcommittee, and the Independent 
Subcommittee.

Supervision and Evaluation of the Board of Directors:
In 2019, The PAN Group’s Board of Directors competently and faithfully advised and guided company 
operations. The Board’s meetings complied with all relevant laws and regulations. The Resolutions 
of the Board of Directors did an excellent job of responding to market conditions, the state of The PAN 
Group ’s operations, and interests of the shareholders, as expressed in the resolutions of the Annual 
General Meeting. They excelled in their managerial role and set a sound example for the Executive 
team to follow.
Investment Activities of PAN Farm: Currently, PAN Farm owns Vietnam Seeds Group Joint Stock 
Company (Vinaseed) and maintains its level of indirect ownership at SSC, QSC, and HSC. In 2019, PAN 
Farm increased its ownership of Southern Seed Corporation (SSC) to 96.4%
Investment Activities of PAN Food: In 2019, PAN Food completed the tender offer to buy shares of 584 
Nha Trang Seafood JSC (584NT), making 584NT a subsidiary with the ownership stake of 73.45%. In 
addition, PAN Food owns PAN Food Manufacturing JSC (PFM), Long An Food Processing Export JSC 
(Lafooco), Bibica JSC (BBC), and Ben Tre Aquaproduct Import and Export JSC (ABT) and through ABT 
owns Sao Ta Food JSC as an associate.
ESOP Issuance to Key Personnel: The PAN Group distributed 3 million shares to key personnel in 
December 2019 at VND 10,000 per share. The company’s chartered capital at the end of 2019 was VND 
1.731 trillion.
Bonus Share Issuance: In 2019, the PAN Group completed the issuance of bonus shares to existing 
shareholders at a ratio of 4:1 during the Extraordinary General Meeting of Shareholders on October 27th 
2018. The bonus share issuance source was from the share premium of the 2017 financial statements.
Selection and Assessment of the Independent Auditor for The PAN Group’s 2019 Financial 
Statements:  
The BOS assessed many independent auditors before selecting the best option.
The PAN Group selected Ernst & Young Vietnam. They audited The PAN Group ‘s 2019 separate and 
consolidated financial statements pursuant to the Resolution of Board of Directors 03-06/2019-NQ-
HDQT on June 26th 2019.
Modification of Company Charter: In 2019, the PAN Group issued the Appendix on February 28th 
2019 and December 3rd 2019 with the content of amendment the Company’s charter capital after 
completing the issuance of bonus shares and ESOP for key personnel.
Information Disclosure: The company complied with regulations on its information disclosure, as 
defined by the Ministry of Finance’s Circular 155/2015/TT-BTC.

2. BASIS OF PREPARATION
2.1. Accounting Standards and System
The consolidated financial statements of the Group, expressed in Vietnam dong (“VND”), are prepared in accordance with 
Vietnamese Enterprise Accounting System and other Vietnamese Accounting Standards issued by the Ministry of Finance 
as per:
- Decision No. 149/2001/QD-BTC dated 31 December 2001 on the Issuance and Promulgation of Four Vietnamese Accounting 
Standards (Series 1);
- Decision No. 165/2002/QD-BTC dated 31 December 2002 on the Issuance and Promulgation of Six Vietnamese Accounting 
Standards (Series 2);
- Decision No. 234/2003/QD-BTC dated 30 December 2003 on the Issuance and Promulgation of Six Vietnamese Accounting 
Standards (Series 3);
- Decision No. 12/2005/QD-BTC dated 15 February 2005 on the Issuance and Promulgation of Six Vietnamese Accounting 
Standards (Series 4); and
- Decision No. 100/2005/QD-BTC dated 28 December 2005 on the Issuance and Promulgation of Four Vietnamese Accounting 
Standards (Series 5).
Accordingly, the accompanying consolidated financial statements, including their utilisation are not designed for those who 
are not informed about Vietnam’s accounting principles, procedures and practices and furthermore are not intended to 
present the consolidated financial position and consolidated results of operations and consolidated cash flows of the Group 
in accordance with accounting principles and practices generally accepted in countries other than Vietnam.
2.2. Applied accounting documentation system
The Group’s applied accounting documentation system is the General Journal system.
2.3. Fiscal year
The Group’s fiscal year applicable for the preparation of its consolidated financial statements starts on 1 January and ends 
on 31 December.
2.4. Accounting currency
The consolidated financial statements are prepared in VND which is also the Company’s accounting currency.
2.5. Basis of consolidation 
The consolidated financial statements comprise the financial statements of the parent company and its subsidiaries for the 
year ended 31 December 2019.
Subsidiaries are fully consolidated from the date of acquisition, being the date on which the Group obtains control, and 
continued to be consolidated until the date that such control ceases.
The financial statements of the subsidiaries are prepared for the same reporting year as the parent company, using 
consistent accounting policies.
All intra-company balances, income and expenses and unrealised gains or losses resulting from intra-company transactions 
are eliminated in full.
Non-controlling interests represent the portion of profit or loss and net assets not held by the Group and are presented 
separately in the consolidated income statement and within equity in the consolidated balance sheet.
Impact of change in the ownership interest of a subsidiary, without a loss of control, is recorded in undistributed earnings.
