3.13 Payable and accruals
Payable and accrual are recognised for amount to be paid in the future for goods and services received, whether 
or not billed to the Group.
3.14 Accrual for severance pay
The severance pay to employee is accrued at the end of each reporting year for all employees who have been in 
service for more than 12 months up to 31 December 2008 at the rate of one-half of the average monthly salary 
for each year of service up to 31 December 2008 in accordance with the Labor Code and related implementing 
guidance. The average monthly salary used in this calculation will be revised at the end of each reporting period 
following the average monthly salary of the 6-month period up to the reporting date.  Increases or decreases to 
the accrued amount other than actual payment to employee will be taken to the consolidated income statement.
This accrued severance pay is used to settle the termination allowance to be paid to employee upon termination 
of their labour contract following Article 48 of the Labor Code.
3.15 Foreign currency transactions
Transactions in currencies other than the Group’s reporting currency of VND are recorded at the actual transaction 
exchange rates at transaction dates which are determined as follows:
Ě Transaction resulting in receivables are recorded at the buying exchange rates of the commercial banks 
designated for collection; and
Ě Transactions resulting in liabilities are recorded at the selling exchange rates of the transaction of commercial 
banks designated for payment.
3. SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (Continued)
Transfers are made to investment properties when, and only when, there is a change in use, evidenced by 
ending of owner-occupation, commencement of an operating lease to another party or ending of construction 
or development. Transfers are made from investment properties when, and only when, there is change in use, 
evidenced by commencement of owner-occupation or commencement of development with a view to sale. The 
transfer from investment property to owner-occupied property or inventories does not change the cost or the 
carrying value of the property for subsequent accounting at the date of change in use.
3.9 Leased assets
The determination of whether an arrangement is, or contains a lease is based on the substance of the arrangement 
at inception date and requires an assessment of whether the fulilment of the arrangement is dependent on the 
use of speciic assets and the arrangement conveys a right to use the asset.
Leases are classiied as inance leases whenever the terms of the lease transfer substantially all the risks and 
rewards of ownership of the asset to the lessee. All other leases are classiied as operating leases.
Where the Group is the lessee
Rentals under operating leases are charged to the consolidated income statement on a straight-line basis over 
the lease term.
Where the Group is the lessor
Assets subject to operating leases are included as the Group’s investment property in the consolidated balance 
sheet. Initial direct costs incurred in negotiating an operating lease are recognised in the consolidated income 
statement as incurred. 
Lease income is recognised in the consolidated income statement on a straight-line basis over the lease term.
3.10 Prepaid expenses
Prepaid expenses are reported as short-term or long-term prepaid expenses on the consolidated balance sheet 
and amortised over the period for which the amount are paid or the period in which economic beneit are generated 
in relation to these expenses.
3.11  Business combinations and goodwill
Business combinations are accounted for using the purchase method. The cost of a business combination is 
measured as the fair value of assets given, equity instruments issued and liabilities incurred or assumed at 
the date of exchange plus any costs directly attributable to the business combination. Identiiable assets and 
liabilities and contingent liabilities assumed in a business combination are measured initially at fair values at the 
date of business combination.
Goodwill is initially measured at cost being the excess of the cost of the business combination over the Group’s 
share in the net fair value of the acquiree’s identiiable assets, liabilities and contingent liabilities. If the cost of 
acquisition is less than the fair value of the net assets of the subsidiary acquired, the difference is recognized 
directly in the consolidated income statement. After initial recognition, goodwill is measured at cost less 
accumulated amortization. Amortization of goodwill is calculated on a straight-line basis over ten (10) years during 
which the source embodying economic beneits are recovered by the Group. The parent company conducts the 
periodical review for impairment of goodwill of investment in subsidiaries. If there are indicators of impairment 
loss incurred is higher than the yearly allocated amount of goodwill on the straight-line basis, the higher amount 
will be recorded in the consolidated income statement.
3.12 Investments
Investments in associates 
The Group’s investment in its associates is accounted for using the equity method of accounting. An associate 
is an entity in which the Group has signiicant inluence that is neither subsidiaries nor joint ventures. The Group 
generally deems they have signiicant inluence if they have over 20% of the voting rights.

Interest
Revenue is recognised as the interest accrues (taking into account the effective yield on the asset) unless 
collectability is in doubt.
Dividends
Income is recognised when the Group’s entitlement as an investor to receive the dividend is established.
3.20 Taxation
Current income tax
Current income tax assets and liabilities for the current and prior years are measured at the amount expected to 
be recovered from or paid to the taxation authorities. The tax rates and tax laws used to compute the amount are 
those that are enacted as at the balance sheet date.
Current income tax is charged or credited to the consolidated income statement, except when it relates to items 
recognised directly to equity, in which case the current income tax is also dealt with in equity.
Current income tax assets and liabilities are offset when there is a legally enforceable right for the Group to offset 
current tax assets against current tax liabilities and when the Group intends to settle its current tax assets and 
liabilities on a net basis.
Deferred tax
Deferred tax is provided using the liability method on temporary differences at the balance sheet date between the 
tax base of assets and liabilities and their carrying amount for inancial reporting purposes. 
Deferred tax liabilities are recognised for all taxable temporary differences, except: 
Ě Where the deferred tax liability arises from the initial recognition of an asset or liability in a transaction which at 
the time of the related transaction affects neither the accounting proit nor taxable proit or loss; and
Ě In respect of taxable temporarily differences associated with investments in subsidiaries and associates where 
timing of the reversal of the temporary difference can be controlled and it is probable that the temporary difference 
will not reverse in the foreseeable future.
Deferred tax assets are recognised for all deductible temporary differences, carried forward unused tax credit 
and unused tax losses, to the extent that it is probable that taxable proit will be available against which deductible 
temporary differences, carried forward unused tax credit and unused tax losses can be utilised, except:
Ě Where the deferred tax asset in respect of deductible temporary difference which arises from the initial 
recognition of an asset or liability which at the time of the related transaction, affects neither the accounting proit 
nor taxable proit or loss; and
Ě In respect of deductible temporarily differences associated with investments in subsidiaries and associates, 
deferred tax assets are recognised only to the extent that it is probable that the temporary differences will reverse 
in the foreseeable future and taxable proit will be available against which the temporary differences can be utilised.
The carrying amount of deferred tax assets is reviewed at each balance sheet date and reduced to the extent that 
it is no longer probable that suficient taxable proit will be available to allow all or part of the deferred income 
tax asset to be utilised. Previously unrecognised deferred tax assets are re-assessed at each balance sheet date 
and are recognised to the extent that it has become probable that future taxable proit will allow the deferred tax 
assets to be recovered.
Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured at the tax rates that are expected to apply in the year when the 
asset realised or the liability is settled based on tax rates and tax laws that have been enacted or substantively 
enacted at the balance sheet date. 
Deferred tax is charged or credited to the consolidated income statement, except when it relates to items 
recognised directly to equity, in which case the deferred tax is also dealt with in the equity account.
3. SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES (Continued) 
At the end of the year, monetary balances denominated in foreign currencies are translated at the actual 
transaction exchange rates at the balance sheet dates which are determined as follows: 
Ě Monetary assets are translated at buying exchange rate of the commercial bank where the Group conducts 
transactions regularly; and
Ě Monetary liabilities are translated at selling exchange rate of the commercial bank where the Group conducts 
transactions regularly.
All exchange differences incurred during the year and arising from the revaluation of monetary accounts 
denominated in foreign currency at year-end are taken to the consolidated income statement.
3.16 Appropriation of net proit
Net proit after tax (excluding negative goodwill arising from a bargain purchase) is available for appropriation 
to investors after approval by appropriate level of authority, and after making appropriation to reserve funds in 
accordance with the Group’s Charter and Vietnamese regulatory requirements.
The Group maintains the following reserve funds which are appropriated from the Group’s net proit as proposed 
by the Board of Directors and subject to approval by shareholders at the Annual General Meeting.
Investment and development fund
This fund is set aside for use in the Group’s expansion of its operation or of in-depth investments.
Bonus and welfare fund
This fund is set aside for the purpose of pecuniary rewarding and encouraging, common beneits and improvement 
of the employees’ beneits, and presented as a liability on the consolidated balance sheet.
3.17 Treasury shares
Cown equity instruments which are reacquired (treasury shares) are recognised at cost and deducted from equity. 
No gain or loss is recognised in proit or loss upon purchase, sale, issue or cancellation of the Group’s own equity 
instruments.
3.18 Earnings per share
Basic earnings per share amounts are calculated by dividing net proit after tax for the year attributable to ordinary 
shareholders of the Group (after adjusting for the bonus and welfare fund) by the weighted average number of 
ordinary shares outstanding during the year.
Diluted earnings per share amounts are calculated by dividing the net proit after tax attributable to ordinary 
equity holders of the Group by the weighted average number of ordinary shares outstanding during the year plus 
the weighted average number of ordinary shares that would be issued on conversion of all the dilutive potential 
ordinary shares into ordinary shares.
3.19 Revenue recognition 
Revenue is recognised to the extent that it is probable that the economic beneits will low to the Group and 
the revenue can be reliably measured. Revenue is measured at the fair value of the consideration received or 
receivable, excluding trade discount, rebate and sales return. The following speciic recognition criteria must also 
be met before revenue is recognised:
Sale of goods
Revenue is recognised when the signiicant risks and rewards of ownership of the goods have passed to the buyer, 
usually upon the delivery of the goods.
Rendering of other services
Revenue is recognised when the services have been rendered and completed.

3.21 Financial instruments 
Financial instruments – initial recognition and presentation
Financial assets 
Financial assets within the scope of Circular No. 210/TT-BTC issued by the Ministry of Finance on 6 November 
2009 providing guidance for the adoption in Vietnam of the International Financial Reporting Standards on 
presentation and disclosures of inancial instruments (“Circular 210”) are classiied, for disclosures in the notes 
to the consolidated inancial statements, as inancial assets at fair value through proit or loss, held-to-maturity 
investments, loans and receivables or available-for-sale inancial assets as appropriate. The Group determines 
the classiication of its inancial assets at initial recognition.
All inancial assets are recognised initially at cost plus directly attributable transaction costs.
The Group’s inancial assets include cash and cash equivalents, trade receivables, other receivables and 
investments.
Financial liabilities
Financial liabilities within the scope of Circular 210 are classiied, for disclosures in the notes to the consolidated 
inancial statements, as inancial liabilities at fair value through proit or loss or inancial liabilities measured 
at amortised cost as appropriate. The Group determines the classiication of its inancial liabilities at initial 
recognition.
All inancial liabilities are recognised initially at cost, net of directly attributable transaction costs.
The Group’s inancial liabilities include trade and other payables, accrued expenses and loans.
Financial instruments – subsequent re-measurement
There is currently no guidance in Circular 210 in relation to subsequent re-measurement of inancial instruments. 
Accordingly, the inancial instruments are subsequently re-measured at cost.
Offsetting of inancial instruments
Financial assets and inancial liabilities are offset and the net amount reported in the consolidated balance sheet 
if, and only if, there is a currently enforceable legal right to offset the recognised amounts and there is an intention 
to settle on a net basis, or to realise the assets and settle the liabilities simultaneously. 
3.22 Segment information

services (business segment) or providing products or services in a particular economic environment (geographical

The Group has the obligation to pay corporate income tax (“CIT”) at the rate of 20% (2015: 22%) of taxable proits. In 
addition, the Company’s subsidiaries are entitled to the following CIT exemption and reductions:
  At PAN Food: ABT is entitled to an exemption from CIT for three (3) years and 50% reduction from CIT for the 
following nine (9) years commencing from the first year of taxable profit making which was 2004.
  At NSC: On 1 March 2011, NSC was approved as a scientific and technological enterprise through the Certificate 
No. 03/DK-DNKHCN issued by the Department of Science and Technology of Hanoi. According to the current 
regulations on scientific and technological enterprise and CIT incentives, NSC shall be entitled to CIT exemption 
and reduction as a newly established enterprise from investment in the sector of high-tech, scientific research 
and technological development if revenues generated from scientific and technological products and goods for the 
first, second and third year exceed total revenue by 30%, 50% and 70%, respectively. In particular:
(i) The tax rate of 10% shall be applied for ifteen (15)yearsfrom the irst year generated revenue from scientiic and 
technological activities; and
(ii) NSC shall be exempted from CIT for a period of four (4) years and entitled to a 50% reduction of CIT payable for 
the subsequent nine (9) years.
The tax returns iled by Group are subject to examination by the tax authorities. As the application of tax laws and 
regulations is susceptible to varying interpretations, the amounts reported in the consolidated inancial statements 
could change at a later date upon inal determination by the tax authorities.

33. FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT OBJECTIVES AND POLICIES 
The Group’s principal inancial liabilities comprise loans, trade and other payables. The main purpose of these 
inancial liabilities is to inance the Group’s operations. The Group has loan, trade and other receivables, and 
cash and short-term deposits that arise directly from its operations. The Group also hold available-for-sale 
investments. The Group does not hold or issue derivative inancial instruments.
The Group is exposed to market risk, credit risk and liquidity risk.
Management reviews and agrees policies for managing each of these risks which are summarised below.
Market risk
Market risk is the risk that the fair value of future cash lows of a inancial instrument will luctuate because of 
changes in market prices. Market prices comprise four types of risk: interest rate risk, currency risk, commodity 
price risk and other price risk, such as equity price risk. Financial instruments affected by market risk include 
loans, deposits and available-for-sale investments.
The sensitivity analyses in the following sections relate to the position as at 31 December 2016 and 31 December 2015.
The sensitivity analyses have been prepared on the basis that the amount of net debt, the ratio of ixed to loating 
interest rates of the debt and the proportion of inancial instruments in foreign currencies are all constant.
In calculating the sensitivity analyses, management assumed that: 
•  the statement of the intconsolidated balance sheet relates to available-for-sale debt instrument; and
•  the sensitivity of the relevant consolidated income statement item is the effect of the assumed changes in 
respective market risks. This is based on the financial assets and financial liabilities held at 31 December2016 
and 31 December 2015.
Interest rate risk
Interest rate risk is the risk that the fair value or future cash lows of a inancial instrument will luctuate because 
of changes in market interest rates. The Group’s exposure to market risk for changes in interest rate relates 
primarily to the Group’s cash and short-term deposits and borrowings. These investments are mainly short term 
in nature and they are not held for speculative purposes.
The Group manages interest rate risk by looking at the competitive structure of the market to obtain rates which 
are favorable for its purposes within its risk management limits.
Interest rate sensitivity
A sensitivity analysis is not performed for interest rate risk as the Group’s exposure to the interest-rate risk is 
minimal at the reporting date as the loans from banks are short-term with ixed interest rates.
Foreign currency risk 
Foreign currency risk is the risk that the fair value or future cash lows of a inancial instrument will luctuate 
because of changes in foreign exchange rates. The Group’s exposure to the risk of changes in foreign exchange 
rates relates primarily to the Group’s operating activities (when revenue or expense is denominated in a different 
currency from the Group’s accounting currency).
The Group is exposed to foreign currency risk in relation to purchases and sales of goods which are denominated 
in currencies other than its accounting currency as disclosed in Note 2.4. The Group manages its foreign currency 
exposure by considering the prevailing and expected market situation when it plans for future purchases and 
sales of goods denominated in foreign currencies, other than increasing natural-hedged proportion. The Group 
does not employ any derivative inancial instruments to hedge its foreign currency exposure.

Equity price risk 
The Group’s listed and unlisted equity securities are susceptible to market price risk arising from uncertainty 
about future values of the investment securities. The Group manages equity price risk by placing a limit on equity 
investments. The Board of Directors reviews and approves all equity investment decisions.
As at 31December 2016, the fair value of the Group’s investments in quoted securities was VND 1,178,634,403 
(31 December 2015: VND 2,440,925,249). A decrease of 10% on the price of these securities could have an impact of 
approximately VND 117,863,440 (31 December 2015: VND 244,092,525) on the Group’s proit before tax, depending 
on whether or not the decline is signiicant or prolonged. An increase of 10% in the value of the securities would 
increase the Group’s proit before tax by VND 117,863,440(31 December 2015: VND 244,092,525).
Credit risk
Credit risk is the risk that counterparty will not meet its obligations under a inancial instrument or customer 
contract, leading to a inancial loss. The Group is exposed to credit risk from its operating activities (primarily for 
trade receivables) and from its inancing activities, including deposits with banks, foreign exchange transactions 
and other inancial instruments.
Bank deposits
The Group’s bank balances are mainly maintained with well-known banks in Vietnam. The Group’s maximum 
exposure to credit risk for the components of the balance sheet at each reporting dates are the carrying amounts 
as illustrated in Notes 5. The Group evaluates the concentration of credit risk in respect to bank deposit as low.
Trade receivables
Customer credit risk is managed by the Group based on its established policy, procedures and control relating to 
customer credit risk management. 
Outstanding customer receivables are regularly monitored. The requirement for impairment is analyzed at 
each reporting date on an individual basis for major clients. The Group seeks to maintain strict control over its 
outstanding receivables and has a credit control department to minimize credit risk. In view of the aforementioned 
and the fact that the Group’s trade receivables relate to a large number of diversiied customers, there is no 
signiicant concentration of credit risk.
Except for the inancial assets for which provision have been made as disclosed in Notes 7and 8, management 
evaluate all inancial assets are neither past due nor impaired as they related to recognized and creditworthy 
counterparties.
Liquidity risk
The liquidity risk is the risk that the Group will encounter dificulty in meeting inancial obligation due to shortage 
of funds. The Group’s exposure to liquidity risk arises primarily from mismatches of maturities of inancial assets 
and liabilities.
The Group monitors its liquidity risk by maintain a level of cash and cash equivalents and bank loans deemed 
adequate by management to inance the Group’s operations and to mitigate the effects of luctuations in cash lows.

OUR STORY 
Sustainable development will be a consistent strategy of The PAN Group as soon as it is restructured 
into the Agriculture - Food field from its initial industrial hygiene activities. 
 
In the negative context of the overall market and unexpected business performance, the PAN Group 
has made many efforts to improve business performance, in which core values “Sustainable 
Development” and Transparent principles are upheld. These core values are significant factors in 
ensuring stable business operations, minimizing risks in the current turbulent period and paving the 
way for development in the coming future. 
 
Also, investors, customers and partners expect The PAN Group to act with these values in mind. 
Sustainable Development Strategic Orientation 
 
 
Continue to strengthen and develop the product value chain from seeds, cultivation to 
production and distribution, in which safety, quality and traceability criteria are highlighted. 
Development of agriculture - food products must be in the direction of high value added 
content aiming to provide more benefits to parties, especially disadvantaged parties such 
as farmers, unskilled labours, ethnic minorities etc. 
 
Gradual application of modern technology that is safe and friendly to the environment and 
people shall be a solution to strengthen and firmly develop existing production platforms.  
 
Establish and improve management systems continuously in regards to social and 
environmental issues according to the Group’s Standards and in line with International 
Practices. Apply these values consistently and periodically observe and ensure compliance 
of all member Companies. 
 
Consider responsible investment, sustainable development as core values and Information 
Transparency as a prerequisite for the Group’s operations. 
 
Become a positive force in promoting sustainable development trends in Vietnam through 
specific actions that shall contribute to global development goals.  
 
We appreciate the COOPERATION of various parties and the DISSEMINATION of positive effects on 
the community aiming to create strong and deep impacts. 
With key performance as a holding and M&A company model, The PAN Group strives to enhance 
positive impacts on carrying out responsible business and production activities to member 
companies, supply chains and enterprises in Vietnam. 
 
Sustainable development is an element that is integrated into every activity. It is the core value and 
spread over all highlighted events of The PAN Group in 2019.

2. Standard of behavior 
 
 CORE VALUE 
Being an Agriculture and Food Group in Vietnam, The PAN Group has chosen sustainable 
development as its core value and solution for rapid and sustainable growth in its long-term vision. 
We are responsible to the community and environment and share values with related parties while 
pursuing our Sustainable Development Strategy   
 
 PRACTICE PRINCIPLES 
The PAN practice principles (‘the principles’) are instituted by The PAN Group Joint Stock Company 
(‘the Group’), and set out the requirements of the Group in the fields of agricultural and food 
production. The principles aim to ensure the activities of stakeholders align with sustainable 
development strategies and the commitment of the Group to “provide high standard products of 
trusted origin in the integrated full value chain” and “create sustainable values for farmers, families 
and society”. 
 
The principles are applied to all member companies of the Group and their compliance must be 
evaluated periodically. The second version of the principles was released in March 2019.  
 
 CODE OF CONDUCT 
Code of conduct is a document that regulates all activities and provides guidelines for internal and 
external conduct of the PAN Group (including organization and employees). This Code of conduct is 
aimed to affirm transparent principles on development policy and commit to integrity in all 
transactions, business and production activities.  
Practice Principles and Code of Conduct are two essential documents that set out all internal and 
external viewpoints, requirements and measures of The PAN Group in regards to a sustainable 
development strategy.

conducted assessment and screenings of targeted companies on environment and society issues in 
the M&A process aiming to ensure compliance with outlined criteria.

In comparison with conventional rice cultivation methods, application of SRI helps to reduce the 
volume of rice seeds by 70% - 90% rice seeds and fertilizer volume by 20%-25%, increase 
productivity by 9-15%, it also limits disease development especially especially sheath blight, 
yellow snails, root choking disease, root bundles, and thrips while increasing rice’s resistance

weather, increases rice plants’ resistance on emerging pests and reduces 30% irrigation

FLOWER COPYRIGHT STORY 
According to Mr Lai The Hung, Manager of Lam Dong Department of Cultivation and Plant 
Protection, the area of growing Dalat Flowers is around 9,000 ha accounting for 30% over the 
country and 3 billion branches are collected per year. However, only 10% are cultivated by 
qualified seed sources which are made by professionally invested enterprises. They privately or 
personaly use that seed to cultivate or redistribute to farmers. 90% of the remains are un-
copyrighted and unidentified seeds. As a result, only 10% equivalent to 300 million Dalat flowers 
are considered suitable for export per year while the rest are consumed domestically with much 
lower value. The price of chrysanthemums purchased at nurseries for domestic consumption 
are valued at around 2,500 – 3,000 VND per branch, while the price of export products cultivated 
from copyrighted seeds is around 5,000 – 7,000 VND. 
A true story related to a nursery exporting flowers to Japan suddenly received a notice of 
destruction of all flowers and was severely punished for accidentally using counterfeit seeds 
without copyright to produce export flowers. A further consequence of this situation is seed 
degeneration. As Mr Le Van Hai’s story, owner of Hai Hien flower production at Thai Phien flower 
village and hundreds of other nurseries have suffered from striped stems disease in their 
chrysanthemums since the beginning of 2019. Over 900 ha out of 1,600 ha chrysanthemum 
cultivation in Dalat is infected with this disease which caused damages of up to billions VND.

Tan Nam farm - strategic strengths of Sao Ta to increase production quality and efficiency 
Tan Nam farm is located in Vinh Tan commune, Vinh Chau town near the sea. The shrimp farm test 
activities on 5 ha based on experience learned from Malaysia, China and Thailand makes Tan Nam shrimp 
farm extend up to 280 ha, maintains high efficiency and the company’s self-control of shrimp raw material 
sources and ensures optimum productivity and quality of rearing. Together with their intensive processing 
capacity, Sao Ta is expected to gain stable and rapid growth in the next period regardless of the common 
difficulties of the industry. Facing diseases and an unfavorable environment, Tan Nam farm has promoted 
its high technical capabilities in shrimp farming and gained impressive farming results with a 71% 
increase in harvesting yield over the same period. In 2019, Enterocytozoon Hepatopenaei (EHP) and white 
feces diseases were broke out in all three major shrimp farming areas in the world (Asean, Central 
America and India). EPH disease is now almost incurable, causing damage to many shrimp farming ponds 
and as a result farmers are subjected to   new and mounting difficulties. This is the reason why many 
Mekong Delta shrimp farmers are concerned about the risks to the next harvest of shrimp.  Tan Nam 
shrimp farm has applied measures to prevent the spread of diseases by spreading bird nets over all 
settling ponds, water canals, sewage ponds and discharging canals. This costs nearly 400 million VND but 
it is highly effective. A few shrimp ponds infected with white spot virus shall be treated by destructive 
chlorine and lime disinfection around the pond. This measure may damage some ponds but it can prevent 
pathogens from spreading to many other ponds. On the other hand, biosecurity measures are strictly 
applied in the farming pond system. Shrimp farming workers are only allowed travel within the area of 
their pond, especially minimizing the movement out and in during the period 30-45 days of shrimp.

Shin coffee story
Shin coffee is a subsidiary of Golden Beans which was acquired by The PAN Group in 2019 corresponding 
to 80% ownership of charter capital. Shin Coffee supplies specialty coffee with many differences compared 
to current Vietnamese coffee products. It is considered as exceptional qualities in creating higher added 
value. Specialty coffee is scored over 80 points in a point scale of 100 with specific points by Specialty 
Coffee American Association (SCAA). This coffee is cultivated in different areas with special geographical 
and climatic conditions. The specialty coffee gains its quality from its nature   and components of farming 
soil that creates various interesting flavours such as fruit and chocolate flavours etc. Shin discovered these 
raw material areas from 2015 and there has recently been a close cooperation with indigenous farmers 
for a purchasing commitment at a higher price than market price (VND 4,000 – 10,000/kg), technical 
training and other kinds of physical assistance.

Difficulties 
In addition to attained achievements, there are some points that we have not done well and not met 
the expectations of interested parties. Shortcomings and disadvantages are always our 
indispensable parts. Most importantly, we have seriously considered, evaluated and taken that as 
an experience lesson and as a basis for continuous improvement. 
 Economic:  
In 2019, due to unfavorable market conditions, we didn’t complete the plan to increase the 
ownership rate in Vietnam Fumigation JSC to over 50%. VFC revenue, therefore, has not been 
consolidated into The PAN Group, caused consolidated net revenue and profit before tax were 
only 74.3% and 80.1% of the year plan, respectively. 
In addition, there were other unfavorable market factors, such as the high inventory amount of 
seafood in importing countries caused lower demand and lower export prices; Cashew nut prices 
continued to fall; Increasing in temperatures, droughts and saline intrusion continued to affect 
agricultural production ... Facing those difficulties, The PAN Group focused on restructuring export 
markets, researching methods to improve farming efficiency, intensively processing to increase 
product value, improving the supply and distribution chain to increase efficiency. Therefore, the 
company have maintained its core strength, the net operating profit after tax in 2019 of core 
business activities grew by 15%. 
 Environment 
Some environmental improvement projects have not reached their expected progress: PAN-
HULIC's composting production project has been delayed for more than a year (from the end of 
2017) until now it can be restarted due to changes in product structure in PAN-HULIC; 
Recirculating Aquaculture System of Aquatex has not been applied on a large scale, only stop at 
hatchery with the adoption rate of about 20%. With the associated farmer system, although there 
is always the support and guidance of technical staff, changing habits for safe farming, wearing 
labor protection when mixing - spraying, or not discarding plant protection packaging in the field 
is still going on. This requests the training activities for farmers should be conducted more 
effectively. 
 Society 
The turnover of the Group has not improved much in the past years. Employees quit work mainly 
as unskilled workers and sales staffs. The reason that these subjects have many opportunities in 
the market and the labor competition of other companies. Part of the reason for short-term 
remuneration and income is not attractive enough. In operation, there are still activities that need

MESSAGE 
FROM THE CEO
Dear valued shareholders, customers, and partners:
Economic growth and profitability are our business goals but 
bringing satisfaction and happiness to the community is our 
ultimate goal.
In addition to doing business effectively and achieving high 
growth, we continually strive to increase the quality and 
quantity of our products so that we can bring more and better 
meals to the families we serve, as well as greater prosperity 
to The PAN Group and its member companies. 
I would like to express my sincere thanks to the investors 
and customers who have always cooperated with us, 
advocated for us, and supported our development. Since the 
beginning, sustainable development has been one of our 
guiding principles. We understand that businesses must 
align themselves and their interests with the interests of their 
country and community.  
2018 witnessed many important milestones for The PAN 
Group. Two successful fundraising campaigns have affirmed 
PAN’s ability to mobilize capital – a combined VND 2,000 
billion – from some of the world’s most desirable investors. 
TAEL Two Partners Ltd., the Sojitz Corporation, PYN Elite 
Fund, GIC, IFC, Hulic, and others are now shareholders of our 
corporation and its member companies. These investors are 
well-known for having some of the highest requirements for 
transparency and sustainable development, and we are proud 
to have satisfied them. 
Our consolidated net revenue reached a record VND 7,828 
billion in 2018, up 92% compared to 2017. Total consolidated 
assets reached VND 9,438 billion, up 158% from the beginning 
of the year. That we have been able to achieve such results 
while fulfilling our corporate social responsibility (CSR) 
obligations is good motivation for us to continue benefiting the 
community and doing our part to help the world attain the 17 
UN sustainable development goals.
We continue to take both direct and indirect measures to 
benefit the environment. Direct measures include things like 
water recapture and recirculation efforts at Aquatex Bentre, 
FIMEX VN, and Bibica; the reuse of waste for compost, feed 
production, and fuel at Vinaseed and elsewhere; and the use 
of advanced, water- and pesticide-sparing, greenhouses and 
irrigation systems at PAN-SALADBOWL. Many of our members 
are implicated in sustainability indirectly; for example, 
Vinaseed’s development of drought and pest resistant seeds 
will provide the world with crops that require less fertilizer, 
less water, and fewer chemical treatments.
We ensure that our activities conform to the ADB’s Safeguard 
Policy Statement, IFC Performance Standards, and other 
international criteria. Our member companies continue 
to maintain their certifications following HACCP, BRC, 
FSSC22000, GLOBALG.A.P., ASC, BSCI, ISO14000, SEDEX, 
et al. We also encourage our affiliates to use GRI reporting 
standards.
We engage in charity and community building throughout 
Vietnam to support the livelihoods and living conditions of 
local residents, especially the vulnerable.
Sustainable development means more to us than pro forma 
adherence to international standards; we believe that it helps 
its practitioners maintain high and stable economic growth. 
In 2018, sustainable corporate culture, human resource 
management, corporate social responsibility, and other such 
topics were discussed at the PAN Gala, the CEO Summit, and 
other internal fora. Through these dialogue mechanisms, the 
belief that environmental protection and corporate social 
responsibility is associated with economic growth has begun 
its spread through our member companies.
As we move into 2019, we will continue to develop and adhere 
to ever more stringent internal norms, comply with every 
relevant legal and voluntary external standard, and build 
systems as needed to solve socio-environmental problems. 
We expect to spread the spirit of sustainable development 
from the corporation’s upper echelons to each employee, and 
thereby, to society at large.
We live in interesting and occasionally troubling times; living 
effectively requires a continual struggle towards responsibility 
and right action. With opportunities like the CPTPP trade 
deal, and threats like the US-China trade war, the tsunami in 
Indonesia, and other natural disasters, the construction of a 
sustainable development strategy is increasingly urgent, and 
its execution, increasingly necessary. The desire to meet the 
challenges posed by our times motivates the 8,000 employees 
of The PAN Group to work and dedicate themselves to our 
cause. I hope this same desire motivates you to accompany us 
and help us spread the philosophy of sustainable development 
so that we can build a more developed, more prosperous, and 
more joyful society. 
CEO
Nguyen Thi Tra My
Best regards!

Vision
A pioneering agriculture and food Group offering trusted products

values on behalf of farmers, families and society.
Guiding Principles
We appreciate that the presence of 
a world-class agriculture and food 
product company increases the food 
security of Vietnam and the region. 
We appreciate that agriculture – 
including aquaculture – lies at the core 
of our country’s economy, traditions 
and rhythms of daily life. 
We strive constantly to raise the bar in 
the quality and value of our offerings.
We believe that improving the quality 
of farming inputs improves farmers’ 
livelihoods.
We promote business practices that 
are tied to the heart of Vietnam’s 
sustainability.
We offer a fair, professional and 
inspiring working environment, and 
opportunities that benefit our people 
and their families.

growth, maximizing value for all key 
stakeholders.

1.1. Crop seed
Vinaseed’s products are characterized 
by vigorous growth, high yields, pest 
resistance, and adaptability to changing 
climactic conditions. They are designed 
to 
maximize 
profit, 
environmental 
stewardship, and consumer health. 
Rice seeds
  
Conventional 
varieties: 
Popular 
varieties, currently dominating the 
domestic market, include Thien Uu 8, 
RVT, Dai thom 8, VS1, Du Huong, and 
Tran Trau Huong.
Hybrid varieties: These varieties are 
quality-certified and include TH3-4, 
Thuy Huong, Bac Uu 64, Bac Uu 903, 
Nhi Uu 63, Nhị Uu 86B, and PAC 807.
Corn seeds
In 2018, Vinaseed focused on developing 
fresh glutinous and sweet corn varieties 
for the domestic market. These varieties 
currently enjoy market dominance due 
to their high productivity and adaptability, 
and the attractive and flavorful end 
product.  Popular corn varieties include 
purple glutinous corn (HN66), hybrid 
glutinous corn (HN88), HN68, single 
hybrid glutinous corn (MX10), and MX6.

cay-trong.htm  
Vegetable seeds
Although Vinaseed’s vegetable seed 
varieties are still limited, existing 
products have been well-received by 
the market. The company has recently 
helped diversify the produce available in 
Vietnam by contributing several melon 
varieties. 
Popular 
vegetable 
seeds 
include heat-tolerant cucumber Sakura, 
Red Pumpkin (Pum1664, Pum1628m, 
and Pum1631); hybrid gourd (F1), Bog 
16 Watermelon (WAM 14123 and WAM 
14127), and hybrid bitter melon (F1: Big 
6131).

Fresh cut flowers

Matissie, Colonge, Dante, Pinky rock, 
Copa, Muse, etc.) and 20 varieties 
of carnation (Borja, Babylon, Apolo, 
Americano, etc.) to Japan. The flowers 
have beautiful colors and can be kept 
fresh for up to 20 days.
Cucumis Melon
Taking 
advantage 
of 
technology 
transfers from Japan, our melons are 
cultivated under strictly controlled 
conditions. PAN-SALADBOWL offers 
GLOBALG.A.P. Standard products  for

Japanese rice products

are grown from a strictly controlled seed

developed for the Japanese market.

the maintenance of nutritional value 
and natural aroma.

most viable agricultural areas for

equipment 
to yield a product that meets the

markets. 
Special rice (red rice, black rice):

function, and stabilize blood sugar 
levels.

Business management and production in agriculture are conducted through

Vinaseed is a leader in the Vietnamese seed industry and enjoys a healthy 
financial situation with steady, sustainable growth. In 2016, Vinaseed 
established Ha Nam High-Tech Agriculture Development and Investment JSC 
to pursue its development strategy for the period from 2016-2020.  The goal of 
this company is to trade and absorb technology transfers for premium melon 
and vegetable farming in domestic and foreign markets. At the same time, it 
is forming large-scale, intensive, and high-tech farming partnerships. In 2018, 
Ha Nam Hi-Tech’s operations stabilized, and they have begun to master the 
relevant technologies. The company has built-up a distribution network of 350 
supermarkets and food chains in urban areas such as Hanoi, Thanh Hoa, Vinh, 
and Hai Phong. Vinaseed continued investing in large-scale projects, including 
a processing warehouse in Thanh Hoa and a rice and rice seed factory in Dong 
Thap. With strong R&D and production capabilities, Vinaseed maintained 
continuous business growth, and was a significant contributor to the overall 
business results of The PAN Group in 2018 (accounting for 20% of revenues 
and 44% of profit before tax).  
PAN-SALADBOWL focused on flower production and export to Korea and 
Japan. The area available for flower production is expected to increase to 200 
ha in next 5 years, including contract farming. With cooperation from Japanese 
partners, the Company also started experimenting. Current products have 
been officially supplied to the Japanese supermarket chains AEON Mall and 
AEON Citimart. It is expected that, in 2019, PAN-HULIC will provide high-end 
strawberry products, using results from the selection and cultivation research 
trials of mid-2018.

2019, The PAN Group increased its stake in VFC to 41.88% by acquiring shares

long-term partnerships with global brands, like Syngenta, Kumiai, Fimex VN, 
Nihon Nohyaku, Nufarm, King Elong, and Sinon. VFC currently has about about 
8% of the Vietnamese pesticide market, the second largest in the industry. In 
fumigation services, VFC has 60% market share, and is the provider of choice 
for Vietnam’s agricultural exporters. In 2018, VFC continued to achieve net 
revenue growth, with VND 2.289 trillion, up 5% from 2017. VFC’s operating 
profit in 2018 was VND 168 billion, up 24% from 2017.

The need to conserve water is becoming increasingly urgent as

take steps above and beyond their legal obligations to reduce 
the amount of water used.

aquacultural activities of member companies such as Aquatex

Effective use of water
Research is an area of core competence for Vinaseed and 
its subsidiary, SSC. Therefore, in a move to consolidate 
the research activities of The PAN Group, Vinaseed has 
established the Vietnam Seed Corporation R&D Center, 
pursuant to Resolution No. 12/TTr-VINASEED-BOD. The use 
of extreme weather resistant crops, whose production will be 
enabled by this R&D center, is one of the ways that The PAN 
group is attempting to reduce its use of water resources.
In addition, member companies such as PAN-HULIC and 
Vinaseed are applying high-tech cultivation techniques to 
the production of greenhouse grown vegetables, flowers, 
melons, and strawberries. 
The PAN Group continues to apply the System of Rice 
Intensification (SRI) in its rice production operations. 
Compared with conventional rice cultivation, SRI reduces 
seed use by 70-90%, fertilizer use by 20-25%, and limits 
the development of diseases and the proliferation of pests, 
especially sheath blight, yellow snails, root choking disease, 
root bundles, and thrips. The cost of inputs decreases by VND 
342-520/kg resulting in a net profit gain of VND 2 million/
ha. Since rice grown using this method doesn’t require the 
flooding of fields, it reduces water use and greenhouse gas 
emissions. Rice crops produced using this method are also 
more physically robust and therefore more able to resist 
storms. Altogether, SRI results in productivity increases of 
between 9% and 15%.
Vinaseed has been recognized as a “Science and Technology 
Enterprise” since 2011, with engineered products accounting 
for 80% of revenue.

THE STORY OF TRADITIONAL FISH 
SAUCE:
Traditional fish sauce has been used 
for generations in Vietnam for its 
distinctive flavor. Traditional fish sauce 
is produced by coating fish – usually oily 
fish like anchovy or mackerel – in salt 
and allowing the fish to decompose and 
ferment for 12-24 months. The result is 
a sauce with a distinctive taste that is 
pure, safe, and healthy. 
584 fish sauce is traditional fish sauce 
produced 
from 
anchovies 
caught 
off the coast of Nha Trang. 584 Nha 
Trang Seafood JSC, formerly a state-
owned enterprise under the Ministry 
of Fisheries, was established in 1977. 
The company’s products – distributed 
in supermarkets such as Maximark, 
Vinmart, BigC, Citimart, and Coopmart 
– have earned an outstanding reputation 
in the Vietnamese market and have been 
exported to Japan, Korea, Australia, 
Cambodia, and Laos. In the coming 
months and years, exporting fish sauce 
to the wider Asian market is a top priority 
for the company.

Achievements
The PAN Group and affiliates achieved the major sustainable development goals that we set for 2017. To proactively manage 
socio-environmental problems, and to integrate such management into our production and business activities in accordance 
with international standards, took a remarkable effort on the behalf of The PAN Group and our member companies. However, 
such action was essential to meet the requirements of investors, customers, workers, surrounding communities, and other 
stakeholders. The following table highlights our major 2018 goals. 
FIELD
 2018 TARGET AND RESULT 
Food safety
Goal: Maintain international food safety certifications for 100% of food production and 
manufacturing facilities. 
Status: Met.
In 2018, food production facilities continued to maintain their pre-existing food safety 
certifications from organizations like BVC, SGS, and Quacert. Pan Food JSC food was 
also certified under FSSC22000 standards. Towards this goal, PAN was advised by 
international experts from the IFC, one of our strategic shareholders, in a special 
cooperation program.
Goal: Apply the PAN Practice Principles to ensure food safety.
Status: Met. 
The PAN Group’s intensive Practice Principles training program was completed by 
all member companies at SSC headquarters in Ho Chi Minh City on May 14th and 
15th. This program included training on GRI’s Sustainability Reporting Standards 
conducted by Mr. Nguyen Cong Minh Bao, the Director of GRI in Vietnam.
Traceability
Goal: Mandate traceability training at all companies and keep complete records 
of these trainings. Perform traceability compliance monitoring at all member 
companies.
Status: Met. 
Traceability has been a strict requirement in the manufacturing operations of member 
companies. The monitoring of original principle of action traceability is also ensured 
through the Group’s annual social environment assessment program. 
FIELD
 2018 TARGET AND RESULT 
Product
Goal: Collect feedback on 100% of member companies product lines.
Status: Met. 
All member companies have customer care departments, communication channels, 
and receive feedback from customers about products and services. All customer 
feedback is now recorded for analysis, remediation, and response. This will help us 
receive information to improve quality and ensure safety of food products.
Environment
Goal: Commit no violations of environmental law. 
Status: Met.
In 2018, member companies welcomed inspection teams from many fields and 
disciplines, including teams looking for violations of environmental law. No violations 
were found.
Safety
Goal: Develop and consistently apply a process for occupational safety and risk 
assessment in all member companies.
Status: Nearly met. 
In 2018, member companies agreed to institute risk assessment processes for all 
corporate activities. This is necessary if we are to mitigate social and environmental 
problems that have the potential for significant impact. However, due to the large 
amount of work required to institute these processes, only 6/9 companies have 
complied.
Assessment of environmental risk and occupational safety is a requirement of the 
IFC’s Performance Standard and the ADB’s Safeguard Policy Statement. The PAN 
Group is committed to compliance with these two standards.
Internal staff and 
community
Goal: Ensure that all member companies implement a mechanism to receive 
complaints and redress grievances, and ensure that stakeholders are informed of their 
rights under this mechanism. 
Status: Nearly met.
In 2018, member companies agreed to institute mechanisms to receive and handle 
feedback from stakeholders, especially complaints on environmental and social issues. 
However, due to the large amount of work required to institute these mechanisms, only 
6/9 companies have complied.
The implementation of the above mechanism is a requirement of the IFC’s Performance 
Standard and the ADB’s Safeguard Policy Statement. The PAN Group is committed to 
compliance with these two standards.
Management system
Goal: Update the Practice Principles based on feedback from member companies.
Status: Nearly met.
The Principles are being revised and supplemented. This revision will be complete in 
the first half of 2019.
All member companies apply the PAN Practice Principles and are periodically evaluated 
for compliance.

Dear Esteemed Shareholders and Business 
Partners!
Vietnam’s economy recorded a successful 
year with many impressive figures in 2017: 
GDP increased by 6.81%, the highest ratio 
in the last 6 years; inflation remained low, 
increased by only 3.53%. The year 2017 also 
marked a new record for the national trade 
value at excessing of US$400 billion. Total 
export of the agriculture in 2017 was over 
US$36.37 billion, up 13% over the same peri-
od, a big win of the sector.
5
Success on the economic area continues to motivate de-
velopment in others. At the micro level, domestic enter-
prises – including The PAN Group – have also obtained 
several achievements on the development journey, ex-
ceeded the sales and profit targets, realized the growth, 
and especially demonstrated a vigorous transformation 
to identify and seize opportunities for development in the 
context of an increasingly global integration.
Since the inception of our journey leveraging Vietnam's 
food and agriculture, the BOD has clearly defined the de-
velopment strategy in line with to sustainability, environ-
mental protection, safety and social responsibility. Over 
the years, this orientation has always been consistently 
understood and determinedly executed by The PAN Group 
and its member companies. Now, we have been reaping 
the initial outcomes from these determinations and en-
deavors. Not only achieving economic success and ex-
panding the scale of operations, The PAN Group has built 
up its reputation in the agricultural and food sector, ob-
taining the consensus and support of the community and 
society. The specific actions are the strongest demon-
stration of commitment to sustainable development, and 
gradually create sustainable values for The PAN Group.
Investing in infrastructure as well as technology to pro-
mote efficiency and environmentally friendly production, 
the factories in Lafooco and PAN Food have been contin-
uously upgraded to minimize energy consumption, elimi-
nate and minimize waste and waste water discharged to 
the environment. 
Applying advanced technologies in agricultural production 
such as (i) deploying recirculating aquaculture system 
(RAS) to reduce the disposal of waste from aquaculture 
into the environment, in Aquatex Bentre; (ii) researching 
to create resistible plant varieties aiming to reduce the 
use of chemicals and fertilizers in NSC and SSC; (iii) ap-
plication of greenhouse and high-density cultivation to im-
prove productivity, save water and reduce chemical use of 
at PAN-SALADBOWL. 
Applying environmentally friendly technologies and using 
materials such as replacing coal by gas to reduce pollu-
tion at Bibica, utilizing agricultural waste as a fuel for pro-
duction or as a compost for soil fertilization thus reducing 
waste disposal in The Group's agricultural companies.
Complying with international practices as well as require-
ments of investors on sustainable development strategies, 
environmental protection, safety and corporate social re-
sponsibility. We proactively develop and apply codes of 
conduct within the Group and have a monitoring mecha-
nism to ensure the compliance. The PAN Group will be the 
pioneer in applying sustainable development criteria to its 
production and business activities, in line with the interna-
tional practices to realize our vision of becoming a leading 
group in the field of agricultural and food in the region. We 
are excited and proud to announce our success not only in 
terms of economic aspect but also in sustainable develop-
ment strategy. This success affirms our right orientation 
and brings benefits not only to The PAN Group, but also 
stakeholders. We would like to express our gratitude to 
all shareholders, partners, customers and employees for 
their support and contribution during the past years. The 
PAN Group will strive to show appreciation through spe-
cific actions, aiming at sustainability and immortality. The 
Group has also affirmed its commitment to transparency 
and openness in its operations as the principles of all ac-
tions to win your long-term trust and companionship.
Entering 2018, in the hustle of the industrial revolution 
4.0, the artificial intelligence development and the global 
integration knocking on the door of every nation and its 
enterprises, The PAN Group optimistically foresees po-
tential opportunities in the future. We will be determined 
to do our best and confidently turn these opportunities 
into actual advantages, and above all, the sustainable de-
velopment strategy is always the lodestar for every plan 
and activity. We understand that this is the key to obtain-
ing greater success in the next journey. The PAN Group 
expects to achieve such miraculous achievement like U23 
Vietnam team in the U23 AFC 2018 final. This is the result 
of an arduous practice, of striving and sacrificing. It also 
motivates us to be more determined and act more force-
fully.

Orientation
- Limit the emissions: Strive to reduce the emissions into the environment by a number of possible measures, such 
as the adoption of new technologies, the investment into the equipment and infrastructure, the replacement of input

Regularly remind the employees of putting the garbage into the designated area, utilize – recycle usable materials to

 Member companies support the clean production and waste reduction program
One of the most significant environment protection activities in production is waste processing and management. In the 
food producing companies, waste management also aims at generating a production environment that ensures food 
safety. Therefore, waste management is a work which is executed in a relatively critical and pro-active manner in all 
the companies.
In waste management, waste water is often the most influential. In order to manage the effluents from production, all 
factories of The PAN Group apply pretreatment measures before being discharged into the environment. Of which, the 
construction of the waste water system is a top priority and is applied to all processing factories. For factory equipped 
with few machines, few workers and production activities without water, simpler treatment systems are used to treat 
such as garbage screens, gas pit system, sedimentation tank. The objective is to ensure that the effluent quality is 
complied with the regulations of the Industrial Park Management Board and the Vietnamese standards for wastewater 
in each specific area and other standards that PAN acknowledged. All factories signed waste disposal contracts with 
the industrial park or have discharge permits. The PAN Group collects and reviews periodically all reports of member 
companies’ waste water quality monitoring to ensure the compliance.

THE PAN GROUP OVERVIEW
Food safety issues have also caused concerns for both 
the public and government and monitoring mechanisms 
have become stricter in response to the increasing 
number and severity of food safety violations.  
Against this backdrop The PAN Group has committed 
to and is implementing a sustainable development 
strategy that has helped the Group to overcome 
difficulties and maintain sustainable growth. The Group 
achieved a consolidated net revenue of VND2,753 
billion, consolidated profit after tax of VND 336 billion, 
with net profit to its shareholders of VND257 billion, a 
20% increase compared to 2015. The Group has become 
one of the largest agriculture and food companies in 
Vietnam with total assets of VND3,762 billion. 
In addition to economic achievements, we also proud of 
the steps taken by The Group in 2016 in order to protect 
the environment and to respect social and community 
responsibilities:
• Protecting the environment by training and raising 
awareness of environmental issues as well as improving 
technology-based solutions and investing in facilities 
to prevent environmental pollution and avoiding the 
depletion of natural resources. Prominent examples 
would be the investment in environmental protection 
for agricultural production at PAN-SALADBOWL, 
improvements in the environmental protection system 
at Lafooco to minimize the emissions and efforts 
to maintain the environmental protection system at 
Bibica.
• Considering the material and spiritual needs of 
employees and building close relationships to maintain 
dedication and good will in the Group. This included 
efforts to maintain and raise benefits at Bibica, National 
Seed Company, Southern Seed Company and Lafooco. 
Despite being a newly established company facing 
many initial challenges, PAN-SALADBOWL has also 
implemented several activities to build relationships 
with workers and to take care of their material and 
spiritual needs. These policies provide more stable 
income, security and risk prevention measures for 
employees. 
• Ensuring safety and security for workers and the 
community throughout investments in upgraded 
facilities, labor protection, safety equipment, labor 
training, monitoring compliance with Laws and 
company’s regulations. In particular, this included 
security investment at PAN-SALADBOWL to meet the 
stringent requirements of the Japanese partners and 
the Global GAP standards; also the implementation 
of safety and maintenance measures at Ben Tre Aqua 
Product Import and Export Joint Stock Company 
meeting the international ASC, MSC, and Global GAP 
standards.
• Implementing community and social programs to 
support people in Central Vietnam after disaster 
losses, help people in difficulties and with critical 
illness at the National Institute of Hematology and 
Blood Transfusion, raise awareness of food safety 
for primary school pupils in Hanoi suburban. These 
programs represent the sincere wishes of The PAN 
Group, which motivate us to create a humanist and 
mutually beneficial society.
• Development and establishment of the internal 
management system, promoting the “PAN Production 
Principles” to establish food safety, environmental 
protection, social safety and security requirements 
and applying them consistently in the Group with 
the consensus of subsidiaries. These principles are 
intended to be guidelines for all the business and 
production activities of the Group.  
In the year 2017, agriculture and food are still hot topics 
that are gaining more attention from the government 
and the public. It is expected that there will be 
increasing numbers of foreign investors, organizations 
and enterprises involved in the field of agriculture and 
food which will need to share and pursue sustainable 
development strategies. Therefore, we are ready to 
welcome and cooperate with them to develop and 
provide fresh, quality and traceable products from 
Vietnam for distribution all over the world. This is how 
we will build the brand name and reputation of The 
PAN Group and it is how we will expand our business 
working with our dedicated and professional partners. 
As the Chairman of The PAN Group Joint Stock Company, 
I would like to express my sincere appreciation to 
those who have always trusted, cooperated and 
supported the sustainable development strategy of The 
Group. I believe that The Group will be successful in 
2017 leading to a better future for farmers and for the 
agriculture and food sectors of Vietnam. Let’s create 
sustainable values together for the people of Vietnam 
and for people all over the world.   
Thank you and best regards!

and have try our best to contribute to the 
sustainable development of our community. Also, 
we want to create safe working environments 
for our workers and to provide safe, quality and

For The PAN Group sustainable development, 
environment protection and social stability are 
not only core values, they are the motivation to 
realize our vision of becoming a leading group in 
the field of agriculture and food in Vietnam and in 
the Asian region.

THE CHAIRMAN’S 
MESSAGE
FOR THE PAN GROUP, 2020 WAS THE YEAR OF CHALLENGES, 
BUT REMAINED MANY IMPRINTS AND POTENTIALS OF 
SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT FOR THE FUTURE.
Dear valued shareholders, customers and partners, 
We went through the historic year of 2020 in the context 
of the world darkened by the Covid-19 pandemic that 
its outbreak resulted in unprecedented decrease of 
growth rates in almost countries over decades. Although 
economies have been seen recovery remarkably since 
the third quarter of 2020, a journey to the normal still 
becomes fragile in the situation that new affected cases 
are increasing with many variants of SARS-CoV-2. The 
global GDP decreased by 4.4% in 2020 after over 10 years 
of consecutive growth since the 2008 financial crisis. 
Almost international organizations share a common view 
that the global economy is unlikely to recover in the short 
term, but it will take more years ahead.
In such difficulties of the pandemic, Vietnam has emerged 
as a phenomenon that it is one of a few countries doing 
a good job in control of the disease widespread while 
keeping the economy a positive growth. Agricultural and 
foodstuff industries have made remarkable contribution 
to the country’s achievements. 2020 was the year of 
big challenge, however, the agricultural sector reached 
the growth rate of 2.65% in GDP, export turnover of 
agricultural-forestry-fishery products still gained 41.25 
billion USD, reaching the highest level ever recorded. 
For The PAN Group, 2020 was the year of challenges, but 
remained many imprints and potentials of sustainable 
development for the future. Right from the time when 
Covid-19 first appeared, the Board of Directors and 
the Board of Management instructed and coordinated 
closely with member companies to response rapidly in 
the complicated changes of the pandemic. As a result, 
production facilities of the Group throughout the country 
kept on business operation without stagnation, ensuring 
jobs for the employees. The sustainable development 
strategy with such proactive response has helped our 
Group turn “danger” into “chance”, coming up with 
business results gained over as planned.  
Chairman of the 
Board of Directors
NGUYEN DUY HUNG
Over the years, The PAN Group has concentrated on building 
up a sustainable development platform based on the value 
chain “Farm- Food- Family”. To date, PAN has owned the 
leading completed agro-food ecosystem in Vietnam which 
is helpful for the tightened control of production cycle from 
seeding, cultivating and processing, and from farm to dining 
tables of families through well-known brand names such as 
Vinaseed, Sao Ta, Aquatex Ben Tre, Bibica, 584 Nha Trang, 
Lafooco, etc., We believe that people shall, in life development, 
have more increasing demands for foods of safety and high 
quality. This trend has been forecasted stronger arising 
after the pandemic. Moreover, in parallel with the country’s 
economic development, the agricultural sector in Vietnam 
shall be in need of moving to a more modern model to 
facilitate provision of products for customers in the global 
with professionalism in researches for scientific application, 
subtlety and pride of the Vietnamese agricultural products, 
instead of low-value raw materials. This is the mission that 
The Pan Group has been working hard and continues to 
pursue.  
Though the pandemic is still happening complicatedly, thanks 
to the emergence of many vaccines and determination of the 
Governments, future of the post Covid-19 world is on the go. 
In the context of changes in consumption demands and supply 
chains, proactive response and creativity of high grading 
businesses are more important than ever. With a contingent 
of whole-hearted, knowledgeable and experienced leaders, 
we believe that The PAN Group shall fulfil its goals already set 
forth, contributing to achievement of sustainable values for 
shareholders. On behalf of the Boards of Directors, I would 
like to extend a big thank to our valued shareholders and 
partners who have accompanied, supported and cooperated 
with the Group over the past periods. 
Wishing you all good health, happiness and success! 
Respectfully,

KEY PRODUCTS AND SERVICES
1. KEY AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS
1.1. CROP SEED
The Group’s products are characterized by vigorous growth, 
high yields, pest resistance, and adaptability to changing 
climactic conditions. They are designed to maximize profit, 
environmental stewardship, and consumer health.
Rice seeds 
Conventional 
varieties: 
popular 
varieties, 
currently 
dominating the domestic market, include Thien Uu 8, RVT, 
Dai thom 8, VS1, Du Huong, and Tran Trau Huong.
Hybrid varieties:  these varieties are quality-certified and 
include TH3-4, Thuy Huong, Bac Uu 64, Bac Uu 903, Nhi Uu 
63, Nhị Uu 86B, and PAC 807.
Corn seeds
Fresh glutinous and sweet corn varieties of PAN currently 
enjoy market dominance due to the high productivity and 
adaptability of the seed and the attractive and flavorful end 
product. Popular corn varieties include purple glutinous corn 
(HN66), hybrid glutinous corn (HN88), HN68, single hybrid 
glutinous corn (MX10), and MX6.
Vegetable seeds
Although Vinaseed’s vegetable seed varieties are still limited, 
they have been well-received by the market. The company has 
recently helped diversify the produce available in Vietnam by 
contributing a number of melon varieties. Popular vegetable 
seeds include heat-tolerant cucumber Sakura, Red Pumpkin 
(Pum1664, Pum1628m, and Pum1631); hybrid gourd (F1), 
Bog 16 Watermelon (WAM 14123 annd WAM 14127), and 
hybrid bitter melon (F1: Big 6131).
Flower seed and young plants 
The Research and Production Center for Seed and Young 
Plants in Don Duong, Lam Dong is a cooperation with Jardin 
(Japan) through copyright transfer contracts to produce 
flower seeds for Vietnam and Asia markets. Specifically, the 
1 ha greenhouse area with Japanese technology is the place 
to test over 100 flower varieties and perform the initial phase 
of the cooperation plan.
1.2. AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS
Fresh cut flowers:
PAN-Saladbowl produces and exports over 40 varieties of 
chrysanthemums (Kindly, Silvia, Celebrate, Olive, Lenior, 
Matissie, Colonge, Dante, Pinky rock, Copa, Muse, etc.) and 
20 varieties of carnation (Borja, Babylon, Apolo, Americano, 
etc.) to Japan. The flowers have beautiful colors and can be 
kept fresh for up to 20 days.

Strawberry
After research and experimental cultivation since mid-
2018, the first strawberries were officially harvested in the 
fourth quarter of 2019 in Lam Dong. In order to get these 
strawberries, the product development and research process 
is conducted rigorously and thoroughly from selecting seeds, 
planting trials to verifying product quality. The project is 
supported by the Japan International Cooperation Agency 
(JICA).
Cucumis Melon: 
Taking advantage of technology transfers from Japan, our 
melons are cultivated under a strictly controlled conditions. 
PAN-Saladbowl offers Global GAP Standard products  for 
domestic consumption and export to international markets 
including Japan, Singapore, and Dubai. 
Packaged rice 
Ban Mai Rice: Ban Mai rice is produced from purebred rice, 
which is a clean fresh rice product produced in a closed 
manner from the selection of good varieties, under strict 
management. Immediately after harvesting, the rice is 
transferred to the modern drying and processing system of 
VinaRice (in Dong Thap), ensuring 100% freshness. Ban Mai 
rice meets the VietGap standards, on a completely closed, 
modern Japanese processing line.
VJ Pearl, VJ Japonica: these varieties are grown from a 
strictly controlled seed stock and are cultivated, harvested, 
and processed using technologies developed for the 
Japanese market. These processing techniques ensure the 
maintenance of nutritional value and natural aroma.  
RVT rice: Vinaseed has identifed the most viable agricultural 
areas for mass production of RVT rice. In these areas, 
seed selection, soil preparation, and irrigation are strictly 
controlled. Postharvest processing is done using German 
and Japanese equipment to yield a product that meets the 
most stringent market requirements.
Special rice (red rice, black rice): these products are rich in 
bioactive substances, fiber, protein, vitamins, minerals, and 
micronutrients. These products protect the body’s ability to 
regulate blood pressure, control cardiovascular functions, 
and stabilize blood sugar levels.
ST24 & ST25 rice
Vinaseed’s ST24, ST25 rice varieties uses purebred rice 
varieties which were provided by engineer Ho Quang Cua. 
These varieties are planted in the “rice-shrimp” cultivation 
areas. To be specific, Vinaseed’s ST24 and ST25 rice 
is produced in a closed “field to table” model utilizing 
“purebred rice varieties’’ produced using special symbiotic 
breeding and production methods that integrate with rice 
and shrimp farming at sites in Soc Trang, Bac Lieu and 
Ca Mau. Aside from this, the rice is processed, milled and 
packed using modern technology from Japan and Israel, and 
is produced under FSSC 22000 certification standards. This 
organic farming method gives the rice grain a bolder and 
more fragrant flavor. The ST24 and the ST25 have long, clear 
and silver-free grain. When cooked, they are still soft and 
fragrant despite cooling. They contain double the amount of 
protein compared regular rice (10% protein).
1.3. AGROCHEMICALS
Since 1996 Vietnam Fumigation Company (VFC) has provided 
farmers with high-quality agrochemical products. These are 
processed and distributed from companies in the US, Japan, 
Switzerland, and Israel. 
1.4. FUMIGATION AND PEST CONTROL
Our associates, VFC, is the first fumigation company in 
Vietnam, with 45 years of history, a comprehensive investment 
from human to equipment. For many years, VFC has met 
most of the domestic and foreign customers’ fumigation 
requirements, as well as specialized import fumigation 
requirements related to customs and plant quarantine. This 
has contributed to improve the preservation, processing, 
production import and export effectively and smoothly. The 
company is also the provider of long-term insect control 
services and the most prestigious in Vietnam.

occasions.
Moon cakes: with a prestigious brand, long experience in 
the market, and a diverse range of nutritious products with 
a many flavors and packaging options to choose from, Bibica 
sits firmly atop the flavorful heap that is the mooncake 
market. 
Cracker: Bibica’s crackers manufactured on modern lines,

gives users a reasonable diet, supporting the creation of a

Wafer: Wafer branded Roppy is produced on modern lines 
with equipment and technology from Europe and US, with 
carefully selected ingredients.

Roasted nuts: Lafooco has been developing nut products

2.1.3 Functional Foods: including products for diabetics,

2.1.4. Specialty coffee
Arabica and Robusta coffee beans are grown in the most ideal 
ecological sub-regions, cared for by the hands of indigenous 
peoples, creating unique flavors for each region of Vietnam. 
Proud to be the one who opened the path of “Specialty 
coffee of Vietnam region”, PAN is making efforts to invest in 
building material areas and branding of specialty coffee by 
creating and honoring coffee flavors from each region across 
Vietnam.
2.2. DAILY MEALS 
2.2.1 Frozen seafood:
Seafood is produced at Aquatex Bentre and FIMEX VN, 
primarily for export to Europe, America, Canada, South 
Korea, and Japan. Our companies are the first to export 
Vietnamese shrimp, pangasius, and clams to the Japanese 
market. Our customers are leading supermarket chains, 
restaurants, food companies whose requirements for quality 
are strict.  
Pangasisus: available year-round from the Mekong Delta, 
GLOBAL GAP and ASC certified. Many specialty products 
are processed using modern techniques that ensure safety 
and maximize flavor, such as Frozen Pangasius Headless 
Gutted Fin Off, Tail Off, Frozen Pangasius Hypopthalmus 
Headless Gutted Steak, Frozen Pangasius Hypopthalmus 
Fillet Untrimmed, Frozen Pangasius Fillet Well trimmed 
Portion Breaded, Frozen Pangasius Fillet Cube Skewer with 
Vegetable.
Clams: collected from pristine sourcing areas in Vietnam. The supply chain is 
strictly monitored and MSC certified sustainable. Frozen packaged clam products 
include whole shell clam, clam meat, and seasoned steamed clam.
Shrimp: Sao Ta offers an assortment of processed shrimp products including: 
PD Shrimp (Peeled & Deveined), PDTO shrimp (Peeled & Deveined Tail-On), IQF 
shrimp (Individually Quick Frozen), Japanese style processed shrimp such as 
Nobashi, Shushi as well as breaded products. Their tempura shrimp are fried with 
a technique that that ensures products retain an attractive shape and texture and 
don’t harden after cooling.
2.2.2 Frozen Vegetable:
Kakiage products include fried and powdered vegetables that are processed with 
the traditional formula. 
2.2.3. Fish sauce products
584 Nha Trang is a traditional fish sauce that has been loved throughout Vietnam 
for the past 40 years. 584 carefully selects input materials and applies its own 
trade secrets to carefully ensure color and flavor. Major product lines of 584 Nha 
Trang fish sauce:
•	 Traditional products branded 584 Nha Trang with an assortment of protein levels.
•	 Fish sauce products supplemented with iron.
•	 Vi Ngon and Bien Bac aromatic, low-sodium products.
•	 Huong Bien fish sauce extracted from anchovies from the Nha Trang Sea.

Overview 
In the context of the world economy’s big difficulties, Vietnam’s economy faced 
with many challenges due to its high openness. The domestic economy 
was affected seriously after three outbreaks of the pandemic. 
However, Vietnam showed strong resilience, reaching bravely its 
economic growth and fulfiling the dual goals set forth by the 
Government. GDP growth rate for the whole year increased 
by 2.91% and there was no quarter of negative growth.
Although GDP growth in 2020 was at the lowest level 
over the past 10 years, in the situation of the COVID-19 
pandemic’s negative impacts, it was a success for 
our country among ones with the highest growth 
rate in the world. Together with China and Myanmar, 
Vietnam was one of three countries in Asia having 
positive growth this year. At the same time, our 
economy size reached more than 343 billion USD, 
surpassing Singapore (337.5 billion USD) and Malaysia 
(336.3 billion USD), making Vietnam the fourth 
largest economy in Southeast Asia (after Indonesia 
1,088.8 billion USD, Thailand 509.2 billion USD and the 
Philippines 367.4 billion USD) (According to the General 
Statistics Office).
