Trade balance
A spotlight in the economic picture in 2020 shows that it remained positive growth 
for exports to struggle difficulties in the epidemic situation. Export surplus of 
goods reached a dramatically high record (19.1 billion USD) and the trade balance 
maintained trade surplus for 5 consecutive years.
The signing of Free Trade Agreements has brought in positive signals for the 
Vietnamese economy, especially the Free Trade Agreement between Vietnam and 
the EU (EVFTA). In 2020, exports to the EU reached 34.8 billion USD. Notably, after 
5 month implementation (from the 1st August 2020) of the latter, Vietnam’s total 
export turnover to the EU reached 15.4 billion USD, increased by 1.6% over the same 
period last year. This reflects the high growth of domestic production capacity, 
favorable investment, production and business environment, and achievements 
gained in the process of Vietnam’s international economic integration. This is an 
encouraging result in the context of economic downturn in the EU region and the 
complicated development of the Covid-19 pandemic.
According to the General Statistics Office, it was 2.55% increase in the agriculture 
sector and 3.08% the fishery (the respective growth rates of industries in 2019 were 
0.61% and 6.30%). In particular, agricultural product export increased dramatically 
in the difficult context caused by the Covid-19 pandemic, rice export turnover for 
the first time gained more than 3 billion USD, increasing by 9.3% compared to 2019.
Meanwhile, seafood export in the whole 2020 reached about 8.4 billion USD, slightly 
decreasing by 1.9% compared to 2019, but it was still the result of more than 
expectation in the context of the complicated COVID-19 pandemic in major export 
markets such as the U.S., EU and Japan. With regard to the structure of seafood 
export, shrimp export reached 3.7 billion USD by the end of 2020, increasing by 
11% compared to 2019. According to VASEP, pangasius export in 2020 reached 
1.49 billion USD, decreasing by 25.5% compared to 2019.
For the food and confectionery industry, opening the door of integration requires 
Vietnamese confectionery businesses to grab continuous innovation to find a 
foothold in the country. However, the emergence of the COVID-19 pandemic has 
hardened the difficulties for domestic enterprises as they have to struggle for the 
fight against the pandemic while maintaining market shares. According to Nielsen 
data, during the peak of the pandemic in March and April 2020, the entire FMCG 
industry decreased by 12%. The biggest decline came from the traditional channel, 
including the buying and consuming ones later decreased by 9%.

3. OUTLOOK IN 2021
The World in 2021
Although the global economy in 2020 showed a downturn, 
research results on vaccines against the pandemic in many 
economies such as the U.S., Russia and UK, etc., in the last 
months of the year along with success of the Brexit trade 
agreement between UK and EU, the adoption of the COVID-19 
bailout package by the U.S. government, etc., have brought in 
a hope to the world economy. If the vaccines are successfully 
deployed, trade relations between major countries are 
stable, people’s lives are guaranteed and the pandemic is 
controlled, the global economy shall not face with a “lock-
down” measure that has been taken place in many countries, 
and economic activities shall be recovered evenly on a large 
scale with controlled financial risks.
The economic growth in 2021 has been forecasted by 
economic institutions and specialists to be seen with two 
scenarios depending on the situation of vaccination and 
pandemic control as follows: 
(i)	 Economic growth shall be strongly boosted when 
vaccination is carried out on a large scale. Loosened 
monetary policy shall have a good effect whereas business 
confidence and consumption are enhancing, etc., In this 
scenario, global GDP in 2021 may increase by 4.5% - 5.5% 
led and contributed by the developing and newly emerged 
economies; 
(ii)	The growth shall continue to decline if the production and 
widespread deployment of vaccines are too challenging, 
prolonging the happening of social distancing measures 
to prevent spreading of the pandemic, and there shall 
remain instable highly, as such the global economy shall 
face with more risks like the global GDP might continue to 
grow only about 2% in 2021 and it is likely to see a gradual 
recovery in 2022.
Vietnam in 2021
Vietnam’s economic growth increased by 2.91% in 2020 and 
it is one of the four economies in the world having the highest 
GDP growth. Based on this positive growth, the National 
Assembly sets a target of 6% GDP growth in 2021, GDP per 
capita scale of about 3,700 USD/person and average CPI of 
4%.
According to the Resolution No.01/ND-CP and the Resolution 
No.02/NQ-CP, the Government determined to strive for GDP 
growth of 6.5%, higher than 6% assigned by the National 
Assembly. The government also clearly identified three 
major growth drivers in 2021: consumption, export and 
investment. Meanwhile, export is under high expectation 
thanks to new FTAs besides EVFTA and other bilateral and 
multilateral trade cooperation, such as UKVFTA signed in 
November 2020.
Following to the 2021 general assessment, organizations and 
experts all believed that Vietnam would be benefited from a 
technology-led recovery, persistent FDI inflows and many 
signed trade agreements. Vietnam also has political stability 
and an improved business investment environment. In the 
latest forecast, HSBC considered that Vietnam’s growth rate 
could be 7.6% this year. The International Monetary Fund 
(IMF) did a forecast that Vietnam’s economy would recover 
strongly in 2021 with GDP reaching 6.5% when the domestic 
and external economic activities continue to the normal 
situation. Meanwhile, the World Bank considered Vietnam’s 
prospect to be positive and growth rate of 6.8%.

STRENGTH
Clear vision and development strategy. With aspiration to become a leading 
regional agricultural and food production corporation in connection to the 
global market, The Pan Group, based on an integrated full value chain and 
sustainable production solutions, is providing safe and nutritious foods in 
response to international standards for domestic and export markets.  
Having the best agricultural companies with many years of experience 
and sustainably competitive advantage, The PAN Group has positioned 
its dominant status in the seed industry, fumigation and agro-chemicals 
industries in Vietnam- the first step to generate a sustainable production 
value chain from seeds and agro-chemicals to finished products. In parallel 
with the agricultural sector, the PAN Group also occupied a leading position in 
food, including confectionery, cashew nuts, traditional fish sauce, pangasius 
and processed shrimp for export with long-standing and prestigious brand 
names with quality always ranked in the high grade segment.
Key personnel of the PAN Group and its member companies including 
those who have been with the companies for a long time, are experienced, 
enthusiastic and share their aspiration and visions with the Group. Valuable 
human resource is the great motivation to facilitate the whole Group to 
develop in a spirit of innovation and creativity. 
The PAN Group owns production and distribution systems throughout 
the country with over 3,000 agents to distribute agricultural materials, 
cooperation in production with over 60,000 farmer households on an area 
of nearly 50,000 hectares. In the food sector, the PAN Group owns a wide 
domestic distribution network with more than 200 major distributors, 
covering more than 145,000 points of sale across the country. In addition, the 
PAN Group’s products are exported to over 40 countries around the world, 
especially fastidious markets with high quality demand such as the U.S., 
Japan, Australia, Canada, Europe, etc., 
Governance system has been developed in transparency, professionalism 
and compliance with high governance standards regularly applied 
throughout functional units of member companies and the Group. The 
Group’s consistent principle is to create a favorable mechanism for 
every member company to be proactive and creative in order to maximize 
potentials of the company and the Group as a whole. 
Our partners are big investors such as Sojitz (Japan’s leading Trading and 
Investment Group), IFC (affiliated to the World Bank) and TAEL Two Partners, 
etc., who are contributing to add more values for the PAN Group through 
their participation in the Board of Directors, consulting on specialized issues 
in each specific field, connecting business opportunities for the PAN Group 
to go further into the world market.
Strength in Research and Development (R&D) to meet international 
quality standards with a research team consisting of leading experts in the 
fields of agriculture and food in Vietnam. The PAN Group also cooperates 
with domestic and foreign research institutes and universities to bring in 
new and high-quality products, improve production processes, respond the 
needs of domestic  consumers and for export.
Benefits from preferential corporate income tax when owning member 
companies in the fields of science and technology, agriculture and fishery 
operating in difficult areas.

SWOT ANALYSIS
WEAKNESS 
Production infrastructure (storage warehouses, processing factories, research and testing facilities) and human 
resource for management has been insufficient and failed to keep pace with rapid growth on large scale in recent 
years among member companies and the whole Group.  
Recruitment of senior management personnel has not timely met the rapid HR demands of the PAN Group to 
implement new projects in the fields of Agriculture and Food. 
OPPORTUNITY
Agricultural, aquatic and food product exports are expected to continue a positive 
trend when the COVID-19 pandemic is gradually controlled over the globe along with 
vaccination being implemented in some countries. A solid macroeconomic foundation, 
ability to control the pandemic and stabilization of production are the advantages for 
Vietnam with readiness to meet the world’s food demand.
Opportunities to export key products to value-added markets are on a rise when trade 
agreements between Vietnam and economic regions take effect (CPTPP, EVFTA, RCEP, 
UKVFTA...) with advantages of preferential tariffs and quotas. These are consumer 
markets for high-end products with high selling prices, but strict requirements on 
quality and technical barriers of imported goods. Therefore, it requires the PAN Group 
as well as Vietnamese businesses to unceasingly improve competitiveness.
The urgent need to handle issues of fragmented production, connection and 
accomplishment of the agricultural value chain creates an opportunity for the PAN 
Group to continue building up and expanding the integrated full value chain with support 
from the Government’s development policy and the inevitable market development 
trend. 
Improvement of people’s income, more interest and understanding of food safety 
are positive factors to enlarge the market segments that the PAN Group is targeting 
ahead. 
THREAT
The scale of Vietnam’s agricultural production is still fragmented in value 
chains and remains many intermediaries, making it difficult to organize large-
scale production and apply science and technology to ensure consistent quality, 
stability and high standard.
Climate change and epidemics are becoming more complicated and 
unpredictable, causing damages to agricultural production, especially in countries 
strongly affected by climate change like Vietnam. Droughts, saltwater intrusion, 
floods, and diseases frequently occur, seriously affecting the cultivated areas, 
productivity and quality of crops.
The labor force in agriculture of Vietnam is largely untrained with low quality and 
improper disciplines. This is a big challenge for high-tech agriculture development 
and advanced applications because it requires less labor but more skills as well as 
disciplines in performance of the labor force in high-tech agriculture.

A. BUSINESS SPECIFIC RISKS
DEMAND RISK 
Solutions to minimize risk
In seed segment, demand risk refers to the possibility of lower than 
expected consumer demand for a firm’s products or services. This risk 
is realized whenever the Group loses access to, share within, or fail to 
penetrate, a target market. The market is small and split between 260 
companies. Each province has its own seeds, with no truly dominant 
varieties, and the product quality is uneven. Domestic producers have 
to compete with standardized, high-quality imports sold by larger 
and more organized agribusinesses. All of these factors lead to low 
competitiveness and low price – both embodiments of realized demand 
risk. 
For agrochemicals segment, realization of demand risk also tends 
to result from competition. Aside from this, there are reputational 
threats that menace the industry generally. Over the past few years, the 
agrochemicals market has been scandalized by the sale of fake and/or 
counterfeit goods. The scandals have created hesitation in the minds of 
potential customers, leading to lower revenue.
In export flowers segment, faces less imminent demand risks because 
Group has signed a contract to import their entire crop. In addition, 
Group’s flower production will likely only meet half of the Japanese 
partner’s demand. 
To minimize this risk, Group has conducted many surveys to assess 
market conditions. It has also tried to increase the quality of its offerings 
by participating in research and technology transfers that allow it to 
produce seed varieties with high yields and strong disease resistance 
characteristics, such as VNR20,... In addition, Group constantly offers 
discounts and sends officers to give free technology training to farmers.
In agrochemicals segment, Group has continuously surveilled the 
market, researched and developed flexible sales policies, and 
attempted to optimize costs.
I. THE AGRICULTURAL SEGMENT
In agricultural segment, the Group faces the normal risks of the industry 
including:

Solutions to minimize risk
Solutions to minimize risk
Operational risk is the possibility that a firm will suffer losses 
greater than forecast from insufficient internal processes 
or external events beyond its control.  Adverse weather 
is an important operational risk that directly threatens 
the core production activities of Group. When such risk is 
realized, it reduces crop yield, crop quality, and tends to 
result in increased seed consumption. Vietnam’s central 
highlands are ideal for certain kinds of cultivation; however, 
they are also home to frequent damaging rainstorms and 
periodic droughts, both of which have a negative impact on 
agricultural operations. 
To minimize operational risks, especially those posed by 
adverse weather events, Group has expanded, and will 
continue to expand, its production areas into different 
ecological zones. It has also maintained warehouses in Dong 
Van and Ba Vi since 2015, where it stockpiles goods to ensure 
continuity of production in case of supply disruption. Finally, 
Group is researching and developing products with cold, 
drought, pest and disease resistance properties to reduce 
the impact of natural disasters and climate change on crop 
yields.
In export flowers, conducts most of its planting and 
growing operations in Belgian and Dutch greenhouses, 
complemented by Israeli irrigation and dike systems. This 
makes their operations less likely to be affected by adverse 
weather.
To minimize further realization of this risk, the company 
has cooperated with local authorities to actively restructure 
planting areas and promote the use of high-quality plant 
varieties meant to improve farmers’ income, help farmers 
sell their crop, keep them on the land, and prevent further 
reductions in the area under cultivation. 
Supply risk is the possibility that a firm will be unable to 
source the raw materials it requires for its basic activities. 
The most fundamental and troubling source of supply risk in 
Vietnam’s agricultural sector is the increasing scarcity and 
fragmentation of land. We cannot grow crops if we do not 
have adequate amounts or concentrations of land on which to 
grow them. Vietnam’s agricultural land is highly fragmented 
due to the nature of the terrain, high population density, 
land allocations, culture, and history. The area available for 
cultivation shrinks gradually every year due to urbanization 
and industrialization. The reduction of available hectarage 
has had consequences for all Vietnamese agriculture, but 
especially for rice production.
In export flower segment, the central highlands, including 
Lam Dong province, have very favorable conditions for 
planting. Group’s operations benefit from these favorable 
conditions and it is buying more land in the area.

II. FOOD SEGMENT
This segment is primarily exposed to demand risk and supply risk, the former from ever-changing 
consumer preferences, and the latter from unpredictable changes in the prices of production 
inputs. Competitive pressure from large market entrants is also an important consideration.  
In cashew processing, the Vietnamese cashew nut harvest 
runs from February to May every year and coincides with the 
beginning of the rainy season. If the harvest goes poorly, or if 
the crop is poorly handled post-harvest, the cashew nuts will 
not dry properly, lowering their quality. The quality of imported 
cashew nuts, mainly from African countries, is also affected by 
less-than-ideal weather and transport conditions. 
Regarding the coffee segment, business activities are also 
exposed to risks from fluctuating prices of raw coffee. Although 
Vietnam is the second largest coffee exporter in the world in 
terms of output, the price of raw materials is unstable but 
fluctuates erratically, depending on the world coffee price.
In confectionery segment, production is highly dependent on raw 
materials like starch, sugar and butter. However, the price of 
these raw materials has been, and is forecast to remain, low and 
stable.
The tastes of Vietnamese consumers are changing fast and the 
market is demanding more high-quality, healthy, and convenient 
products. If The PAN Group’s food companies fail to develop new 
products to meet these demands, they risk falling behind.
The Vietnamese market also has begun to attract the attention 
of international investors. Many multinational companies have 
recently invested. The financial strength and high production 
capacities of foreign multinationals are creating huge 
competition pressures for domestic enterprises. The risk of 
losing market share and reducing revenue is quite clear.
Cashew nut processing activity currently faces many market 
risks as well as competitive pressure due to a number of main 
reasons: (i) fluctuating price of cashew kernels that makes 
export enterprises unable to attend. Predicting the market and 
being able to bear large losses, (ii) many large enterprises are 
also participating in the market due to low barriers of entry 
leading to increased competition pressure, and (iii) cashew nuts 
with products. substitutes that consumers may switch to as 
almonds, leading to reduced competitive advantage.
For coffee, the Group’s main market is specialty coffee, with 
clean products, traceability, and high quality coffee varieties. 
This is a very potential market of Vietnam, when the standard 
of living of people has increased significantly, along with 
increasing demand for enjoying safe, quality and special foods. 
Currently, this segment market is relatively fragmented, with 
the participation of many small and medium-sized companies 
due to low entry barriers, low initial investment capital.
To deal with supply risk, Group has prepared a plan to upgrade 
and enlarge its storage system and processing chain in order to 
ensure the best quality of material inputs. The project completed 
in 2017. In addition, PAN has also enhanced its raw material 
market forecasts so that it can purchase and store quality supply 
at reasonable volumes and prices.
In confectionery segment, Group has signed fixed price plus 
percentage contracts with a variety of input suppliers to diversify 
sources of supply and minimize the impact of price fluctuations.
The Group has developed specialty coffee growing areas, closely 
connect to farmers with technical, economic support, and 
commitment to take consumption. Raw materials purchasing 
contracts are signed long-term, with relatively stable prices, 
thereby reducing the risk of input price fluctuations.
To minimize these risks, PAN has stepped up its R&D, 
marketing, and new product development efforts. PAN’s R&D 
budget for the period from 2015 to 2020 is higher than the budget 
for the previous period. Group is also improving its marketing by 
moving into spaces that it has heretofore neglected, like online 
marketing and creative television content, and also restructuring 
and reorganizing its traditional distribution methods as it seeks 
to access new trade channels.
In cashew processing, PAN is currently restructuring and 
shifting its focus to high-quality value-added products that can 
command consistently high prices to reduce risks from changing 
market conditions.
With coffee, the Group defines quality not only from brand, 
processing, but also from seeding, planting, tending and 
harvesting from its own farms, thus making a difference. with 
other brands. In addition, the Group also participates in many 
fairs and exhibitions in high-end markets such as the US, Japan, 
and the EU to find opportunities to export specialty coffee.

III. AQUACULTURE
PAN’s seafood business has established its position and high competitiveness in the international 
market, one of the leading corporation in Vietnam. However, the Group’s seafood business still 
faces many difficulties due to the impact of typical risks as follows:
Clam harvest yield depends on natural spat production. Unusually 
hot weather and pollution have recently caused higher death 
rates for clam spats, which has directly affected production 
capacity and yield. Pangasius production is threatened by 
environmental degradation, stock contamination issues, and 
disease outbreaks. However, while there have been no major 
epidemics recently, minor outbreaks during the fish breeding 
process require frequent management. 
Fish sauce is threatened by both competitive pressures and raw 
material shortages. These shortages are due to a narrowing 
of fishing grounds and the common use of indiscriminate, 
unsustainable harvesting methods which lead to depletions of 
fish stock.
Shrimp  is exposed supply risk through unpredictable changes 
in shrimp price and quality. The risk can be realized in various 
ways: a decline in the quality of the environment, changes in 
breeding stock quality, poor use of technology, insufficient feed 
supplies, and epidemics.
Major export market such as EU and USA penetration is difficult, 
and demand may be lower than forecast due to high levels of 
competition, unpredictable changes in consumer behavior, and 
the more rigorous regulation of food imports, either due to 
health concerns, or as a form of trade protectionism.
Traditional fish sauce products are facing tough competition 
from industrial fish sauce. The image of the entire traditional fish 
sauce sector has been adversely affected by media campaigns 
discussing the supposed high levels of arsenic found in some 
traditional fish sauce brands.
In pangasius and shrimp segment, to minimize environmental 
risks, PAN has taken steps to optimize the farming environment 
and minimize farmed fish and clam disease and mortality rates. 
In parallel, the company is seeking to diversify its supply by 
accessing new sources of clams in both north and south. 
To cope with increasingly aggressive competition over raw 
materials, PAN has taken several measures to shorten the time 
between material acquisition and processing. Specifically, it has 
created two production bases located near ports where it buys 
large amounts of fish – Phan Ri and Ca Na. 
Group also routinely prepares detailed purchase plans and 
monitors the shrimp supply in its farming areas to have the best 
possible information about its production inputs. PAN is growing 
its own shrimp to ensure steady supply.
In pangasius and shrimp segment , to minimize demand 
reduction and regulatory risk, we consistently manages the 
quality of its production processes according to international 
standards of sustainable development like ASC, GLOBALG.A.P., 
and MSC. In 2020, it introduced a series of policies on quality 
management and manufacturing improvements to increase 
efficiency, improve quality, and lower cost.
Group uses modern technology to create and maintain the 
quality of traditional fish sauce products. In the pursuit of quality, 
584 Nha Trang fish sauce meets ISO 22000:2005, HACPP, GMP, 
and SSOP certifications to create unique product of tastes and 
colors. It is also seeking to expand to other Asian markets.
In exporting shrimp segment, PAN  focuses on investing in

changing requirements of consumer markets.

Environmental pollution negatively affects The PAN

and exhaust gases are agents that can cause pollution if they 
are not properly treated, adversely affecting the company’s 
production activities. Incidents, if occurred, not only affect 
the surrounding environment but also reduce the reputation 
of the Group.
If an incident occurs it shall immediately affect the health 
and even the lives of employees. Therefore, this issue is 
always placed on top of every business. Although production 
in agriculture - food sectors is not at high risk of accidents, 
there remains a possibility of incidents, such as hand pinch, 
electric shock, fire and explosion, slip and fall, poisoning, 
etc., Apart from consequences on human-being, settlement 
costs and subsequent legal liability also cause heavy affects 
on the business.
For agricultural and food products, the risk in quality is quite 
possible, even threatening the safety of users. Risks could be 
arisen from many factors and really affect the business, not 
only in term of material damage but also the reputation and 
trust before the customers and investors, etc., Therefore, 
this is the core in production and product related risks are of 
our particular concern as a vital element in the development 
process.
PAN always selects raw material and production areas that 
are safe and have little risk of contamination, and always 
dispatches technical staff to work closely with households to 
control the production process and quality.
In processing, all types of waste are applied the 3R principles: 
Reduce - Reuse - Recycle to minimize the possibility of 
pollution. All boiler systems are designed to discharge into 
the environment in response to the Vietnamese standard 
regulations on emission. Wastewater is also treated to the 
required standard before being discharged, especially there 
is a wastewater quality monitoring system and data virtually 
transmistted to the provincial Department of Natural 
Resources and Environment. For activities with risks of 
causing environmental pollution with chemicals, an incident 
response plan has been developed and approved by the State 
management agency.
In addition to the regulations by laws to ensure the health 
and safety for employees, such as health check, protective 
equipment, training, The PAN Group’s companies have 
also invested in production lines with modern equipment 
to minimize the risks of incidents and limit hazardous jobs 
to employees. At every factory, an occupational safety and 
health network has been set up and it alternately monitors 
safety issues and international standards to ensure work 
safety. To come up with further improvement, The PAN 
Group has also established a set of sustainable development 
indicators, including the most important one which is the 
number of accidents happened. This indicator shall be 
monitored and reported annually to assess the safety status 
in production. 
The PAN Group has built up a tightened production and control 
system, and applied technology and management tools to 
create good products as truly committed and announced as

modern production lines imported from Europe and Japan, 
the technology transferred from big manufacturers, and 
the food safety and quality management system such as 
ISO22000, FSSC22000, BRC, IFS, etc.,

CREDIT RISK
Credit risk directly affects the business operations (mainly 
customer receivables) and financial operations of The 
PAN Group, including its bank deposits, foreign exchange 
transactions, and other financial instruments.
Solutions to minimize risk
To effectively control credit risk, The PAN Group periodically 
considers the creditworthiness of customers and the 
condition of its deposits and other financial instruments. 
The Group has focused on maintaining strict control over 
outstanding customer receivables and employs credit 
control staff to reduce risk. The PAN Group approves a list 
of customers based on their financial situation and payment 
history on a quarterly and yearly basis.

treasurer. Only large, high-profile banks shall be chosen for 
deposit placement. We maintain a system of continuous risk 
reporting to closely monitor these operations.

The PAN Group’s interest rate risk exposure mainly comes 
from short-term liabilities as well as short-term deposits of 
the company and some of its subsidiaries.

The PAN Group  manages interest rate risks by carefully 
monitoring relevant markets, including currency markets. 
The PAN Group’s Accounting-Finance Department and 
those of member companies produce forecasts, sensitivity 
analyses, and adjust leverage and investment strategies 
according to their prevailing view of interest rate risk.   
In addition, PAN currently mainly uses equity and bond loans 
with relatively fixed interest rates, so it is hardly affected by 
financial expenses due to the adjustment of interest rate 
level. . PAN’s member companies, which operate in the 
fields of agriculture, fisheries, and food processing, can 
access preferential loans with low and fixed interest rates 
from banks, thereby leading to interest risks. productivity is

at the member companies.

F. MARKET RISKS
PRICE RISK: STOCK PRICE RISK
Price risk is the chance of loss resulting from a negative 
change in the value of a portfolio. 
Since pivoting to focus on the agriculture and food sectors, 
The PAN Group’s investments are all long-term and 
strategic. For The PAN Group’s holdings, therefore, the risk 
of meaningful negative stock price fluctuations is not very 
high.
Solutions to minimize risk
The PAN Group manages price risk using Value at Risk (VAR), 
establishing conservative investment limits, and diversifying 
the investment portfolio. The PAN Group’s investment sub-
committee is responsible for considering and approving 
investment decisions in stocks. They focus on buying the 
stock of companies that have good internal operations, 
reasonable price-to-earnings ratios, and other metrics 
indicating stability. 
Stock price risk is regularly reviewed by the Finance-
Accounting department and the CFO.
COMMODITY PRICE RISKS
The PAN Group and its subsidiaries operate in many 
different fields that are sensitive to the price of commodities: 
agriculture, seafoods. Adverse commodity price fluctuations 
are a realization of supply risk when member companies 
require these commodities as inputs. They are realizations of 
demand risk whenever a member needs to sell materials it 
produces to a third party. Rapid changes in commodity prices 
can damage The PAN Group’s business and operations.
Solutions to minimize risk
The PAN Group manages commodity price risks through 
carefully monitoring domestic and foreign markets, ensuring 
timely commodity purchases, production planning, and 
prudent stockpiling. 
Risks related to commodity price fluctuations are monitored 
by the purchasing department, the production departments 
of subsidiaries, and reported to Director of Production and 
Chief Executive Officer on a weekly basis.
EXCHANGE RATE RISK
Exchange rate risk is the risk of loss due to adverse changes 
in exchange rates and it arises whenever The PAN Group or 
affiliates engage in transactions denominated in currencies 
other than the Vietnamese Dong. The PAN Group is exposed 
to this risk through its subsidiaries and affiliates engaged in 
import and export and whenever they raise foreign capital.
Solutions to minimize risk
The PAN Group estimates exchange rate risk through the 
issuance of shares for capital increase and has adjustment 
policies for incomes with foreign currency elements, export 
mechanisms, and trade credit. Import and export plans are 
carefully developed to limit exchange rate risk. 
Of The PAN Group’s subsidiaries, Aquatex Bentre, FIMEX 
VN, VFC, Pan-SALADBOWL and Lafooco have the largest 
FX risk exposure. As Aquatex Bentre and FIMEX VN buy raw 
materials within Vietnam and export their finished products, 
they benefit from the relative depreciation of the Dong. 
The import and export operations of Lafooco and VFC are 
controlled and monitored more closely, since they source 
most of their inputs abroad. Companies seek to minimize the 
impact of exchange rate fluctuations generally.
LIQUIDITY RISK
Liquidity risk occurs when The PAN Group faces difficulties 
fulfilling financial obligations due to cash shortages. For 
The PAN Group, this risk arises when the maturity dates of 
financial assets and financial liabilities are mismatched.  
Solutions to minimize risk
The PAN Group tightly manages its cash flow and maintains 
a reasonable amount of cash and deposits. It also arranges 
short-term and long-term credit contracts with banks and 
other financial institutions to ensure loans will be repaid 
after the Group completes financial plans, maintains 
liquidity indexes at healthy levels, and maintains a balanced 
ratio between assets and liabilities. Every month, cash flow 
and liquidity position statements are made by the relevant 
departments and reported to the Executive Board. The PAN 
Group faces low liquidity risk.
Market risks arise from the possibility of loss caused by adverse moves in interest rates, exchange rates, market liquidity, 
and stock prices. Market risk management aims to keep those risks within acceptable bounds while maximizing profits.

Q1 and Q2 of 2020 were marked as a challenging period of Vietnam’s aquaculture industry 
while the POs were delayed by social distancing in big import countries like USA and EU. 
Till Q3/2020, after the epidemic was successfully controlled, the new market was recorded 
with some thriving signs. Vietnam’s fishery export continued growing in Q4/2020 with 
growth rate of 2.7% compared to the same period, obtaining 2,4 billion USD mainly thanks to 
outstanding growth of export shrimp product. White shrimp was recorded with positive growth 
in Q4, fulfilling 17.4% of the same period. Ending 2020, aquaculture export reached 8.4 billion 
USD, slightly down 1.9% against the same period. This was the great effort of aquaculture 
industry when myriad of the Covid-19 related difficulties were faced as what VASEP shared.
Shrimp sector group - Successful 2020 year thanks to good production maintenance and 
grasping opportunities in the context of global interrupted shrimp supply. In 2020, the 
global shrimp production and trading activities were significantly affected by the Covid-19 
pandemic outbreak, resulting in lower consumption demand in developed countries. However, 
the supply was also interrupted when the world’s big shrimp suppliers such as Ecuador, 
India, Indonesia and Thailand, etc., were severely damaged by the epidemic and the domestic 
production was delayed. Thanks to great success in the Covid-19 pandemic control, Vietnam 
maintained shrimp production, flexibly shifting the market and making use of interrupted 
supply time to enhance export. Moreover, the retail sales of frozen aquaculture items in 
developed countries were sharply increased when the local persons tended to eat more at 
home rather than eating in restaurant. Accordingly, export to USA, EU, Korea and U.K climbed 
up 33% YoY, 6% YoY, 3% YoY and 20% YoY, respectively.

The local residents’ consumption behaviors and habits on packed foods are remarkably 
affected by the Covid-19 pandemic. Two highlights affecting the sector include transformation 
to multipurpose products and booming on online shopping.
The pandemic-related social distancing has created a great push to the world’s sales channel 
transformation and new trend in shopping habits. Consumption via online sales channel grew 
25% of value in 2020 and forecast to obtain the average growth rate of 7%-9% in the next 5 
years as a long-term change impact of consumer’s behavior on consumption trend in general 
and packed food category in particular. However, the conventional trading channel (GT) was 
still made up big density in total retailer value in Vietnam; the modern trading (MT) channel 
was remarkably shifted in terms of retail model with growth of small-size outlets.
In Q4/2020, the Company’s strength was still upheld in developing GT and MT export sales 
task forces and maintaining the two-digit growth rate for the number of distributors and POSs 
against the same period of last year. Moreover, the Company was also facilitated to make 
attempts to restructure and standardize the sales channels, change the sales and customer 
care model in GT and MT channels to be well matched with online transformation trends.
At the end of the year, a series of new products were launched and actively welcome by the 
customers. The partners were also negotiated to further expand new and more diversified list 
of products from foods to beverage. 
The consumer’s online shopping trend was quickly developed. With response to that trend, 
the Company’s App Shop model was completed in 6 big cities such as Hanoi, Hai Phong, Da 
Nang, Nha Trang, Ho Chi Minh and Can Tho and PAN CG online sales website was put into 
operation at the end of December 2020.
In addition, the strategic distribution cooperation signing ceremony was held on 7 January 
2021 to fulfill the sustainable development goals, catch up with the development trends in 
the new period, making active contribution and speeding up the sharp growth between PAN 
CG and its partners, namely Ba Huan Company, Hae Ryong Foods, Quoc Viet Foods Import- 
Export Company and International Food Industry Joint Stock Company.
With great advantages about PAN CG’s nationwide distribution network and partners’ 
international standardized products, the Company is expected to best exploit the strength 
of each Party and market potential, offering the best healthy and international standardized 
product ranges with reasonable price.

A strategic compensation policy is a “lever” for developing human resources at an organization 
that encourages passion in the workplace. It is an effective tool for stabilizing human resources 
and attracting and retaining talent. The wage and reward policy of PAN has three tiers, Fair 
– Appropriate – Competitive, and is structured to ensure motivation for employees. The wage 
policy strictly complies with legal provisions, registered documentation with authorities, and 
commitment to employees. 
All PAN employees are paid based on a simple wage scale system, according to capacity, 
responsibility, workload, and performance. Reward systems for individual and group 
excellence: Bonuses go to the best-performing staff and year-end KPI evaluation stand-
outs. Extraordinary bonuses are given to individuals with outstanding achievements. The 
13th month salary and year-end bonuses are also given to recognize devoted employees. Any 
achievement is recognized and rewarded. The reward policy has encouraged employees with 
continuous contributions and efforts for a strong and sustainable PAN.
WAGE AND  
REWARDS
Welfare policy is a core component of PAN’s human resource strategy. It is an important link 
in the comprehensive value quantification chain that benefits employees and the brand. PAN’s 
existing welfare policy is rated highly by employees, which enhances the loyalty, commitment, 
and satisfaction of personnel.
Employees enjoy benefits in compliance with the law. Moreover, PAN develops and applies 
welfare programs above and beyond legal requirements to motivate employees and recognize 
their efforts and contributions. The welfare policy is regularly readjusted to raise employee 
commitment and improve the corporate culture. All employees are provided periodic 
comprehensive medical check-ups. Permanent employees are entitled to additional health 
insurance from leading insurance companies (apart from health insurance mandated by 
law). Additional or special insurance is provided in particular cases. Employees are entitled 
to benefits and gifts on national holidays and other special occasions, for their children’s 
outstanding academic performances, hospital visits, weddings, difficult circumstances, …
Furthermore, PAN provide employees with fully-equipped facilities, e-working space and 
digital transformation in the industry 4.0… the diversified solution to working conditions is a 
competitive advantage, ensuring work continuity and efficiency, especially during the Covid-19 
pandemic.
Understanding that people are the most valuable assets in any organization. At PAN, we 
appreciate all contributions from employees. We maintain a system to help each employee 
mature in his or her career at PAN, as well as to help them contribute to the society and 
environment. All of these solutions are developed around and connected to the organization’s 
vision and culture.

INCREASE IN OWNERSHIP PERCENTAGE IN VIETNAM FUMIGATION JOINT STOCK COMPANY (VFC)
Reasons
VFC is a local leading manufacturer of agricultural materials, a very important chain in the 
agricultural production value chain to be developed and perfected by the PAN Group. VFC is recorded 
with myriad of high potentials especially when comprehensive cooperation is initiated to capitalize 
the available advantages. 
•	Agro-pharmaceuticals: VFC is characterized by over 25 years of experience, 7% of market shares, 
the second rank in the industry with revenue of 2,300 billion, nationwide distribution system and 
trusted as reliable partner of many the world leading pharmaceutical manufacturers (Syngenta, 
Kumiai, Nippon, etc.) 
•	Fumigation (for agricultural product export): VFC is recorded with over 30 years of experience, 60% 
of market shares, revenue of ~300 billion VND/ year (accounting for 11% of total revenue, making 
contribution up to 22% of profit before tax), a member of International Maritime Fumigation 
Organization (IMFO) since 1999, awarding with the certificate of ISO 9001:2000 BVQI-UKAS/ ANSI-
RAB since 2001.
•	VFC is supported by nationwide distribution system and 16 VFC branches in provinces with over 
2,500 agro-pharmaceuticals agents (sub-agent), 2,300 fumigation customers/agents. 
•	Long-lasting brand: VFC under agro-pharmaceuticals, fumigation and pest control perspectives is 
referred to the great professionalism and prestige. VFC is prioritized rather than other rivals by the 
demanding exporters of agricultural products (EU, USA and Japan market). 
•	VFC is the home of extensively experienced and loyal managers, creating a reliable relationship 
with agency and customer system, as a favorable condition to further develop the resonance 
strength between VFC and the PAN Group.
•	In 2019, the PAN Group owned 41.88% of VFC’s charter capital with total investment value of 510 
billion VND. The PAN Group targeted to continue increase in owning the charter capital at VFC up 
to over 51% to consolidate VFC’s business results in the consolidated financial statements and 
scale up the Group.
Implementation 
method and 
schedule
In October 2020, public offer was officially initiated by the PAN Group to increase its ownership 
percentage in VFC. As a result, in November 2020, 2,151,871 VFC shares were successfully offered by 
the Group, increased by 47.97 % of VFC charter capital.
Investment 
results
As of 31 December 2020, the Group officially owned 47.97% of VFC charter capital, corresponding to 
15,390,932 shares.

MOBILIZATION OF ALL RESOURCES 
TO RUN THE PROGRAM “TOWARDS

the people in the central region affected by 
the floods and storms during 30th October

the CSR “Program for the central region”

of the plan to support people in the central 
region to overcome difficulties and address

reconstruction for localities after natural 
disasters through activities to repair damaged 
schools, hospitals, roads and houses, etc. 
through which the people were helped for life 
stabilization after the floods.

parallel with environmental protection and in response to 
the initiative of planting 1 billion trees by 2025 launched by

with conservation and social security with key activities to 
restoration and afforestation in Di Linh district, Lam Dong 
province.
Sustainable development and sharing of values with the 
community is always one of the top priorities of The PAN 
Group. Many raw material development areas of the Group

Binh Phuoc, coffee areas in Da Lat, Son La, Khe Sanh, Pleiku, 
A Luoi, etc., Therefore, the development and protection of 
forests has always been concentrated by the Group.

The Group’s strategic orientation in the period 2020 - 2025 is to focus on developing core 
production capacity in each business segment on existing platforms, and at the same time, 
take advantage of opportunities for M&A if any in the market to merge good companies in line 
with the business areas and development strategies.
Therefore, in 2020, the Group did not generate major M&A activities, partly due to impacts 
of the Covid-19 pandemic which made it difficult to find opportunities for cooperation and 
investment. The majority of the Group’s new investments during the year were purchases 
to increase ownership in the existing companies (VFG - agriculture and FMC - fisheries). For 
the greater part, the Group and its member companies focused their resources on projects 
to improve internal production capacity: Vinaseed: increased capacity for drying seeds, rice; 
FMC: increased the area of ​ponds and processing plants; 584 Nha Trang: built a new factory.
Notale M&A transctions during the year include:
Increase of ownership rate at Vietnam Fumigation Joint Stock Company: In October 2020, 
the PAN Group officially made a public offer to increase its ownership rate at VFC. As a result, 
in November 2020, the Group successfully offered to buy 2,151,871 shares of VFC, raising its 
ownership to 47.97 % of VFC’s charter capital. In December 2020, the Group transferred all 
47.97% of VFC’s charter capital, equivalent to 15,390,932 shares to a member company, the 
PAN Farm Joint Stock Company.
VFC is the leading company in the field of production and trading of agricultural materials, a 
very important link in the agricultural production value chain that the PAN Group is building 
and completing. VFC has great potentials, especially when cooperating comprehensively with 
PAN to realize existing advantages. The main strengths of VFC are: (i) VFC has a nationwide 
distribution system with 16 VFC branches in the provinces with more than 2,500 agents (level 
2) of agricultural and pharmaceutical products, 2,300 customers/fumigation agents; (ii) VFC 
has a very experienced and long-term management team, creating a strong connection with 
the system of agents and customers, which is a favorable factor to promote the synergistic 
advantage between VFC and the PAN Group; and (iii) Long-standing brand: Talking about VFC 
in agro-pharmaceuticals, sterilization, pest control means professionalism and prestige. 
Customers exporting agricultural products to fastidious markets (EU, Japan, USA) prefer VFC 
to other firms.
Investment to increase capital at Sao Ta Food Joint Stock Company (Fimex VN): In January 
2021, Fimex VN increased its capital through the form of preferential offer to existing 
shareholders at the ratio 5:1, selling price of 25,000 VND/share. The PAN Group is estimated 
to exercise all its buying rights, thereby increasing the investment in Fimex of PAN and its 
member companies to about 160 billion VND. 
Fimex VN is the leading company in Vietnam’s shrimp industry with great development 
potential for many years to come. It has a long-term development strategy and a plan to 
maximize the potential and available advantages.
In 2020, Fimex VN continued to achieve new growth milestones with the sale of 4.4 trillion 
VND, increasing up to 19% over the same period. This is also the company’s historic sale 
since its establishment.  
The PAN Group and Fimex VN have been cooperating very effectively in the fields and realized 
a lot of synergistic values between Fimex VN and other member companies of the Group.
The PAN Group has exposed its positive appreciation about Fimex VN’s prospects and wished 
to in-depth strengthening cooperation with the company.

BUSINESS PERFORMANCE IN 2020
In 2020, The PAN Group faced with many difficulties due to the outbreak of the Covid-19 
pandemic, peaking in the first 6 months of the year, plus the great impact from the historic 
salinity drought in the Mekong Delta and floods in the Central region. However, thanks to the 
Government’s success in the fight against the pandemic, the Group’s proactive coordination 
and efforts from member units, the Group still exceeded the plan at most of its main targets.
Also during the year, despite many tough times, the Group still successfully completed 
its role as a special sponsor for Vietnam’s 2020 ASEAN Chairmanship. PAN also has 5 
product categories recognized as the National Brand, namely value-added products which 
are being consumed strongly both domestically and for export. In addition, with the goal 
of sustainable development, the whole Group has joined hands to provide material support 
for the Government’s anti-epidemic work, mobilized great resources to provide goods and 
necessities for the Central region after natural disasters, and started a project of afforestation 
aiming at restoring silviculture.

IMPROVEMENT ON  
ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE, 
POLICIES AND MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
The Law on Enterprises encourages joint stock companies to apply international good governance practices by 
offering two options for businesses, opening a mechanism to allow joint stock companies to follow the governance 
model without a Supervisory Board, but having an independent member of the Board of Directors instead. According 
to international experience, this shall help separate much clearer between ownership and governance.
To timely keeping pace with the trend of international governance, on 18th June 2020, the Group’s General Meeting 
of Shareholders issued the Resolution No.01-06/2020/NQ-DHDCD approving a change of the Group’s management 
structure. Accordingly, the organizational structure of management after the change included: General Meeting of 
Shareholders, Board of Directors, Chief Executive Officer, Internal Audit Subcommittee under the BOD, Independent 
members of the BOD cum members of the Internal Audit Subcommittee and one independent member of the 
BOD was the Head of the Subcommittee. The application of this model shall help tighten the monitoring of risk 
management, improve transparency in operation of the BOD and the Board of Management.

Apart from building a strong governance structure on the basis of compliance with the provisions of Vietnamese 
laws in  combination with application of international practices on corporate governance, the Group has developed, 
issued and continuously updated its system of internal documents in order to create a consistent and transparent 
governance mechanism to control and supervise operation of the businesses in a professional, transparent and 
effective manner, contributing to ensure  interests of the shareholders and harmonization of the stakeholders’ 
interests. In 2020, the Group amended and promulgated the Company’s Charter and Internal Regulations on 
Corporate Governance, focusing on contents of the organizational structure, shareholders’ rights and the 
procedures to organize the General Meeting of Shareholders as required in reality. In September 2020, the Group 
issued the Operation Regulation of the Internal Audit Subcommittee, creating a foundation for the subcommittee’s 
activities right at the time it was established.
In 2021, the Group shall continue to review, amend and supplement provisions in the Charter and Internal Regulations 
in line with newly adopted legislation such as the 2020 Enterprise Law, the 2019 Securities Law. 
The Pan Group has annually reviewed the execution and application of internal standards at its member companies. 
This program aims to evaluate the compliance of regulations by laws and commitments before investors and 
customers on environment, labor safety and social responsibilities. The 2020 evaluation also referred to the 
execution of requirements of the ADB Protection Policy which the PAN Group pledged to comply with in 2019. Over 
the years, the annual assessment on socio-environmental issues has been consistently and effectively carried out 
by the Group’s member companies and so they continued to increasingly comply with and better meet international 
standards and practices.
Socio-environmental assessment is the requirement of the Production Principles which was issued by the PAN 
Group and has been applied internally at its member companies.

PLAN AND ORIENTATION OF 
THE BOD IN 2021
•	 Orientation and the production and business plan 2021 have been prepared by the Board of 
Management in the direction of maximizing resources for growth and market opportunities 
after successful control of the Covid-19 pandemic, ensuring the Company continues 
to develop in the right direction to become “a regional leading company in the field of 
Agriculture and Food, providing packaged Agricultural and Food products with safety, high 
quality and traceability for domestic and international markets”. 
•	 In parallel with the business plan 2021, the BOD shall focus on market solutions to prevent 
risks of epidemics and climate change which have been considered as great impacts if 
any on the entire operation and business activities of the Group. These solutions include 
contingency plans in production, inventory and finance - investment.
•	 Continuing to look for opportunities and buy dominant shares of the companies with 
strength in agriculture and food sectors to focus on improving and expanding the 
Agriculture and Food platform. Special attention shall be paid to implementation of the 
uncompleted targets in 2020 due to market conditions.
•	 Instructing implementation of detailed review of production and business efficiency and 
efficiency of capital investment at the Group and its member companies, therefore making 
necessary adjustments in strategy as well as the ownership structure of the Group, 
ensuring the best interests for shareholders.
•	 Continuing to support subsidiaries in strategy formulation, governance and operation to 
maximize their potentials and improve business efficiency.
•	 Implementing circumspectly and maximizing efficiency of the approved business projects 
in agriculture and distribution.

The separation between the Chairman of the BOD and the CEO
The separation between the Chairman of the BOD and the CEO represents a clear division of responsibilities between the 
Chairman of the BOD and the CEO to ensure the independence of the BOD and the CEO. This separation also ensures the 
division of power, increases responsibilities and enhances the independence in decision-making of the Board of Directors.
Appointment of the BOD members
The appointment of new members to the BOD is carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Charter and Internal 
Governance Regulations of The PAN Group Joint Stock Company. In case there is a change of the BOD members in the 
mid-term, the BOD shall carry out the procedures to nominate and appoint a replacement member of the BOD in accordance 
with the provisions of the Charter and Internal Governance Regulations of the Company and then submit such appointment to 
the General Meeting of Shareholders for official approval in the nearest General Meeting of Shareholders. 
In 2020, The PAN Group had no change in number and the personnel of the BOD members.

2. 
SUBCOMMITTEES 
OF THE BOARD 
OF DIRECTORS
The Resolution No.16-07/2013/NQ-HĐQT issued on 15th July 2013 decided to establish 04 
Sub-Committees to support the activities of the Board of Directors, including Investment 
Subcommittee, Human Resource Subcommittee, Social Responsibility Subcommittee 
and Independent Governance Subcommittee. However, the Resolution of the 2014 Annual 
General Meeting of Shareholders approved the establishment of the Investment Council 
with the functions and duties as specified in Clause 3, Article 29 of the Charter of the 
Pan Pacific Joint Stock Company issued on 28th October 2014. Accordingly, the Resolution 
No.15-06/2014/NQ-HĐQT canceled the contents related to the Investment Subcommittee 
in the Company’s internal documents and dismissed the Investment Subcommittee under 
the Board of Directors.
On 6th April 2015, the Board of Directors approved for establishment of the Sustainable 
Development Subcommittee affiliated to the BOD to support the latter on development, 
consultation, monitoring and evaluation over sustainable development activities of the 
Company with focus on three big issues on economics, environment and the society. 
This subcommittee establishment reﬂects the Company’s strategy to professionalizing 
its socio-environmental activities and code of conduct realization for sustainable 
development in the future. Members participated in the subcommittee and coordination 
network of member companies are those who have comprehensive understanding of the 
Company’s activities, are experienced in social science and have involved in training and 
assessments on environment, safety and social issues for corporations from Europe, USA, 
Japan, Korea… such as Sumitomo, Yamaha, CJ Vina, Palffger and Levi Strauss (Levi’s), 
etc., The Sustainable Development Subcommittee was established under the Resolution 
No. 04-04/2015/NQ-HĐQT on 6th April 2015.
On 24th April 2015, the General Meeting of Shareholders of The PAN Group JSC (at that 
time it was the Pan Pacific JSC) subsequently approved cancellation of the Investment 
Council and removal of the provisions related to regulations of the Investment Council 
and amended the corresponding Charter through which all power and obligations of the 
Investment Council according to the provisions of the current Charter were transferred to 
the Board of Directors under the Article 7, Clause B of the Resolution No.01-04/2015/NQ-
DHDCD dated 24/04/2015.
On 18th November 2018, the Board of Directors of The PAN Group Joint Stock Company 
issued a resolution on approval to restructure personnel of Subcommittees under the 
BOD to meet the provisions of the Decree 71/2017/ND-CAP on corporate governance 
and Internal Regulations on corporate governance adopted by the General Meeting 
of Shareholders on 27th October 2018. Specifically, the Board of Directors approved 
renaming of the Subcommittee on Social Environment and Sustainable Development to 
the Sustainable Development Subcommittee.
On 29th September 2020, The PAN Group announced the Resolution No.02-09/2020/
NQ-HĐQT of the Board of Directors approving the establishment of the Internal Audit 
Subcommittee and adoption of the Internal Audit Regulations.
As of 31st December 2020, the Company had 04 Subcommittees under the Board of Directors 
including Human Resource Subcommittee, Sustainable Development Subcommittee, 
Independent Subcommittee and Internal Audit Subcommittee.

From September 2020, Internal Audit Committee was established with the following tasks 
and scope of work: 
•	 Independently evaluate the suitability and compliance with regulations, policies, the 
Company’s Charter and decisions of the General Meeting of Shareholders and the BOD;
•	 Check, review and evaluate the adequacy, effectiveness and efficiency of the internal audit 
system, risk management with the aim to improve this system;
•	 Assess the compliance with regulations by laws, control measures to ensure asset safety;
•	 Evaluate the compliance with the internal policies and procedures;
•	 Evaluate the means of protecting assets, verifying the existence of such assets;
•	 Evaluate internal audit through financial information and business processes;
•	 Evaluating activities or programs to determine whether results are consistent with 
established goals and objectives and whether activities or programs are carried out as 
planned;
•	 Evaluate the process of identifying, assessing and managing business risks;
•	 Assess the compliance with commitments in the contracts;
•	 Conduct internal audit of the Company and its subsidiaries (if required)
•	 Investigate violations within the Company;
•	 Unscheduled audit, consult at the request of the Board of Directors;
•	 Prepare annual audit report and internal audit plan to submit to the Board of Directors for 
approval and carry out internal audit activities according to the approved plan;
•	 Advise the Company in selecting and controlling the use of independent audit services; 
maintain regular communication with independent auditors to ensure effective cooperation;
•	 Periodically report on the purpose, authority, responsibility and performance of the Internal 
Audit Subcommittee.

5. ACTIVITIES OF THE BOD’S SUBCOMMITTEES
The composition of the Board of Directors of The PAN Group in 2020 ensured a balance between members of the Board of 
Directors who are executive members, non-executive members and independent members of the BOD.
Members of the Board of Directors are all personnel with many years of domestic and international experiences in areas of 
operation of the Company, including Agriculture and Food. They also have in-depth experiences in management, finance, 
sales, marketing, etc.,
Non-executive independent BOD members play an important role in providing professional and technical advice and helping 
the Company to access opportunities in the Agriculture and Food industry, including inventions, products, production methods 
and markets.
Given the qualifications and experience of the members of the Board of Directors as well as the existing structure of the BOD, 
all decisions could be made objectively and independently. 
Therefore, in addition to the general duties of the Board of Directors, independent members of the BOD also undertake the 
assigned tasks of the Subcommittees they participate in.
The subcommittees of the Board of Directors operate in accordance with the responsibilities and duties specified in the 
Charter, Corporate Governance Regulations and the Resolution No.01-04/2016/NQ-HĐQT. 
The subcommittees have made great efforts in developing and perfecting the operating regulations, at the same time effectively 
implementing the tasks and work of each subcommittee after being entrusted by the Board of Directors and the General 
Meeting of Shareholders. The activities and performance results of the subcommittees are timely reported to the Board 
of Directors and each member is proactive in performing his/her responsibilities and contributing opinions to the Board’s 
decisions.

IMPLEMENTATION OF CORPORATE 
GOVERNANCE REGULATIONS
The Board of Directors determined that improving the quality and capacity of corporate 
governance is an important content in the strategic direction of the Group in order to build a 
strong management system on the basis of applying international practices combined with 
the overall strength of resources to control and monitor activities responsibly, transparently 
and effectively.
The Group strictly implemented the regulations on information disclosure in the 
Circular 155/2015/TT-BTC, regulations of the Ho Chi Minh City Stock Exchange and 
the State Securities Commission. Information related to corporate governance, 
business operation and unusual information was disclosed by the Group within 
the prescribed time limit, ensuring transparency before all shareholders and 
investors.
The PAN Group also aimed to publish Vietnamese-English bilingual information 
so that foreign investors could easily access, learn and analyze information about 
the business. Important internal management documents of the Group such as 
the Charter, Internal Governance Regulations were translated and posted on 
the PAN’s website in both English and Vietnamese. Programs and documents 
for the Annual General Meeting of Shareholders, Minutes and Resolutions of the 
Meeting were all published in Vietnamese and English. This is an important step 
towards international governance practices in ensuring shareholder rights and fair 
treatment among shareholders, especially foreign shareholders and investors.
The Group recognized and respected the rights of shareholders, the owners 
of the Company, including minority shareholders and foreign shareholders by 
ensuring fair and appropriate treatment for each shareholder through disclosure 
of accurate, transparent and timely information. The Group paid attention to the 
adequacy of information disclosure so that shareholders could make decisions 
under provided information at the General Meeting of Shareholders, including 
voting and expressing opinions on significant changes and electing members of 
the Board of Directors based on the accurate, complete, transparent, and equitably 
shared information. Shareholders’ rights were also clearly defined in the Group’s 
Charter and protected by the Vietnamese laws.
Every year, the Board of Directors holds an effective Annual General Meeting of 
Shareholders. The Group sends shareholders full information about the meeting 
of shareholders, including attached documents with full information related to the 
meeting. The company also posts information related to the meeting on the websites 
of HOSE and The PAN Group so that shareholders have time to study properly. 
The General Meeting of Shareholders is held in accordance with the program 
mentioned in the relevant invitation letter. In 2020, the Group successfully held the 
annual General Meeting of Shareholders in the form of semi-virtual  conference. 
The Chairman of the Board of Directors and the Board of Management jointly 
answered questions and provided full information upon request of shareholders. 
Minutes of the General Meeting of Shareholders was recorded accurately, fully 
and timely in accordance with the laws and published together with the Resolution 
of the General Meeting of Shareholders to HOSE, SSC as well as posted on the 
website of PAN within 24 hours after the meeting.

2. INVESTOR RELATION ACTIVITIES
Investor Relations (IR) is always the activity in focus by the company in order to provide quick 
and sufficient information for the company’s shareholders in particular and investors in the 
market in general. In 2020, due to impacts of the Covid-19 pandemic, the company limited its 
face-to-face meetings, but held online events instead. 
2020 is the first year that the Group organized an online General Meeting of Shareholders, 
whereby shareholders directly watched the meeting program and asked questions as well as 
delivered opinions right at the Group’s website. The Meeting was taken place successfully 
with the number of direct attendees limited to only 20 participants at 2 sites in Hanoi and 
Ho Chi Minh City. However, there were more than 1,000 viewers on both in Vietnamese and 
English online versions.

3. FURTHER IMPROVEMENT TO ENHANCE 
CORPORATE GOVERNANCE PRACTICE
With the goal of applying and gradually approaching the corporate governance standards of 
the region and the world in the coming time, The PAN Group needs to continue doing the 
following tasks related to corporate governance:
•	 Continuing to update the PAN website with full disclosure of information for shareholders, 
customers, domestic and foreign investors to easily access. 
•	 Continuing to update, amend, supplement and comply with regulations on information 
disclosure and transparency as required in the Circular 96/2020/TT-BTC and standards 
in the regional corporate governance scorecard in the ASEAN region to provide timely and 
accurate information to domestic and foreign shareholders and investors.
•	 Participating in corporate governance training courses organized by the State Securities 
Commission. In addition, with a commitment to ensure corporate governance on the basis 
of applying international best practices, the Group shall regularly update knowledge and 
international practices on corporate governance internally and externally, and at the 
same time actively share information related to corporate governance and organizational 
structure with major institutional shareholders to take advantage of experiences in 
developing a corporate governance model with international governance standard.
In order to improve the quality of corporate governance, the Group has set forth long-term 
goals that need to focus on implementation and perfection in the next period as follows:
•	 Continuing to perfect the governance model in order to strengthen the coordination between 
the Group and its member units, and among the member units on the basis of ensuring the 
consistency and enhancing compliance across the Group;
•	 Promoting the role of centralized governance, supporting the Group’s governance over 
its member units in term of finance, human resource - training, information technology, 
brand, investment and fundamental construction of the whole Group;
•	 Regularly updating knowledge and international practices on corporate governance 
internally and externally to make it happen in reality at The PAN Group;
•	 Applying the ASEAN Corporate Governance Scorecard Tool to enhance the Group’s 
corporate governance capability and practice in Vietnam and reaching out to the region;
•	 Strengthening risk management, compliance and internal audit to provide information for 
corporate governance;
•	 Continuing to improve the performance of the Internal Audit Subcommittee with the 
supporting role of the Board of Directors.

MANAGEMENT’S RESPONSIBILITY
Management is responsible for the preparation and fair presentation of these consolidated financial statements in accordance 
with Vietnamese Accounting Standards, Vietnamese Enterprise Accounting System and the statutory requirements relevant 
to the preparation and presentation of the consolidated financial statements, and for such internal control as management 
determines is necessary to enable the preparation and presentation of the consolidated financial statements that are free 
from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error.
AUDITORS’ RESPONSIBILITY
Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these consolidated financial statements based on our audit. We conducted our 
audit in accordance with Vietnamese Standards on Auditing. Those standards require that we comply with ethical requirements 
and plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the consolidated financial statements are free 
from material misstatement.
An audit involves performing procedures to obtain audit evidence about the amounts and disclosures in the consolidated 
financial statements. The procedures selected depend on the auditors’ judgment, including the assessment of the 
risks of material misstatement of the consolidated financial statements, whether due to fraud or error. In making those 
risk assessments, the auditors consider internal control relevant to the Group’s preparation and fair presentation of the 
consolidated financial statements in order to design audit procedures that are appropriate in the circumstances, but not for 
the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the Group’s internal control. An audit also includes evaluating the 
appropriateness of accounting policies used and the reasonableness of accounting estimates made by management, as well 
as evaluating the overall presentation of the consolidated financial statements.
We believe that the audit evidence we have obtained is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our audit opinion.
OPINION
In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements give a true and fair view, in all material respects, of the consolidated 
financial position of the Group as at 31 December 2020, and of the consolidated results of its operations and its consolidated 
cash flows for the year then ended, in accordance with Vietnamese Accounting Standards, Vietnamese Enterprise Accounting

2. BASIS OF PREPARATION
2.1 ACCOUNTING STANDARDS AND SYSTEM
The consolidated financial statements of the Group, expressed in Vietnam dong (“VND”), are prepared in accordance with 
Vietnamese Enterprise Accounting System and other Vietnamese Accounting Standards issued by the Ministry of Finance 
as per:
•	 Decision No. 149/2001/QD-BTC dated 31 December 2001 on the Issuance and Promulgation of Four Vietnamese Accounting 
Standards (Series 1);
•	 Decision No. 165/2002/QD-BTC dated 31 December 2002 on the Issuance and Promulgation of Six Vietnamese Accounting 
Standards (Series 2);
•	 Decision No. 234/2003/QD-BTC dated 30 December 2003 on the Issuance and Promulgation of Six Vietnamese Accounting 
Standards (Series 3);
•	 Decision No. 12/2005/QD-BTC dated 15 February 2005 on the Issuance and Promulgation of Six Vietnamese Accounting 
Standards (Series 4); and
•	 Decision No. 100/2005/QD-BTC dated 28 December 2005 on the Issuance and Promulgation of Four Vietnamese Accounting 
Standards (Series 5).
Accordingly, the accompanying consolidated financial statements, including their utilisation are not designed for those who 
are not informed about Vietnam’s accounting principles, procedures and practices and furthermore are not intended to 
present the consolidated financial position and consolidated results of operations and consolidated cash flows of the Group in 
accordance with accounting principles and practices generally accepted in countries other than Vietnam.
2.2 APPLIED ACCOUNTING DOCUMENTATION SYSTEM
The Group’s applied accounting documentation system is the General Journal system.
2.3 FISCAL YEAR
The Group’s fiscal year applicable for the preparation of its consolidated financial statements starts on 1 January and ends 
on 31 December.
2.4 ACCOUNTING CURRENCY
The consolidated financial statements are prepared in VND which is also the Company’s accounting currency.
2.5 BASIS OF CONSOLIDATION
The consolidated financial statements comprise the financial statements of the parent company and its subsidiaries for 
the year ended 31 December 2020.
Subsidiaries are fully consolidated from the date of acquisition, being the date on which the Group obtains control, and 
continued to be consolidated until the date that such control ceases.
The financial statements of the subsidiaries are prepared for the same reporting year as the parent company, using consistent 
accounting policies.
All intra-company balances, income and expenses and unrealised gains or losses resulting from intra-company transactions 
are eliminated in full.
Non-controlling interests represent the portion of profit or loss and net assets not held by the Group and are presented 
separately in the consolidated income statement and within equity in the consolidated balance sheet.
Impact of change in the ownership interest of a subsidiary, without a loss of control, is recorded in undistributed earnings.
3. SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES
3.1 CASH AND CASH EQUIVALENTS
Cash and cash equivalents comprise cash on hand, cash at banks and short-term, highly liquid investments with an original 
maturity of less than three months that are readily convertible into known amounts of cash and that are subject to an 
insignificant risk of change in value.		
3.2 INVENTORIES
Inventories are stated at the lower of cost incurred in bringing each product to its present location and condition, and net 
realisable value. Net realisable value represents the estimated selling price in the ordinary course of business less the 
estimated costs to complete and the estimated costs necessary to make the sale.
The perpetual method is used to record inventories, which are valued as follows:
Raw materials and consumables 
-- cost of purchase on a weighted average basis.
Finished goods and work in  
process
-- cost of direct materials and labour plus attributable manufacturing overheads 
based on the normal operating capacity on a weighted average basis.
Provision for obsolete inventories
An inventory provision is created for the estimated loss arising due to the impairment of value (through diminution, damage, 
obsolescence, etc.) of raw materials, finished goods, and other inventories owned by the Group, based on appropriate evidence 
of impairment available at the balance sheet date.
Increases or decreases to the provision balance are recorded into the cost of goods sold account in the consolidated 
income statement.
3.3 RECEIVABLES
Receivables are presented in the consolidated financial statements at the carrying amounts due from customers and other 
debtors, after provision for doubtful debts.
The provision for doubtful debts represents amounts of outstanding receivables at the balance sheet date which are doubtful 
of being recovered. Increases or decreases to the provision balance are recorded as general and administrative expense in the 
consolidated income statement.
3.4 TANGIBLE FIXED ASSETS
Tangible fixed assets are stated at cost less accumulated depreciation.
The cost of a tangible fixed asset comprises its purchase price and any directly attributable costs of bringing the tangible fixed asset 
to working condition for its intended use.
Expenditures for additions, improvements and renewals are added to the carrying amount of the assets and expenditures for 
maintenance and repairs are charged to the consolidated income statement as incurred.
When tangible fixed assets are sold or retired, any gain or loss resulting from their disposal (the difference between the net disposal 
proceeds and the carrying amount) is included in the consolidated income statement.
3.5 INTANGIBLE ASSETS
Intangible assets are stated at cost less accumulated amortisation.
