After a challenging 3-year period due to the Covid pandemic, 2022 marks a remarkable economic recovery 
along with ups and downs in social and environmental life. We are stepping through a trial period with 
contingencies such as pandemics, wars, natural disasters, economic recessions... However, it also 
highlights the consensus on the core values of society, namely safety, health; Integrity and fairness; 
Responsibility for the environment and community…
It can be said that the Covid - Pandemic is a test, a selection process for the community to better 
understand and evaluate the role of sustainable vision in business development. Somewhere along the 
line, we see that challenges seem to make society more resilient, people become stronger and ready 
to change to adapt to any context. With such quick adaptation, I believe that any difficulties will pass to 
move towards a more sustainable future. It can be clearly seen which strong, resilient businesses with 
new sustainable development policies exist and transform "crises" into "opportunities". The world with 
scientific advances, management experience... is gradually adapting, restoring sustainable balance.
At The PAN Group, the core activities in the agricultural and food sector have continued to operate positively 
in 2022 despite being heavily affected by the current context. In order to achieve specific benefits, we are 
addressing each issue, such as sustainable and quality raw material sources; production systems that 
apply advanced, safe, and environmentally friendly technologies; strengthening and developing domestic 
and international markets, and developing human resources with a focus on responsibility, which is 
also an important factor for stable operations. In particular, the governance system has been improved 
to better control and operate more efficiently, aiming for greater benefits for stakeholders. Moreover, 
there are many other plans and actions that the company is implementing to meet the expectations of 
shareholders, customers and partners…
Through those activities, in 2022, The PAN Group completed its revenue and profit plan with the 
corresponding figures of VND 14.1 trillion and VND 794.3 billion, respectively. In addition, PAN also 
implemented many meaningful activities for the company as well as the environment and the community. 
Accordingly, we have established a supply chain of agriculture and aquaculture with 220 agents, 
cooperatives, and traders; 36,381 households of farmers on 31,919 hectares of farming land across 
Vietnam. The PAN Group also directly created jobs for 9,830 workers, with an average monthly income of 
VND 11.88 million, 1.43 times higher than the 2022 Vietnamese average income (8.25 million VND). In the 
past year, The PAN Group did not allow any violation of laws and regulations related to the environment, 
society, and labor; planted an additional 202,000 trees in cooperation programs with reputable partners, 
reduced greenhouse gas emissions intensity from energy consumption by 12.8% compared to 2021, and 
contributed to the community with a value of VND 9.88 billion;
Despite the promising results, The PAN Group will be cautious about the significant challenges in 2023 
and beyond. We believe that the hardest phase of the pandemic is behind us, and the current difficulties 
are temporary on the brink of success. All employees understand the position and potential of The PAN 
Group in the near future, and are determined to realize those potentials and advantages to create value 
for the company, shareholders/investors, employees, and other stakeholders.
Your support - in any form - is highly appreciated and a strong motivation for The PAN Group and 
individuals to fulfill their duties and responsibilities to the best of their abilities.
Once again, we thank you for your support in recent years, which has given The PAN Group more 
opportunities and resources for development in the near future.

and other taxes paid, excluding VAT (which is included in 
payments to suppliers) and employment-related taxes 
(which are included in employee salary and benefits).
	ĕ Payment to capital providers: This covers payments made 
for dividends and interest.
	
ĕ Asset investments: This encompasses cash investments 
made in tangible, intangible, and financial assets, 
excluding business acquisitions and all liquidations.
	
ĕ Community investments: This includes investments 
made in the community and society.

This product has contributed greatly to the effectiveness of 
fungal disease management, increased crop productivity, 
reduced pesticide spraying and costs for farmers.

and development in countries. Transparency in corporate tax practices fosters trust and credibility. For us, tax is a fundamental 
aspect of business transparency, and it is the responsibility of regulators, shareholders, customers, and society at large. We 
firmly believe that tax compliance and tax performance are intertwined, and both are essential for sustainability. Compliance 
with tax regulations ensures the longevity and success of our business.

taxes are paid accurately, timely, and in the appropriate jurisdiction. We maintain an open and transparent relationship with 
tax authorities, and we disclose all relevant facts and circumstances to them for better understanding.

recycling, and treating waste from producers and importers is 
specifically regulated in Articles 54, 55 of the Environmental Protection 
Law; Chapter VI and Appendices 22, 23 of Decree No. 08/2022/NĐ-CP;

ANIMAL WELFARE - THE GLOBAL 
TREND IN FARMING
Increasing demands for animal welfare require changes in the processes of farming, 
harvesting, and processing. Initially, the requirement was to follow the ASC process, then 
gradually tighten the requirements for stocking density, not too intensely, and especially 
to control environmental indicators such as dissolved oxygen, toxic gas, etc. Then, the 
requirement for shrimp harvesting is to make the shrimp die and preserve them in a chilled 
state within 2 minutes after being pulled to the surface, and not to use electric shock to catch 
jumping shrimp in the net. More recently, customers have demanded faster shrimp killing 
for humane reasons. The upcoming trend is to install cameras under the shrimp ponds to 
monitor the activities of the animals.
Currently, the seafood industry of the PAN Group is implementing measures to meet these 
requirements, such as killing shrimp by machine and transporting fish through water troughs 
into the factories.
Transporting fish to the factories using troughs helps 
prevent fish from being knocked around, stressed... and 
contributes to improving animal welfare.
Using an electric shock machine to stun shrimp is in line 
with animal welfare requirements.

Sustainability Performance Index 2022
Accordingly, the revenue and profit achieved the targets set out in the 
Annual General Meeting of Shareholders.
The labor force underwent many changes due to the need to change jobs 
and the residence of the workers but maintained a stable number of 
direct jobs with 9,829 employees, which has been stable for many years. 
This is a significant effort when looking at the context of a sharp decline 
in consumer demand, a period of high unemployment rates, and many 
companies in Vietnam and the world being forced to lay off a large number 
of employees.
The average income of male and female workers in 2022 is VND 13,101,718 
and VND 10,580,148, respectively, much higher than the average income of 
workers in Vietnam in 2022 (reaching VND 6,700,000 according to the General 
Statistics Office of Vietnam). However, the difficult economic situation has 
somewhat affected the income of workers.
Regarding other issues such as commitments to environmental protection, 
resource reduction, greenhouse gas emission reduction, etc., the company 
maintains stable operations and carries out activities that are appropriate 
for green, sustainable, circular economic development trends. Among 
them, the themes of greenhouse gas reduction, renewable energy, low-
carbon production, etc. are of concern and have achieved better results. 
The greenhouse gas emissions from the company's energy use decreased 
by 12.9% compared to 2021. Although it does not fully reflect the situation, 
it is also a positive signal that reflects the effectiveness of improvements 
in fuel use, process optimization, and other objective advantages (reduced 
greenhouse gas emissions from the power grid, merger of VFC subsidiaries 
to increase revenue and reduce emission intensity, etc.). In addition, the 
PAN Group has conducted in-depth research on greenhouse gas reduction 
solutions, organized seminars, and consulted with major businesses in 
Vietnam with the support of VCCI - VBCSD to implement effectively.
Among the important indicators, the workplace accident rate is still an 
issue that the company is not satisfied with as accidents still occur during 
production. Although the accidents are not at a serious level, do not leave 
long-term disabilities and workers return to work soon, it still shows that 
there are safety risks.
Finally, in 2022, the PAN Group fulfilled its responsibility to the environment 
and the community, not allowing any environmental or social incidents to 
occur in the past year, and continued to contribute to the supply chain and 
community in terms of income, employment, support, sponsorship, and 
planting more trees for the environment with a total of 202,000 trees. These 
are positive signals for future efforts to improve Environmental - Social - 
Governance issues.

ENVIRONMENT
With 
Vietnam's 
strong 
commitments 
to 
the 
environment, and the growing awareness of the 
negative environmental impact in recent years, The 
PAN Group places great emphasis on controlling 
environmental issues and has set out a roadmap for 
improvement to contribute to the overall trend of 
Vietnam and the world.
Accordingly, the Group has begun researching 
greenhouse gas issues and will soon implement an 
inventory, evaluate the situation and plan for future 
reduction.
Along with greenhouse gasses, the Group will also 
develop a monitoring system and action plan for 
other environmental indicators such as wastewater, 
solid waste, energy consumption, and contribute to 
positive environmental improvement actions such as 
tree planting (the Life from Forestry project) and the 
application of environmentally friendly agricultural 
production techniques.
SOCIETY
With a commitment to sharing value, The PAN Group 
is currently implementing the "For a Happy Working 
Community" project to help employees have a 
better material and spiritual life. Gender equality is 
an important issue in the labor force and is aimed 
towards creating a comprehensively just society.
For the community outside the company, students 
are a group that The PAN Group is interested in, as 
they will be the future labor force responsible for 
economic development and social stability. Therefore, 
the sponsorship program for students in related fields 
was launched in 2022 and will be implemented in the 
next phase, aiming to create high-quality human 
resources for the agriculture and food industry. 
The PAN Group also commits to sharing values 
with the supply chain, especially farmers who are 
directly impacted by the Group's activities through 
cooperation, training, and financial support…
Even in emergency situations such as natural 
disasters, pandemics, and difficult circumstances, 
The PAN Group maintains support programs as in 
previous years to solve urgent problems, quickly 
stabilize and recover.
GOVERNANCE
With the strong trend of ESG practices nowadays, 
The PAN Group constantly improves its management 
system. This is the foundation for decision-
making, system operation, improving operational 
efficiency, building trust, and maximizing benefits 
for stakeholders. The improvements will range from 
structure to policies, procedures and specific actions. 
Good management is also a means to prevent issues 
such as lack of transparency, corruption, fraud, and 
injustice... and build trust with shareholders/investors.
The PAN Group aims to create momentum for 
development from innovative activities, through 
support and 
encouragement of 
research and 
development. The PAN Group Innovation Award is 
expected to encourage employees to participate, not 
only bringing economic benefits but also improving 
environmental, social and governance factors.

THE CHAIRMAN’S MESSAGE
Dear Valued Shareholders,
The global economy faced numerous challenges in 2023. The 
ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict, coupled with new conflicts 
erupting in the Middle East and the Red Sea towards the end of 
the year, significantly impacted the global landscape. Extreme 
weather events, such as El Nino-induced droughts, disrupted 
food production and consumption, leading to imbalances. The 
global commodities market experienced substantial volatility, 
with inflation remaining high, weak trade growth, and slow 
consumer confidence recovery. In response, many countries 
maintained tight monetary policies to curb inflation. These 
factors, along with weak demand and sluggish economic growth, 
and protectionist trade policies in major markets like the United 
States, Japan, and the EU, exerted considerable pressure on 
exporting countries.
Vietnam embarked on its 2023 plan facing both opportunities and 
challenges. Apart from addressing the negative impacts of the 
international context, our country had to resolve long standing 
issues while promoting growth, ensuring macroeconomic 
stability, and alleviating difficulties for businesses. The GDP 
growth for 2023 reached 5.05%, with an increasing trend each 
quarter. The total import-export turnover was USD 683 billion, a 
6.6% decrease from the previous year.
In this setting, the agriculture sector grew by 3.83%, at its 
highest rate in recent years, considerably contributing to overall 
economic growth. The total export value of agriculture, forestry, 
and fishery products remained high at over USD 53 billion, with a 
trade surplus of USD 12.07 billion, a record high. Agriculture has 
maintained its vital role as a solid foundation for food security 
and macroeconomic stability.
In 2023, PAN Group’s core businesses struggled in the first half 
of the year but improved dramatically by year-end. Consolidated 
revenue reached VND 13.2 trillion, a slight decrease of 3.3% 
compared to the previous year, owing mostly to declines in the 
aquaculture and packaged food sectors, which were offset by 
growth in agriculture with higher profit margins. As a result, net 
profit attributable to parent company shareholders increased by 
9% compared to 2022.
Despite a challenging year, the Group adapted flexibly to 
maintain stable business operations while creating new 
future opportunities. Notably, a cooperation agreement with 
Standard Chartered Bank Vietnam was signed during the 
COP28 conference, allowing PAN to access ESG-based financial 
solutions and services to meet infrastructure investment needs.
Furthermore, the Group had made strategic initiatives to align 
with the government’s project for sustainable development 
of one million hectares of high-quality, low-emission rice 
cultivation linked to green growth in the Mekong Delta by 
2030. Specifically, with a relatively complete ecosystem in the 
rice sector, the Group signed a cooperation agreement with 
the People’s Committee of Dong Thap province and other 
business partners to implement the project, aiming to increase 
productivity, improve product quality, reduce emissions, and 
enhance farmers’ incomes.
Internal collaboration among member companies was also 
strengthened to optimize resources and increase synergistic 
value through cooperation in finance, production, business, and 
trade. Examples include the collaboration between Vinaseed 
and Khang An Foods in supplying vegetables for frozen products 
mixed with shrimp; Vinaseed and VFC in developing the rice 
value chain in the Mekong Delta, and Lafooco and SHIN Coffee 
in cross-selling and distribution.
Dear Valued Shareholders,
2024 is anticipated to be another challenging year for business 
operations, with unpredictable volatility in exchange rates and 
interest rates. Inflation and interest rates in Vietnam’s main 
export markets, such as the United States and the EU remain 
high, hindering strong recovery in consumer demand and 
orders. The domestic market is also just entering a recovery 
phase after two difficult years. Therefore, the business plan 
for 2024 of each member company and Group consolidation 
is developed with a certain level of prudence. In an optimistic 
scenario, we can expect substantial recovery in both export and 
domestic markets in the second half of the year, resulting in 
high growth for PAN’s business sectors.
Finally, on behalf of the leadership, I would like to extend my 
gratitude and appreciation to our esteemed shareholders, 
customers, partners, and all employees of the Group for your 
unwavering support and dedication to PAN on our journey to 
elevate Vietnamese agriculture and food.
Best wishes for your good health, happiness, and success!
Despite a challenging year, 
the Group adapted flexibly 
to maintain stable business 
operations while creating 
new future opportunities.
The Chairman
Nguyen Duy Hung

A policy reversal by the US Federal Reserve (FED) and the European Central Bank (ECB) could occur around 
mid-2024, while developing markets are expected to start an easing cycle earlier. In this context, Vietnam is

of economic and geopolitical risks. In addition, the impact of monetary tightening and declining aggregate demand, along with the 
sluggishness of business activities in major economies, has caused the early-year recovery phase to turn into a slowdown, even a 
decline towards the end of the year. Evidence of this is the sharp increase in corporate bankruptcies in major economies compared to 
the same period last year, with the US up 30%, the EU up 13%, and even exceeding the pre-2008-2009 crisis level in Northern Europe...

banks had stopped raising benchmark interest rates

trend was not yet fully clear. The policy reversals of 
the FED and ECB could occur around mid-2024, while 
developing markets will start an easing cycle earlier.

trend since the beginning of Q4/2023. Exchange rate 
pressure on developing and emerging economies 
will ease as the USD will be less “green” as the FED 
and ECB cut benchmark rates.
In the context of economies becoming increasingly 
sensitive and affected by conflicts between alliances 
or economic, political and military blocs, in 2024, the

elections in about 50 countries (from superpowers

I. Agriculture sector
In agriculture business, the Group has to confront many industry-specific risks, typically as follows:
Market risks and competition pressure
As for the seed segment, the risk of the consumption 
market occurs when the Group loses its available 
markets or cannot penetrate the target market due to 
the impact of external factors or the low competitive 
products or the company’s policies. Vietnam’s seed 
industry has small scale and fragmented production, 
each province has its own seeds, there are no truly 
dominant varieties, as a result, agricultural products 
have uneven quality, low competitiveness and low prices.
For the agrochemicals segment, the competition 
pressure risks reflect in the sales promotion programs 
and marketing activities in the market. Over the past few 
years, the agricultural agrochemicals market has been 
scandalized with increasingly sophisticated fake and/or 
counterfeit goods.
Weather risks
This risk directly threatens the production activities as 
well as the cultivation of farmers, thereby influencing 
the quality and consumption output. The Group’s main 
agricultural production regions are the Mekong Delta, 
the Central Highlands and the Central region, where 
the climate is increasingly harsh with frequent storms, 
droughts and severe saltwater intrusion.
Solutions to minimize the risks:
The Group has continuously conducted surveys to 
assess market demand, focused on research and 
technology transfers that allow it to produce high 
quality and short-day seed varieties with high yields 
and strong disease resistance, which are well received 
and highly appreciated by the markets. Free technical 
training courses are also provided to farmers to improve 
production efficiency. In addition, the Group regularly 
gathers market information, researches and develops 
flexible sales policies for cost optimization.
Agricultural land viability risks
Vietnam’s agricultural land is highly fragmented due 
to the nature of the terrain, population density, land 
allocations, culture, history and institutional policies. 
The area available for cultivation shrinks gradually 
every year owing to urbanization and industrialization. 
These factors directly cause consequences for the seed 
business and agricultural product manufacturing.
Solutions to minimize the risks:
The PAN Group has cooperated with local authorities 
to actively restructure planting areas and encourage 
the use of high-quality plant varieties meant to improve 
farmers’ income, support their product consumption 
through The Group’s rice value chain.
Solutions to minimize the risks:
The PAN Group has expanded its production areas into 
different ecological regions, and at the same time, 
invested in building warehouses to preserve goods to 
ensure adequate supply in case of natural disasters. The 
Group also researches and develops products that are 
well adapted to different ecological regions, diversifying 
production areas to the North for risk prevention.

The PAN Group’s seafood business has established its position and high competitiveness in the international market as 
one of the leading corporations in Vietnam. However, it still faces these following typical risks:
Input material risks
Shrimp is exposed to supply risk through unpredictable 
changes in input materials price and quality. The risk

2023 had the largest agricultural value-added growth 
in the last decade. The agriculture, forestry, and 
aquaculture trade surplus hit a new high of USD 12.07 
billion, accounting for more than 42.5% of the total 
trade surplus. The agricultural value-added increased 
by 3.88% over the previous year, accounting for 0.34 
percentage points of overall value-added growth in 
the economy. This reinforces its critical function as an 
economic component, guaranteeing food security and 
promoting macroeconomic stability.
Favorable weather circumstances, strategic crop 
variety conversion, and improved farming techniques 
in localities resulted in reasonably high grain 
production. The grain crop output was 47.9 million 
tons, an increase of 0.8 million tons over the previous 
year. Rice production reached 43.5 million tons, 
representing a 795 thousand ton gain due to increased 
rice yields in most seasons. Emphasizing overall grain 
and rice production growth over the previous year 
fulfilled domestic consumption demand, ensured 
food security, supported processing and export 
activities, and brought several benefits to the Group’s 
agrochemicals business.
The International Rice Festival, the Vietnam Craft 
Village Conservation and Development Festival, 
and the ASEAN Ministerial Meeting on Disaster 
Management were among the significant national and 
international events successfully organized in 2023. 
These events helped to promote the image and brand 
of agricultural, forestry, and fishery products on a 
national, regional, and worldwide scale, consequently 
increasing agricultural product consumption. Notably, 
the implementation of the Project on Sustainable 
Development of 1 million hectares of high-quality, 
low-emission rice cultivation for green growth in the 
Mekong Delta by 2030 has begun.
In 2023, the worldwide rice price index rose 21% year 
on year. Rice prices in key producers like Thailand and 
Vietnam have risen by 35-45%, hitting their highest 
level in 15 years. This was primarily owing to fears 
about the influence of El Nino on rice production, 
which prompted numerous countries to raise their 
stockpiles and imposed export restrictions by India. 
Vietnam’s rice export price in 2023 increased by 18.3% 
from 2022, averaging USD 575/ton. Surprisingly, there 
were occasions when Vietnam’s rice export price was 
the highest in the world, exceeding Thailand and India. 
Domestic rice prices rose by 40-53% in 2023, outpacing 
export price increases, resulting in a bumper harvest 
and good prices for rice farmers.
Despite rising input costs and expenses in 2023, Vinaseed’s crop 
seed and rice business division maintained its company size and 
market share in comparison to the same period the previous year. 
Vinaseed also brought economically high-value hybrid rice types to 
high-quality shrimp-rice farming areas, creating potential markets 
for 1,000 tons of hybrid rice per crop. The company’s agricultural 
segment saw tremendous development, with a gross profit margin 
rising from 9.7% to 15.2%. It also expanded its rice export markets 
to new countries, including Canada and Mozambique, and began 
exporting to Costco Canada.
The seed and agricultural product portfolios continued to be key, 
accounting for 70% and 23% of revenue, respectively, including high-
value hybrid rice seeds, waxy corn seeds, and packaged rice products.

In 2023, total aquaculture production 
exceeded estimates, reaching 9.269 
million tons. This contained 3.861

5.408 million tons from aquaculture, a

around 1.9 billion USD, mollusks about 
0.8 billion USD, and tuna around 0.9

in 2023 was predicted to be 1.3 million

cubic meters of marine cage farming.
After a steady fall since the beginning 
of the year, shrimp exports increased 
significantly from July to the end of the 
year, hitting 682 million USD, down 
15% from 2022. US shrimp import data 
in November 2023 also showed a sixth 
consecutive month of rise. Declining 
inventory 
and 
steadily 
improving

spurred the spike in demand during the 
year-end period. Inflation in the United 
States fell sharply in 2023, hitting 3.1%

Japanese market fell steadily in 2023 as

depreciation of the JPY, influencing 
Japanese 
importers’ 
purchasing 
decisions. In 2023, shrimp exports to this 
market totaled USD 511 million, a 24% 
decline from 2022. However, the last 
month of 2023 saw a 6% gain over the 
same period in 2022.

PERSONNEL STRUCTURE
As of the end of 2023, the total number of employees in the 
Group was 10,321, representing a 5% increase compared to 
2022. The workforce in the agricultural sector and food sector 
accounted for 21.9% and 77.9% respectively. The common 
age range of employees is between 30 and 50, constituting 
61% of the total workforce. The group under 30 years old 
accounts for 34%, while those over 50 years old account for 
5%. The majority of the workforce are ordinary laborers, 
suitable for the characteristics of the industry. Gender 
balance is maintained with 5,150 females and 5,171 males.
RECRUITMENT AND TALENT ACQUISITION
TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT
A strong and culturally aligned workforce is the foundation for 
an organization's development. Recruitment is a crucial action to 
provide human resources for production and business activities, 
goals, and development strategies of the enterprise.
In 2023, recruitment remained a strategic priority for the 
Group, with prudent investments made to secure a high-caliber 
workforce. The recruitment process focused on attracting 
talent, targeting individuals with extensive experience and top-
notch professional qualifications, as well as enticing promising 
young talent and identifying highly skilled workers. Each position 
and job title had its set criteria and standards with detailed job 
descriptions. Recruitment activities are conducted systematically, 
with announcements made publicly and selections carried out 
transparently. Objective assessments were employed to choose 
candidates who aligned with the corporate culture, thereby 
ensuring the effectiveness of recruitment endeavors across the 
Group and its member companies. These efforts significantly 
bolstered the employer brand and reinforced the foundation for 
organizational development.
The Group and its member companies place a strong emphasis 
on systematically designing and implementing training programs 
aimed at enhancing labor productivity and efficiency, as well 
as maintaining and elevating the quality of human resources. 
These initiatives are integral to creating a competitive edge for 
the enterprise, preventing outdated management practices, and 
nurturing a cadre of skilled managers and professionals.
As an investment in the organization's human capital, training 
programs at PAN not only impart knowledge, skills, and expertise 
to meet job requirements but also facilitate employees' personal 
development and instill positive values.
Practical training activities conducted throughout the year include:
- Orientation training: Introducing company regulations and 
government policies to familiarize new employees with their 
rights and responsibilities at work.
- Mandatory training as required by law: Provide training in the 
operation of equipment with strict safety requirements (boiler, 
forklift...); Fire prevention training and drills; Occupational safety 
and health training; Food safety knowledge training (for food 
production companies);
- Technical training for employees, contractors, cooperative 
farmers... who directly create products, and require regular 
training and retraining to ensure up-to-date skills and knowledge 
for the job.
- Practical training on quality standards, food safety, 
environmental and social standards: BRC, ISO22000, FSSC, 
HACCP, GAP, ASC, BSCI, SEDEX, etc.
- Soft skills training, self-leadership thinking, team leading.
Elevating the quality of the management team is always a top 
priority of PAN and its member units to meet development needs. 
During the year, the Group continued to implement courses for 
the core team, senior management and focused on advanced 
training to develop management capacity and standardize the 
middle management team. These efforts align with the overall 
goal of sustainable human resource development, effectively 
supporting the business strategy.

COMPENSATION AND REWARDS POLICY
PROMOTION POLICY
WELFARE AND BENEFITS POLICY
The compensation policy serves as an effective lever to stabilize the 
workforce, as well as attract, and retain talent. The compensation and 
reward policy of PAN has three tiers, Fair – Appropriate – Competitive, 
ensuring that employees are motivated to fulfill their duties effectively. 
The salary policy is strictly designed with a system of salary scales, 
payroll, and allowances associated with job positions, qualifications, 
capabilities and responsibilities of employees; consistent with the 
operational structure and division of labor. The form and method of 
salary payment are specifically and clearly defined and clear in the 
Salary Regulations.
The Group and its subsidiaries employ a diverse reward policy to 
recognize the efforts and contributions of individuals and groups, 
regardless of the scale of their achievements. Employees receive 
bonuses based on labor productivity and work efficiency, with 
various bonus packages available. These packages include rewards 
for dedicated individuals, promising employees, top-performing 
employees and groups, extraordinary bonuses for individuals with 
outstanding achievements, bonuses linked to business targets, Tet 
bonuses, 13th-month salaries, and year-end bonuses.
The full implementation of compensation and reward policy has 
encouraged employees to dedicate themselves and strive for a strong 
and sustainable PAN.
The internal promotion and career development 
strategy is the core components of PAN’s 
human resource planning and development 
policy, aimed at providing employees with a 
comprehensive outlook and on their future 
career path while fulfilling the organization’s 
short-term and long-term human resource 
requirements.
Equal career advancement opportunities are 
achieved through a specific human resource 
utilization plan and career path for each 
position. 
This 
roadmap 
empowers 
each 
employee to gauge their position within their 
career trajectory and identify knowledge and 
skills required for advancement. The practice 
of internal promotion policy shows recorded 
specific results in reducing the duration 
of human resource shortage, motivating 
employees and curbing the job turnover rate.
The PAN Group prioritizes developing internal 
human resources through job rotation, ensuring 
the right person for the right job, creating 
conditions for individuals to fully bring into their 
strength to maximize their contributions.
Annual human resource planning and staffing 
endeavors are undertaken to ensure the stability, 
continuity, and progression of the organization's 
workforce. The talent development program is 
implemented by focusing on the recruitment 
of young, talented individuals and providing 
training to align with PAN's accelerated human 
resource development plan.
Good welfare policy serves as the cornerstone for affirming the enterprises 
‘ position in the labor market. The Group always associates revenue growth 
with enhancement of working conditions for all members, addressing both 
tangible and intangible factors to boost human resources self-development. 
This approach lies in the heart of PAN’s  human resource strategy, an 
important link in the comprehensive value quantification chain that benefits 
employees, in addition to the brand values, opportunities for career and 
personal development, accumulated knowledge value and competitive 
compensation and rewards system.
To recognize employees' efforts and contributions, the Group implements 
various welfare and benefit schemes that are regularly adjusted to increase 
employee commitment. These schemes include comprehensive employee 
healthcare programs offering periodic health check-ups, disease risk 
screening, and supplementary health insurance tailored to different ranks. 
Additionally, PAN provides support packages for sick visits, condolences, 
allowances for individuals facing difficulties, as well as gifts on holidays and 
special occasions, and personalized birthday packages. Annual team-building 
programs, vacations, and activities for employees' children are organized to 
foster stronger connections among members. These welfare policies reflect 
the Group's commitment to caring for the material and spiritual well-being of 
its employees, strengthening their loyalty, cohesion, and satisfaction.
Recognizing that people are the most valuable assets in any organization, 
PAN values each individual's contribution to collective success, regardless of 
their position. The Group creates a dynamic, fair, professional, and friendly 
working environment where each employee has the opportunity to achieve 
career success and personal fulfillment. Employees are provided with fully-
equipped facilities, online working platforms, and digital transformation 
infrastructure in line with industry 4.0 standards. Investing in multi-channel 
working solutions has not only created a competitive advantage but also 
ensured work continuity and efficiency.
The PAN Group offers a diverse range of solutions tailored to support 
individuals in developing and advancing their careers within the organization 
while contributing to society and the environment. These solutions are 
developed in close relations with the organization’s vision and culture.

OVERVIEW
The PAN Group's consolidated revenue in 2023 was VND 
13.2 trillion, a 3% reduction from 2022, and represented 
roughly 90% of the 2023 revenue plan. This reduction was 
mostly caused by import and export market variations in

However, revenue increase in the agricultural sector (+9%), 
particularly in the agricultural chemicals, seeds, and 
packaged rice segments, which was driven by higher rice 
prices and strong market demand, somewhat offset the 
decrease.
The Group's strategic orientation for the 2020-2025 period 
is to focus on developing core production capacity in each 
business segment, building on the existing foundation, while 
seizing any available market opportunity for the acquisition 
of good companies that align with the business lines and 
development strategy.
The Group and its member companies’ investment and M&A 
strategy focuses on ongoing initiatives to improve internal 
production capacity, as well as M&A to raise ownership 
ratios in existing subsidiaries.
In 2022, the Group had already successfully completed the 
initial infrastructure investments in important projects. 
These included the construction of two new factories, the 
extension of farming areas at FMC, the opening of a new 
fish sauce factory in Dien Phu, and investments in further 
farming grounds and machinery at ABT. The total investment 
for these projects was around VND 1,500 billion.
In 2023, amidst difficult macroeconomic hurdles such as 
shifting interest rates, geopolitical tensions, and economic 
crises, the Group took a careful approach to expanding M&A 
investments and launching new projects, guaranteeing 
financial stability.

2. Business results in 2023 compared to 2022
In 2023, the net profit to the parent company's shareholders reached VND 406 billion, a growth of nearly 9% compared to 2022, 
including an extraordinary gain from the sale of a factory. Excluding this, core business profit in 2023 saw a remarkable growth of 
approximately 23% over the same period.
The agriculture sector, particularly the agrochemical industry, 
enjoyed strong growth in 2023, with sales and profit increasing 
by 10% and more than 30%, respectively. Record-high rice 
and durian export prices encouraged farmers to invest more 
in production, increasing demand for agrochemicals. The 
company's superior distribution management ensured timely 
delivery of goods, resulting in higher profit margins. The 
packaged rice sector also made for a significant portion of 
overall profit by taking advantage of high rice prices to increase 
profits. As a result, the rice segment's gross profit margin 
increased from about 9% to more than 15% by 2023.
Despite a 10% decrease in revenue, the aquaculture sector's 
profit remained nearly similar compared to the same time, 
as the company concentrated on deep-processed items with 
high added value and primarily exported to Japan, protecting 
profit margins. Shrimp farming was also successful, with 
good disease prevention, adequate shrimp harvests, and lower 
input costs. This strong performance contrasts with the overall 
downturn in the aquaculture business in 2023, when shrimp 
exports decreased by 21% and pangasius exports by 25%.
In the packaged goods segment, both Bibica (confectionery) and 
Lafoco (cashew nuts) saw small revenue losses (-7% and -15%, 
respectively), but nevertheless managed to increase profits. 
The cashew nut's net profit climbed by 11%, owing mostly to 
the company's good inventory management for manufacturing, 
combined with a large drop in interest payments in 2023 
compared to 2022. Meanwhile, Bibica's core business profit 
increased by 53%, driven by the successful market introduction 
of new high-margin items. In terms of production, Bibica was 
continually making adjustments to increase efficiency and 
actively monitoring raw material prices in order to negotiate 
with suppliers for cost savings. The increased export activity 
was a bright area for confectionery in 2023, with numerous new 
markets to explore in the following years.

ASSESSMENT BY THE BOARD OF

OPERATIONAL ASPECTS
In 2023, the global economy faced significant obstacles, with 
most economies reporting slower-than-expected growth due to 
decreased aggregate demand. While inflation has eased, it remains 
high. Tightening monetary policies, record-high global public debt, 
the intensifying military conflict between Russia and Ukraine, 
increased geopolitical instability, food hunger, natural disasters, 
and climate change all present substantial problems. By the end 
of 2023, international organizations' worldwide economic growth 
expectations had been revised from previous estimates, with the 
majority forecasting slower growth than in 2022.
Vietnam's economy expanded by only 5.05% in 2023, falling short 
of the National Assembly's 6.5% forecast. Nonetheless, this 
performance demonstrates the economy's ongoing recovery, 
since growth rose in successive quarters (Q1: 3.41%; Q2: 4.25%; 
Q3: 5.47%; Q4: 6.72%). Agriculture, forestry, and fisheries 
expanded by 3.83%, contributing 0.46 percentage points to 
overall GDP growth.
In line with the gradual economic recovery, PAN’s core business 
segments also experienced notable growth, particularly in the 
latter part of the year. Consolidated revenue reached VND 13.2 
trillion, a slight decrease of 3.3% compared to the previous year, 
fulfilling approximately 87% of the revenue plan. The shortfall 
in revenue was primarily attributed to the seafood (-11%) and 
packaged food (-8%) segments, which were offset by growth in 
the agriculture segment (+9%).
The PAN Group's business structure underwent a transformation 
in 2023, favoring high-margin segments. The agriculture 
segment accounted for a larger share, increasing from 36% 
to 40% of revenue and contributing 76% to net profit after tax 
(NPAT). The aquaculture segment's share declined from 46% 
to 43% of revenue and contributed 45% to NPAT, while the 
food segment accounted for approximately 17% of revenue but 
experienced a significant decline in NPAT from 31% to 18% for 
the entire group.

HIGHLIGHTS OF 2023
COOPERATION WITH DONG THAP PROVINCIAL PEOPLE'S COMMITTEE  
TO BUILD AND IMPLEMENT THE PROJECT "IMPROVING RICE FARMERS' INCOME".
Contributing to resolving the bottlenecks of the agriculture 
sector, PAN has partnered with Dong Thap province to build 
and implement the project "Improving Rice Farmers' Income", 
thereby providing sustainable solutions to build a closed value 
chain in the rice sector. Specifically, the project will support the 
improvement of rice cultivation techniques, promote the use of 
licensed varieties, strive to reduce the use of chemical fertilizers 
and pesticides in rice production, strengthen consumption 
linkages, and build product brands for rice farmers in Dong 
Thap province. The project is closely linked to the Government-
level project "Sustainable Development of 1 Million Hectares 
of High-Quality, Low-Emission Rice Cultivation Associated with 
Green Growth in the Mekong Delta Region by 2030". Accordingly, 
the project aims to increase the income of rice farmers in Dong 
Thap province by 2025, with a focus on 2030.
This was PAN's first participation in an international 
exhibition at the Group level, helping to reposition 
Vietnam's agricultural and food brands in the 
global marketplace. The Group built a large booth 
representing Vietnam's agriculture and food business, 
which became a focal point for the entire Vietnamese 
exhibit area. During the three-day fair, members of 
the PAN Group received hundreds of foreign partners.

The plan was developed based on the careful assessment and judgment of 
the Board of Directors (BOD) and the Board of Management. Accordingly, 
2024 is still assessed to be a challenging year for production and business 
activities when macroeconomic conditions such as exchange rates, interest 
rates, and credit continue to fluctuate unpredictably, and have an adverse 
impact on the expansion of production and business activities. Inflation 
and interest rates in Vietnam's main export markets such as the US and 
EU remain high, and as a result, consumer demand and orders from these 
markets are not yet clearly recovering. Meanwhile, the domestic market 
is also just entering a recovery phase after two years of difficulties in 
2022 and 2023. Therefore, the business plan of each company as well as 
the consolidated plan for 2024 is built with a certain degree of caution: 
consolidated revenue and consolidated profit will grow by 12% and 10%, 
respectively. In a more positive scenario, we expect both the export market 
and the domestic market to recover strongly in the second half of 2024, 
and may bring higher-than-expected growth to PAN's business segments.
The agriculture segment with its crop seeds, rice, and plant protection 
and fumigation business, is expected to continue to achieve good revenue 
growth, but profits may increase at a slower rate due to the impact of 
fluctuating input prices, purchase prices, and the high exchange rate, 
which are adversely affecting business efficiency. In addition, the El Nino 
phenomenon will continue to affect crop seasons, fruit trees, and indirectly 
negatively impact the consumption of plant protection products. The 
packaged rice business is likely to continue to be positive as rice prices 
are at a high level, somewhat offsetting the risks and difficulties in the crop 
seeds and pesticides business.
In the packaged food segment, the confectionery segment is expected to 
continue to grow well in its core business, following the recovery from the 
end of 2023; along with new growth drivers from stronger exploitation of 
the export market. However, the high level of some key raw materials such 
as sugar and flour will reduce overall efficiency.
In the meantime, the nuts and snacks generally has a good growth plan 
as sales to customers in China and Hong Kong recover, and the strong 
exploitation of the Japanese market (which began two years ago) will also 
be an important driver in the next five years of this business.
ĕ Confectionery: Revenue is expected to grow by 15%; while pre-tax profit 
from core operations is expected to grow at a single-digit rate, with the 
estimated increase in input raw material prices higher than in 2023.
ĕ Nuts and snacks: Revenue and profit will grow well by 10% - 15%, as 
2024 is expected to fully restore sales to traditional customers as well as 
exploit the Japanese market.
Meanwhile, the aquaculture segment will not see a rapid recovery, at 
least in the first half of the year, as major consumer markets such as 
the US and EU still have high inflation and orders have not recovered as 
strongly as expected. In addition, developments in the US anti-dumping 
and anti-subsidy case against the shrimp industry could also have adverse 
effects and create price competition pressure from other shrimp exporting 
countries. After the first half of the year, consumption is expected to 
recover more quickly in positive macroeconomic scenarios.
ĕ Shrimp business: revenue is planned to grow by a single digit compared 
to 2023, but pre-tax profit is expected to grow higher, from 12% - 15%; due 
to the expectation of higher profit margins when exploiting the entire area 
of self-raised ponds and the cooling down of transportation and feed costs.
ĕ Pangasius business: strongly affected by the export market context and 
the export price level has not improved much - revenue and profit are 
expected to grow slightly by a single digit.

EVALUATION OF CORPORATE GOVERNANCE STANDARD 
IMPLEMENTATION (CG CODE/CG ASEAN AND OTHER STANDARD)
The Board of Directors (BOD) of the Group identifies the enhancement of corporate governance quality and capacity as a key element 
in its strategic direction to build a robust governance system based on the application of international practices, in conjunction 
with the overall strength of resources across the system to control and supervise the company’s operations in a responsible, 
transparent, and effective manner.
In 2023, The Group strictly implemented the regulations on information disclosure in Circular 96/2020/TT-BTC, regulations of the Ho 
Chi Minh City Stock Exchange and the State Securities Commission. Information related to corporate governance, business activities, 
and unusual information was disclosed within the prescribed time limit, ensuring transparency with all shareholders and investors.
COMPLIANCE OF REGULATIONS ON INFORMATION DISCLOSURE AND TRANSPARENCY
The Group recognized and respected the rights of shareholders, 
the owners of the Company, including minority shareholders 
and foreign shareholders by ensuring equal and appropriate 
treatment for each shareholder through disclosure of accurate, 
transparent and timely information. The Group paid attention 
to the adequacy of information disclosure so that shareholders 
could make decisions under provided information at the AGM, 
including voting and expressing opinions on significant changes 
and electing members of the BOD. Shareholders’ rights were 
also clearly defined in the Group’s Charter and protected by the 
Vietnamese laws.
The AGM is annually organized, of which attached documents 
with full information are priorly sent to all shareholders. 
The company also posts AGM information on the websites of 
HOSE and The PAN Group for the shareholders’ references. 
The AGM agenda closely followed the content informed in the 
relevant invitation letter. In 2023, the Company successfully 
held its Annual General Meeting of Shareholders (AGM) at the 
Ho Chi Minh City Stock Exchange, after three years of holding 
it semi-online due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The Chairman 
and the BOM and representatives from subsidiaries jointly 
answered questions and provided information upon request of 
shareholders. Minutes of the AGM were recorded accurately, 
fully and timely in accordance with the laws and published 
together with the Resolution of the AGM for HOSE, SSC on 
PAN’s website within 24 hours after the meeting.
The PAN Group also aims to publish Vietnamese-English 
information so that foreign investors can easily access 
information. Important internal management documents of the 
Group such as the Charter, Internal Governance Regulations are 
translated and posted on the PAN’s website in both English and 
Vietnamese. Programs and documents for the AGM, Minutes 
and Resolutions of the Meeting are all published in Vietnamese 
and English. This is an important step towards international 
governance practices in ensuring shareholder rights and equal 
treatment among shareholders, especially foreign shareholders 
and investors.
In 2023, the Group sent two executives to participate in a training 
course for members of the Board of Directors (DCP). In addition, 
the Group also assigned personnel to research the latest corporate 
governance practices according to the ASEAN Scorecard 2023 
(ACGS) to identify new points and gaps that the company needs to 
master and develop an implementation roadmap.
EQUAL TREATMENT TO SHAREHOLDERS
In 2023, the BOD of The PAN Group had 2/7 independent members, satisfying the provisions of Decree 155/2020/ND-CP. The 
independent Board members at The PAN Group have the ability to promote the independent judgment of all BOD members 
and the integrity of the governance system. In addition, 02 independent members of the BOD are members of the Internal Audit 
Subcommittee under the BOD of which 01 member is the Head of the Subcommittee.

2. BASIS OF PREPARATION 
The consolidated financial statements of the Group, expressed in Vietnam dong (“VND”), are 
prepared in accordance with Vietnamese Enterprise Accounting System and Vietnamese 
Accounting Standards issued by the Ministry of Finance as per:
•	
Decision No. 149/2001/QD-BTC dated 31 December 2001 on the Issuance and Promulgation 
of Four Vietnamese Accounting Standards (Series 1);
•	
Decision No. 165/2002/QD-BTC dated 31 December 2002 on the Issuance and Promulgation 
of Six Vietnamese Accounting Standards (Series 2);
•	
Decision No. 234/2003/QD-BTC dated 30 December 2003 on the Issuance and Promulgation 
of Six Vietnamese Accounting Standards (Series 3);
•	
Decision No. 12/2005/QD-BTC dated 15 February 2005 on the Issuance and Promulgation of 
Six Vietnamese Accounting Standards (Series 4); and
•	
Decision No. 100/2005/QD-BTC dated 28 December 2005 on the Issuance and Promulgation 
of Four Vietnamese Accounting Standards (Series 5).
Accordingly, the accompanying consolidated financial statements, including their utilisation are 
not designed for those who are not informed about Vietnam’s accounting principles, procedures 
and practices and furthermore are not intended to present the financial position and results 
of operations and cash flows in accordance with accounting principles and practices generally 
accepted in countries other than Vietnam.
2.1 Accounting 
standards and 
system
The Group’s applied accounting documentation system is the General Journal system.
2.2 Applied accounting 
documentation system
The Group’s fiscal year applicable for the preparation of its consolidated financial statements 
starts on 1 January and ends on 31 December.
2.3 Fiscal year 
The consolidated financial statements are prepared in VND which is also the Company’s 
accounting currency.
2.4 Accounting 
currency 
The consolidated financial statements comprise the financial statements of the Company and its 
subsidiaries for year ended 31 December 2023.
Subsidiaries are fully consolidated from the date of acquisition incorporation, being the date on 
which the Group obtains control, and continued to be consolidated until the date that such control 
ceases.
The financial statements of the subsidiaries are prepared for the same reporting year as the 
parent company, using consistent accounting policies.
All intra-company balances, income and expenses and unrealised gains or losses result from 
intra-company transactions are eliminated in full.
Non-controlling interests represent the portion of profit or loss and net assets not held by the 
Group and are presented separately in the consolidated income statement and within equity in the 
consolidated balance sheet.
Impact of change in the ownership interest of a subsidiary, without a loss of control, is recorded 
in undistributed earnings.

3. SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES 
Cash and cash equivalents comprise cash on hand, cash at banks and short-term, highly liquid 
investments with an original maturity of no more than three months that are readily convertible 
into known amounts of cash and that are subject to an insignificant risk of change in value.
3.1 Cash and cash 
equivalents
Receivables are presented in the consolidated financial statements at the carrying amounts due 
from customers and other debtors, after provision for doubtful debts.
The provision for doubtful debts represents amounts of outstanding receivables at the 
consolidated balance sheet date which are doubtful of being recovered. Increases or decreases 
to the provision balance are recorded as general and administrative expenses in the consolidated 
income statement. When bad debts are determined as unrecoverable and accountant writes off 
those bad debts, the differences between the provision for doubtful receivables previously made 
and historical cost of receivables are included in the consolidated income statement.
3.3 Receivables
Tangible fixed assets are stated at cost less accumulated depreciation.
The cost of a tangible fixed asset comprises its purchase price and any directly attributable costs 
of bringing the tangible fixed asset to working condition for its intended use.
Expenditures for additions, improvements and renewals are added to the carrying amount of the 
assets and expenditures for maintenance and repairs are charged to the consolidated income 
statement as incurred.
3.4 Tangible fixed 
assets 
Inventories are measured at their historical costs. The cost of inventories comprises costs of 
purchase, costs of conversion (including raw materials, direct labor cost, other directly related 
cost, manufacturing general overheads allocated based on the normal operating capacity) 
incurred in bringing the inventories to their present location and condition.
In case the net realizable value is lower than the original price, it must be calculated according to 
the net realizable value.
Net realisable value (“NRV”) represents the estimated selling price in the ordinary course of 
business less the estimated costs to complete and the estimated costs necessary to make the 
sale.
The perpetual method is used to record inventories, which are valued as follows:
Raw materials, tools and supplies 
andconsumables
Finished goods and work in process
Provision for obsolete inventories
An inventory provision is created for the estimated loss arising due to the impairment of value 
(through diminution, damage, obsolescence, etc.) of raw materials, finished goods, and other 
inventories owned by the Group, based on appropriate evidence of impairment available at the 
consolidated balance sheet date.  
Increases or decreases to the provision balance are recorded into the cost of goods sold account 
in the consolidated income statement. When inventories are expired, obsolescence, damage or 
become useless, the difference between the provision previously made and the historical cost of 
inventories are included in the consolidated income statement.
3.2 Inventories 
— Cost of finished goods, semi products on a weighted 
average basis.
— Cost of purchase on a weighted average basis.
Borrowing costs consist of interest and other costs that the Group incurs in connection with the 
borrowing of funds. 
3.7 Borrowing costs
Intangible fixed assets are stated at cost less accumulated amortisation.
The cost of an intangible fixed asset comprises its purchase price and any directly attributable 
costs of preparing the intangible asset for its intended use.
Expenditures for additions, improvements are added to the carrying amount of the assets and

business or for rent to others by the Group and when the Group receives the LUR certificate. The 
cost of LUR comprises any directly attributable costs of preparing the land for its intended use. 
The advance payment for land rental, of which the land lease contracts have effectiveness prior to 
2003 and land use right certificate being issued, are recorded as intangible fixed asset according 
to Circular No. 45/2013/TT-BTC issued by the Ministry of Finance on 25 April 2013 providing 
guideline for the management, use and calculation of depreciation or amortisation of assets 
(“Circular 45”).
Copyrights
Copyrights of maize and rice varieties are recognized at the purchase price for varieties not 
researched and developed by the Group. Copyrights are amortized on a straight-line basis over 
the short period of time between the estimated useful life and the time of purchase.

Business combinations are accounted for using the purchase method. The cost of a business 
combination is measured as the fair value of assets given, equity instruments issued and liabilities 
incurred or assumed at the date of exchange plus any costs directly attributable to the business 
combination. Identifiable assets and liabilities and contingent liabilities assumed in a business 
combination are measured initially at fair values at the date of business combination.
Goodwill acquired in a business combination is initially measured at cost being the excess of the 
cost the business combination over the Group’s interest in the net fair value of the acquiree’s 
identifiable assets, liabilities and contingent liabilities. If the cost of a business combination is 
less than the fair value of the net assets of the subsidiary acquired, the difference is recognised 
directly in the consolidated income statement. After initial recognition, goodwill is measured at 
cost less any accumulated amortisation. Goodwill is amortised over 10-year period on a straight-
line basis. The parent company conducts the periodical review for impairment of goodwill of 
investment in subsidiaries. If there are indicators of impairment loss incurred is higher than the 
yearly allocated amount of goodwill on the straight-line basis, the higher amount will be recorded 
in the consolidated income statement.

Investments in associates
The Group’s investment in its associates is accounted for using the equity method of accounting. 
An associate is an entity in which the Group has significant influence that is neither subsidiaries 
nor joint ventures. The Group generally deems they have significant influence if they have over 
20% of the voting rights.
Under the equity method, the investment is carried in the consolidated balance sheet at cost plus 
post acquisition changes in the group’s share of net assets of the associates. Goodwill arising 
on acquisition of the associate is included in the carrying amount of the investment. Goodwill is 
not amortised and subject to annual review of impairment. The consolidated income statement 
reflects the share of the post-acquisition results of operation of the associates.
The share of post-acquisition profit/(loss) of the associates is presented on face of the consolidated 
income statement and its share of post-acquisition movements in reserves is recognised in 
reserves. The cumulative post-acquisition movements are adjusted against the carrying amount 
of the investment. Dividend receivable from associates reduces the carrying amount of the 
investment.
The financial statements of the associates are prepared for the same reporting period and use 
the same accounting policies as the Group. Where necessary, adjustments are made to bring the 
accounting policies in line with those of the Group.

Interest
Revenue is recognised as the interest accrues (taking into account the effective yield on the asset)

Dividends
Income is recognised when the Group’s entitlement as an investor to receive the dividend is 
established.
Income from transfer of trading securities
Income from the transfer of trading securities is determined as the difference between the selling 
price and the transferred cost price. This income is recognized on the transaction date, i.e., when 
the transfer contract is executed.
Current income tax
Current income tax assets and liabilities for the current and prior periods are measured at the 
amount expected to be recovered from or paid to the taxation authorities. The tax rates and tax 
laws used to compute the amount are those that are enacted as at the balance sheet date.
Current income tax is charged or credited to the consolidated income statement, except when it 
relates to items recognised directly to equity, in which case the current income tax is also dealt 
with in equity.
Current income tax assets and liabilities are offset when there is a legally enforceable right for 
the Group to offset current tax assets against current tax liabilities and when the Group intends to 
settle its current tax assets and liabilities on a net basis.
Deferred tax
Deferred tax is provided using the liability method on temporary differences at the balance sheet 
date between the tax base of assets and liabilities and their carrying amount for financial reporting 
purposes.
Deferred tax liabilities are recognised for all taxable temporary differences, except:
•	
Where the deferred tax liability arises from the initial recognition of an asset or liability in a 
transaction which at the time of the related transaction affects neither the accounting profit 
nor taxable profit or loss; and
•	
In respect of taxable temporarily differences associated with investments in subsidiaries and 
associates where timing of the reversal of the temporary difference can be controlled and it is 
probable that the temporary difference will not reverse in the foreseeable future.
Deferred tax assets are recognised for all deductible temporary differences, carried forward 
unused tax credit and unused tax losses, to the extent that it is probable that taxable profit will be 
available against which deductible temporary differences, carried forward unused tax credit and 
unused tax losses can be utilised, except:
•	
Where the deferred tax asset in respect of deductible temporary difference which arises from 
the initial recognition of an asset or liability which at the time of the related transaction, 
affects neither the accounting profit nor taxable profit or loss; and
•	
In respect of deductible temporarily differences associated with investments in subsidiaries 
and associates, deferred tax assets are recognised only to the extent that it is probable that 
the temporary differences will reverse in the foreseeable future and taxable profit will be 
available against which the temporary differences can be utilised.
3.20 Taxation 
The carrying amount of deferred tax assets is reviewed at each balance sheet date and reduced to 
the extent that it is no longer probable that sufficient taxable profit will be available to allow all or 
part of the deferred income tax asset to be utilised. Previously unrecognised deferred tax assets 
are re-assessed at each balance sheet date and are recognised to the extent that it has become 
probable that future taxable profit will allow the deferred tax assets to be recovered.
Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured at the tax rates that are expected to apply in the 
period when the asset realised or the liability is settled based on tax rates and tax laws that have 
been enacted or substantively enacted at the  balance sheet date.
Deferred tax is charged or credited to the consolidated income statement, except when it 
relates to items recognised directly to equity, in which case the deferred tax is also dealt with 
in the equity account.
Deferred tax assets and liabilities are offset when there is a legally enforceable right for the Group 
to offset current tax assets against current tax liabilities and when they relate to income taxes 
levied by the same taxation authority on:
•	
Either the same taxable entity; or
•	
When the Group intends either settle current tax liabilities and assets on a net basis or to 
realise the assets and settle the liabilities simultaneously, in each future period in which 
significant amounts of deferred tax liabilities or assets are expected to be settled or recovered.

31.	 CORPORATE INCOME TAX
The Company and its subsidiaries has the obligation to pay 
corporate income tax (“CIT”) at the rate of 20% of taxable profits. 
In addition, the Company’s subsidiaries are entitled to the 
following CIT exemption and reductions:
ĕ ABT Company: The CIT rate applicable to profits from 
aquaculture activities of ABT Company is 10%.
ĕ Vinaseed Company is entitled to an exemption and 
reduction of CIT as a newly established enterprise from 
investment projects in the fields of high technology, scientific 
research and technological development if the company’s 
revenue from products and goods sold from scientific and 
technological activities accounted for a minimum of 30% of 
the total revenue. Specifically:
(i) The company is entitled to a CIT rate of 10% for 15 years 
commencing from the first year in which revenue is earned 
S&T activities to the effective date of Circular 03/2021/TT-BTC; 
(ii) The company is entitled to corporate income tax exemption 
for 4 years from the first year the enterprise has taxable 
income from new investment projects and a reduction of 50% 
in the following 9 years.
ĕ Vinarice Co., Ltd is entitled to CIT incentives with a 
preferential tax rate of 10% for a period of 15 years from the 
first year of official operation (in 2019) and at the common 
tax rate in other years. Later. This company is also exempted 
from CIT for four 4 years from the first year of taxable income 
(2020) and reduced by 50% of the applicable CIT rate for the 
next 9 years (from 2024).
ĕ Ha Nam High Tech Agricultural Development and Investment 
are entitled to a reduction of corporate income tax with the 
rate of 17%. This company also entitled to a CIT for the 2 years 
commencing from the first year in which taxable profits and  a 
reduction of 50% in the following 4 years.
ĕ FMC Company, KAC Company and VTC Company are exempt 
from corporate income tax during the operation period for 
agricultural and fishery products activities in extremely 
difficult areas, FMC Company is entitled to 10% tax rate 
for the entire period. operating time for fishing activities in 
disadvantaged areas.
ĕ VFG Company: The applicable tax rate is 17% within 10 years 
since the revenue is generated, tax exemption for 2 years and 
50% reduction of tax payable within the next 4 years from the 
first year of profit for VFG Company's Long An factory.
ĕ 584NT: The CIT rate applicable to profits from processing 
aquatic products activities of 584NT Company is 15%.
The tax returns filed by the Company and its subsidiaries 
are subject to examination by the tax authorities.  As the 
application of tax laws and regulations is susceptible 
to varying interpretations, the amounts reported in the 
consolidated financial statements could change at a later 
date upon final determination by the tax authorities.

Dear Valued Stakeholders, 
The year 2023 has been a significant 
journey for us, marked by numerous 
challenges, opportunities, and notable 
achievements. 
These 
milestones 
contribute to a diverse and vibrant 
picture of The PAN Group’s sustainable 
development.
With the belief “Think Green - Act 
Strong,” our activities are not 
only about understanding, but 
also about taking continuous and 
determined action in this spirit. 
“Think Green” is our promise to the 
future, a commitment to caring for 
and protecting the environment, 
society, and the community. “Act 
Strong” is our strength in turning 
dreams into reality, building a 
solid foundation, and growing a 
sustainable business with each 
step forward. 
In the challenging global market 
context of 2023, our Group’s 
revenue 
marginally 
declined, 
reaching VND 132 trillion, while 
consolidated profit was VND 819 
billion, a 3% rise over the same 
period 
in 
2022. 
Additionally, 
PAN also carried out a number 
of worthwhile community and 
environmental 
initiatives. 
We 
directly employed 10,321 workers 
with an average monthly pay of 
VND 12.33 million, which is 1.45 
times greater than Vietnam’s 
highest provincial minimum wage 
in 2023. Throughout the year, PAN 
did not encounter any violations 
regarding environmental, social, 
or labor issues, and contributed 
VND 98 billion to the community. 
Towards the goal of planting 1 
million trees by 2030, we have 
planted over 500,000 trees in 9 
provinces across the country. 
As a business in the agriculture 
and food sector with a sustainable 
development goal, PAN has been 
a pioneer in participating in major 
projects such as the “Sustainable 
development of 1 million hectares 
of 
high-quality, 
low-emission 
rice cultivation linked to green

2030” and “Increasing Farmers’ 
Income.” Additionally, we have 
committed 
VND 
3 
billion 
in 
scholarships under the “Lighting 
Up 
Dreams” 
and 
“Nurturing 
Talents” programs for students 
with difficult circumstances and 
outstanding 
achievements 
in 
agriculture, forestry, and fisheries 
study. By participating in the 
green transition, we are planting 
green seeds that will help to 
create a green future for both the 
community and ourselves.

Chartered Bank Vietnam signed a 
Memorandum of Understanding to 
implement ESG financial solutions 
and services, granting qualifying 
projects 
to 
access 
Standard 
Chartered’s green capital. As 
a result, our commitment to 
the Go Green vision has been 
partially achieved through the 
Go Global strategy over the past 
year. Throughout this journey, I 
believe the spirit of “Think Green 
- Act Strong” has provided a lot 
of inspiration and positive energy.

of

change

to

The signing ceremony of the Memorandum of Understanding 
(MOU) between The PAN Group and Standard Chartered Bank 
(Vietnam) took place within the framework of COP 28. According 
to the MOU, Standard Chartered (Vietnam) will support The PAN 
Group in accessing financial solutions and services based on ESG 
factors (Environmental, Social, Governance), to meet the expanding 
financial options for PAN’s sustainable development projects.
In addition to green credits and/or sustainable bonds, the 
program also provides financial support for projects such as 
cashew processing line development, promoting value-added 
aquaculture products, and increasing income for rice farmers.
Projects that meet the criteria and comply with Standard 
Chartered Vietnam’s Sustainable Finance Framework, as 
well as principles for green loans or green bonds, will receive 
financial support from the UK-based bank.
This cooperation opens opportunities for both parties. The PAN 
Group can expand its financial options for the development 
projects of the Group and its subsidiaries through ESG-related 
solutions. For Standard Chartered Vietnam, through ESG financial 
solutions with the PAN Group, the bank can support PAN’s green 
projects, contributing to promoting Vietnamese enterprises’ 
access to green financial markets, thereby contributing to 
sustainable development goals, emission reduction, and carbon 
neutrality commitments strongly advocated by the Government.

Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) is the responsibility 
of producers and importers to manage the packaging of 
their products when they are disposed of in the environment. 
Since the Vietnamese Government began implementing clear 
regulations on EPR, as outlined in the Environmental Protection 
Law of 2020, PAN Group has proactively researched, developed, 
and effectively applied EPR solutions across its member units.
We adhere to the principle of “Avoid - Minimize - Reuse, Recycle,” 
helping our units effectively manage waste at the source.
At our confectionery manufacturing plants, we have redesigned 
the packaging of cakes and candies, resulting in a 9.5% 
reduction in packaging materials for cakes and 10% for candies. 
Bibica has replaced nylon bags with paper bags during the Mid-
Autumn Festival and Lunar New Year, eliminating approximately 
1 million nylon bags annually.
Khang An Foods has established a Recycling Fund with the 
goal of encouraging employees to practice waste segregation 
at the source. After two years of implementation (2022-2023), 
the company has collected over 4,000 kg of plastic bottles 
for recycling. This is a meaningful program that enhances 
environmental protection responsibilities for employees and 
the community.

Using an electric shock machine to stun shrimp is in line with animal welfare requirements.
The increasing demands for animal welfare require changes in farming, harvesting, and 
processing procedures. The requirement initially was only to follow the ASC process, then it 
gradually became more strict including stocking density, not too intense, and especially to 
environmental indicators management such as dissolved oxygen, toxic gas, etc. Then there 
are requirements for shrimp harvesting after being pulled up to the water surface to be 
killed and preserved by cold immersion within 2 minutes, followed by a requirement that 
shrimp harvesting when pulling nets should not use electric shock to make shrimp jump into 
the nets. Recently, customers have demanded faster shrimp killing and must be done with 
electricity, as Sao Ta is currently implementing. The upcoming trend is to install cameras 
under shrimp ponds to monitor its activities.

Affirming its commitment to sustainable development, The PAN Group 
has established the Sustainable Development Subcommittee under 
the Board of Directors, with Ms. Nguyen Thi Tra My, the CEO, appointed

The subcommittee is responsible for advising the Board of Directors 
and the Board of Management on strategies and plans aligned with 
sustainable development objectives, as well as participating in the 
implementation and support of The PAN Group's activities.
Implementing sustainable development activities, ESG is the 
Sustainable Development Division of The PAN Group along with a 
network of sustainable development coordinators at the manage-
ment levels within subsidiary companies. The network is established 
to ensure the dissemination of the Group's policies widely and 
effectively implemented in all subsidiary companies, as well as 
progressively enhancing awareness and adjusting behaviors in line  
with the development direction.
The network of coordinators serves as the focal point for collaborat-
ing with specialized departments on environmental, social, gover-
nance issues, etc., within subsidiary companies, carrying out 
directives from the CEOs of these companies and coordinating with 
The PAN Group's Sustainable Development Division.

Along with the organizational structure established above, The 
PAN Group also sets criteria and regulations to comprehensive-
ly manage related activities to manage environmental, social, 
and governance issues.
Internal Code of Conduct
Regulating activities and providing guidelines for The 
conduct of The PAN Group internally and externally, aiming 
for transparency in development policies, commitment to 
integrity, and responsibility in actions.
Sustainability Report according to GRI Standards 2021
The Sustainability Report according to GRI standards aims 
for comprehensive transparency in all financial and non-fi-
nancial activities.
Responsible Investment
As an investment company, The PAN Group sets criteria for 
investments that align with sustainable development 
strategies. Accordingly, we do not invest in industries 
restricted by law or conditional businesses such as 
resource exploitation, casino or gambling businesses, 
alcohol production, or those employing illegal labor, etc. 
PAN also conducts assessments and screens target 
companies regarding environmental and social issues in 
M&A plans to ensure compliance with established criteria.
The PAN Group's Sustainability performance index
With a desire to rigorously measure and promote 
improvements and effectiveness in activities towards 
sustainable development, The PAN Group has estab-
lished an index to track results, compare year by year, 
and declare future targets. Alongside financial figures, 
The PAN Group's Sustainability performance index will 
most clearly reflect the results of our operations.
Practice Principles
This document is issued to ensure that the activities of member 
companies and stakeholders are in line with the direction of 
sustainable development and the commitment of the Group, 
which is: "Providing high-quality products with reputable origins 
in a complete value chain."
Applying international standards and norms
We voluntarily adhere to international norms regarding environ-
mental, social, and governance aspects, as well as other interna-
tional standards such as IFC’s performance standard, ADB's 
safeguard policy statement, Global GAP, ISO14000, ASC, BAP, 
BSCI, SEDEX, FSSC22000, HACCP, BRC, and IFS.
FOUNDATION POLICIES 
In 2023, marked a shift in the sustainable development gover-
nance of the Group. A new governance structure was formed 
with the establishment of the Sustainable Development Steer-
ing Committee, consisting of the Group's CEO and representa-
tives from the leadership of the three main business segments, 
creating a seamless thread throughout the Group in imple-
menting the sustainable development strategy. 
In the context of the implementation of ESG strategy, sustain-
able development goals, and emission reduction pathways 
becoming increasingly imperative from the government to 
businesses, innovation in the governance structure is necessary 
and expected to bring about even more achievements for the 
Group in the future.

a thorough understanding of
