its opportunities and challenges;

assets and image of the Group;

responsibility for risk

M&A of Atani Holdings Joint Stock Company
Rationale
Atani Holdings JSC specializes in probiotics with proprietary microbial strains produced in the 
advanced U.S. technology-based manufacturing line. 
The PAN Group’s investment in Atani offers strategic advantages for both parties. For PAN, this 
acquisition diversi昀椀es its investment portfolio, capitalizing on Atani’s expertise in probiotics 
while creating synergies with existing business operations. The Group can utilize its extensive 
distribution network to bring Atani’s probiotic products to consumers.
Probiotics play a crucial role in agriculture, enhancing plant disease resistance, mitigating the 
negative effects of pesticides, and improving soil health. These bene昀椀ts lead to stronger crop 
growth, thus increasing agricultural productivity and quality.
Additionally, this investment expands Atani’s product and service offerings. By integrating 
probiotics with existing crop varieties and plant protection products, Atani can provide farmers 
with comprehensive agricultural solutions. The company can also add value to its product 
lineup by offering consultation and support services on probiotic usage.
Implementation 
and timeline
Following Resolution No. 01-03/2024/NQ-HĐQT, dated March 18, 2024, the Board of Directors

results

of昀椀cially became a subsidiary of PAN Farm JSC as of the acquisition date.
Increasing Ownership in PAN Farm JSC
Rationale
PAN Farm, holding a central position in the Group’s agricultural ecosystem, plays a pivotal 
role in realizing The PAN Group’s strategic objectives. With two key subsidiaries, Vietnam 
Fumigation JSC and Vietnam National Seed Group JSC, PAN Farm has achieved signi昀椀cant 
strides in revenue and pro昀椀t in recent years, primarily driven by the strong growth of Vietnam 
Fumigation JSC.
Increasing PAN’s ownership in PAN Farm is a strategic move aimed at reinforcing its market 
position and expanding its in昀氀uence in the agricultural sector.
Implementation 
and timeline
Following Resolution No. 01-10/2024/NQ-HĐQT, dated October 31, 2024, the Board of Directors of 
PAN Group JSC approved the acquisition of additional equity in PAN Farm from transferring parties.

Taxation
Income tax expense represents the sum of the tax currently payable and deferred tax.
The tax currently payable is based on taxable pro昀椀t for the period. Taxable pro昀椀t differs 
from pro昀椀t before tax as reported in the consolidated income statement because 
it excludes items of income or expense that are taxable or deductible in other years 
(including loss carried forward, if any) and it further excludes items that are never

Deferred tax is recognised on signi昀椀cant differences between carrying amounts 
of assets and liabilities in the interim consolidated 昀椀nancial statements and the 
corresponding tax bases used in the computation of taxable pro昀椀t and is accounted for 
using balance sheet liability method. Deferred tax liabilities are generally recognised 
for all temporary differences and deferred tax assets are recognised to the extent that 
it is probable that taxable pro昀椀t will be available against which deductible temporary 
differences can be utilised. 
As at 31 December 2024, the Parent company and PAN-Hulic Joint Stock Company -a

Deferred tax is calculated at the tax rates that are expected to apply in the period when 
the liability is settled or the asset realised. Deferred tax is charged or credited to pro昀椀t or 
loss, except when it relates to items charged or credited directly to equity, in which case 
the deferred tax is also dealt with in equity.
Deferred tax assets and liabilities are offset when there is a legally enforceable right to

taxes levied by the same tax authority and the Group intends to settle its current tax 
assets and liabilities on a net basis. 
The determination of the tax currently payable is based on the current interpretation of

ultimate determination depends on the results of the tax authorities’ examinations.
Other taxes are paid in accordance with the prevailing tax laws in Vietnam.

31. BUSINESS AND GEOGRAPHICAL SEGMENTS
The Group chooses business segments as the main reporting ones because the Group’s risks and pro昀椀tability are primarily impacted 
by the differences in products and services provided by the Group. Segments by geography are secondary reporting ones. The Group’s 
business activities are organized and managed according to the nature of the products and services provided by the Group with each 
division being a strategic business unit that provides different products and serves different markets.
The Group consists of segments divided by main business activities as follows:
 
●Agriculture;
 
●Food production and processing;
 
●Others.
The Group’s business activities include export and domestic activities.
Prices applied to transactions between segments are determined on the same basis as with third parties. Revenue, expenses, and 
business results of segments include transactions between them. These transactions are eliminated when preparing the consolidated 
昀椀nancial statements.

In 2013, Southern Seed Joint Stock Company (“SSC Company”) - 
a subsidiary of the Company, purchased assets from East-West 
Seed Joint Venture Company (“EW”) including land use rights. 
According to Decision No. 3201/QD-UBND dated 28 June 2014, 
SSC Company has been approved by the People’s Committee 
of Ho Chi Minh City (“People’s Committee”) to use a land area 
of 259,717.2 m2 in Pham Van Coi Commune, Cu Chi District, Ho 
Chi Minh City with the purpose of researching and producing 
vegetable seeds. Therefore, SSC Company is obliged to pay land 
rent from the date of signing this Decision to 30 December 2020. 
Currently, the above land area is being used by SSC Company. 
However, the Department of Natural Resources and Environment 
and the Ho Chi Minh City Tax Department have not determined 
the of昀椀cial land rent unit price. Therefore, SSC Company and 
local management agencies have not yet been able to determine 
the land rent amount for the above leased land for the entire 
corresponding lease period. The land rent has been temporarily 
accrued annually by SSC Company based on the land rent unit 
price of EW (the previous lessee) under the land lease contract 
No. 9018/HDTD-GTD dated 29 June 2000 between EW and the 
People’s Committee of Ho Chi Minh City. On the date of issuance 
of these consolidated 昀椀nancial statements, SSC Company has 
temporarily accrued land rent from July 2014 to December 2024 
with an amount of VND 6,457,217,824. When there is an of昀椀cial 
land rent unit price and a notice of adjustment of the land rent 
from the relevant state management agencies, SSC Company 
will make adjustments and pay additional amount for the next 
payment period (if any).
On 27 May 2005, SSC Company signed a land lease contract with 
the People’s Committee of Binh Duong Province for a land area 
of 776,947.3 m2 in Tan Hiep Commune, Phu Giao District, Binh 
Duong Province to be used for agricultural purposes for a period 
of 20 years from 25 March 2002 to 25 March 2022. In 2020, SSC 
Company carried out procedures to extend the land lease period 
and was approved by the People’s Committee of Binh Duong 
Province to extend it according to Decision No. 685/QD-UBND 
dated 13 March 2020.
On 21 April 2022, SSC Company received the Notice of temporary 
payment of land rent in the form of annual form No. 12/TB-CCT 
from the Tax Department of Tan Uyen Region for the above land 
with a unit price of 192 VND/m2. Accordingly, on 07 June 2022, 
the Tax Sub-Department of Tan Uyen Region issued Of昀椀cial 
Letter No. 3424/BPMCPG-CCTKV con昀椀rming that the company 
had ful昀椀lled its 昀椀nancial obligations on land rent for the years 
from 2006 to 2021.
However, on 15 July 2022, SSC Company received Notice No. 
11988/TB-CTBD from the Tax Department of Binh Duong 
Province on land rent and water surface rent in the form of annual 
payment. According to this Notice, the adjusted land rental unit 
price has increased from 192 VND/m2 to 5,258 VND/m2 with a 
price stabilization period from 13 March 2020 to 13 March 2025.
On 28 October 2022, SSC Company issued Of昀椀cial Letter No. 334/
CV-SSC proposing the People’s Committee and the Department 
of Natural Resources and Environment (“Natural Resources and 
Environment”) of Binh Duong Province on the adjustment of the 
land unit price and assigned by the People’s Committee to the 
Land Registry for consideration and response. Therefore, SSC 
Company and local management agencies have not been able to 
determine the land rent amount for the above leased land.
SSC has provisionally paid the entire land rental fee for 2022 and 
2023 with an amount of VND 4,085,188,093 per year according 
to Notice No. 11988/TB-CTBD dated 27 October 2022 and 29 
November 2022 and Notice No. 12/TB-CCT of the Tax Department 
of Tan Uyen Area (SSC received this Notice on 16 January 2024). 
In 2024, the land rental fee for 2023 was reduced by 30%, 
equivalent to VND 1,225,556,671, according to Decision No. 911/
QĐ-CTBDU dated 26 March 2024 issued by the Head of the Binh 
Duong Tax Department. The land rental reduction was based on 
Article 3, Decision No. 25/2023/QD-TTg dated 03 October 2023 of 
the Prime Minister regarding the reduction of land rental fees 
for 2023.
As at the end of 2024, SSC Company has not yet received an of昀椀cial 
notice from the tax authorities regarding the land rental fee 
payable for 2024, therefore it has self-assessed and temporarily 
paid the land rental fee for the year 2024 with an amount of VND 
2,859,632,232 after deducting the amount eligible for exemption. 
SSC Company will adjust and make any additional payment or 
refund in the next payment period (if any).

MESSAGE FROM THE CHAIRMAN OF 
THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS
Dear Valued Shareholders,
The year 2025 came to a close amid a highly uncertain 
business environment. The global economy remained 
fragmented, trade protectionism continued to rise, 
supply chains had yet to fully stabilize, and climate 
change became increasingly evident with greater 
intensity and unpredictability. For the agricultural sector, 
these are no longer distant risks, but daily pressures felt 
across the entire value chain — from production, 
procurement and processing to exports.
Against this backdrop, Vietnamese agriculture faced 
dual pressures: volatility in international markets and 
increasingly severe natural conditions. Prices of 
several key commodities, particularly rice, remained 
low for much of the year, while input costs and 
weather-related risks continued to erode profit 
margins across the industry.
The PAN Group was not immune to these impacts. 
However, what matters most is not whether conditions are 
favorable or difficult, but how a business chooses to 
navigate them.
In 2025, The PAN Group recorded revenue of VND 17,586 
billion, up 8.7%, while profit after tax attributable to 
shareholders of the parent company reached VND 673 
billion, an increase of 10.5% compared to the previous 
year. In a year that was challenging for most businesses 
in the agriculture and food value chain, these results 
reflect the resilience, discipline and operational capability 
of our entire system. More importantly than the numbers, 
however, we has taken another step in reassessing 
ourself, reviewing our portfolio of businesses, and 
preparing for a new phase of development with a clearer 
strategic focus.
After a year of challenges, one conviction has become 
even clearer to us: PAN should not pursue an overly 
diversified path. The future of the Group lies in agriculture, 
including aquaculture, where we has built our deepest 
foundations, the clearest ecosystem, and the strongest 
potential to create long-term value.
The PAN Group do not pursue growth at any cost. What 
we pursues is quality growth: better capital efficiency, 
stronger resilience, deeper control of the value chain, 
and a more sustainable competitive position. In 
today’s environment, growth is no longer simply a 
matter of scale. It is about quality, adaptability, 
technology, financial discipline, and making the right 
strategic choices.
This mindset shaped PAN’s decisions throughout the 
past year. We continued to conduct a comprehensive 
review of our business portfolio, proactively reallocated 
resources, sharpened our focus on core sectors, and 
maintained strict discipline in investment, cash flow 
management and financial health preservation. For PAN, 
prudence does not mean retreat — it is the condition for 
going further in a volatile environment.
At the same time, the Group continued investing in long-
term foundations: seed research and development, 
farming areas, aquaculture zones, processing capacity, 
product quality, and the ability to meet increasingly 
stringent market standards. These investments do not 
generate immediate results, but they will determine the 
quality of PAN’s growth for many years to come. We 
believe that the greatest value in agriculture does not lie 
in selling more raw commodities, but in the ability to 
create products of higher quality, greater added value, 
and stronger, more sustainable market positions.
Entering 2026, we remain cautious but not pessimistic. 
The world will continue to face volatility. Trade barriers, 
exchange rate pressures, climate risks, and the 
reshaping of global supply chains will continue to create 
challenges for the agricultural sector. At the same time, 
demand for safe, traceable, and higher value-added food 
products continues to grow. This is the foundation for us 
to remain steadfast in our chosen direction.
In the coming period, The PAN Group will focus on 3 
priorities: 
strengthening 
our 
core 
agricultural 
ecosystem; enhancing capabilities in research, seeds, 
production technology and processing; and expanding 
markets in a more sustainable, diversified and proactive 
manner amid global trade fluctuations. In short, PAN 
will move forward with greater focus, deeper 
capabilities, and higher efficiency.
We do not expect dramatic leaps in the short term. First 
and foremost, 2026 will be a year to reinforce our 
foundations, strengthen resilience, and prepare for a 
new growth cycle. PAN has gone through many difficult 
periods, and what has helped us remain steadfast has 
never been flashy decisions, but the ability to maintain 
discipline, stay committed to what is right, and build 
capabilities over time.
On behalf of the Board of Directors, I would like to 
express my sincere gratitude to our valued shareholders, 
partners, and all employees for your continued trust and 
support throughout the past year.
We enter the next stage of our journey with necessary 
prudence, with determination to innovate, and with the 
belief that a strong agricultural enterprise is not built on 
short-term growth, but on the quality accumulated 
steadily over many years.
Yours sincerely,

According to the General Statistics Office, in 2025 the total 
rice cultivation area reached 7.13 million hectares, a 
decrease of 1.1 thousand hectares compared to 2024. 
However, thanks to the adoption of new seed varieties and 
improved farming techniques, rice productivity improved. 
Total national grain output reached 47.9 million tons, up 
96.4 thousand tons year-on-year. Rice production 
amounted to 43.54 million tons, the highest level in the 
past four years, despite numerous challenges, including 
unfavorable weather, localized pest outbreaks during the 
Winter–Spring crop, and significant impacts from storms, 
and flooding during the Summer–Autumn crop.
The cultivated area and output of several annual crops 
continued to be restructured, reducing acreage for low-
economic-efficiency crops while expanding higher-value 
crops. Maize cultivation area reached 865.6 thousand 
hectares, down 5.9 thousand hectares compared to the 
previous year, yet output was estimated at 4.4 million tons, 
up 7.8 thousand tons. Other food crops such as peanuts,

Business prospects 
Although global rice supply in 2026 is forecast to remain 
abundant and prices of conventional rice are unlikely to 
increase significantly, the market is expected to become 
increasingly segmented. The strategy of focusing on 
premium branded rice (such as ST25, organic rice, and 
Jasmine) enables Vinaseed to benefit from selling prices 
typically 10%–30% higher than standard rice. This allows 
the Group to maintain healthy profit margins even as 
overall rice prices remain in a cyclical adjustment phase.
Vinaseed owns a nationwide network of subsidiaries and 
seed research centers (in Ha Nam, Quang Nam, Southern 
Vietnam, etc.), enabling tight control across the entire 
value chain from seed development to finished products. 
With year-end 2025 inventory exceeding VND 808 billion 
(mostly finished goods), Vinaseed has ample supply 
capacity to quickly meet demand for premium branded 
rice orders in 2026, as the market increasingly favors 
highly transparent and traceable products.
In 2026, Vinaseed is expected to continue its profit growth 
cycle, driven by a successful transition from a volume-
based model to a value- and responsibility-oriented 
approach. Strong rice brands combined with an efficient 
cost management system will be key factors enabling the 
Group to weather challenges and achieve breakthrough 
growth amid the ongoing repositioning of the rice industry.
The outlook for Vietnam Fumigation Joint Stock Company 
(VFC) in 2026 is also assessed as highly positive, as the 
company enters a new development cycle built on solid 
strategic alliances and a shift toward green agriculture 
trends. The agrochemical industry is rapidly transitioning 
toward biological products, with annual growth exceeding 
16.4%. VFC has identified future growth drivers in 
emerging agricultural trends such as bio-fertilizers and 
low-emission farming.
Effective February 10, 2026, Circular 75/2025/TT-BNNMT 
officially takes effect, prioritizing biological active 
ingredients and advanced formulations (such as OD and 
WG). VFC has proactively invested in production lines for 
these formulations at its Long An factory to comply with 
new regulations and align with market trends. The 
company continues to maintain its leading position with 
approximately 60% share of the national fumigation 
market. Although this market has matured, being the only 
enterprise owning advanced fumigation technologies 
(such as J-System and SIROCIRC) enables VFC to secure 
stable revenue streams and high profit margins, serving 
as a quality assurance backbone for Vietnamese 
agricultural products entering stringent markets such as 
Australia and the United States.
However, 2026 will also present significant challenges, 
as competitive agricultural commodity prices may 
directly affect the revenue scale and profitability of the 
Group’s agriculture segment. The green transition and 
increasingly stringent environmental standards act as a 
filter, compelling the agricultural sector to shift from 
quantity-driven expansion to quality enhancement and 
bio-safety compliance in order to sustain long-term 
growth momentum.

Despite record export revenue, the industry faced 
mounting policy headwinds in the U.S. market. A new 
reciprocal tariff of 20% was imposed in August 2025, 
alongside a preliminary anti-dumping duty on shrimp 
(POR19) of up to 35.29%. Additionally, the U.S. decision 
not to recognize the equivalence of 12 Vietnamese 
fisheries under the Marine Mammal Protection Act 
(MMPA) poses a direct risk to over USD 500 million in 
annual exports. Meanwhile, the European Commission’s 
IUU “yellow card” continues to elevate compliance costs 
and weigh on product reputation.
Against this backdrop, strategic restructuring toward 
higher value-added products, deeper processing 
capabilities, and the standardization of sustainable 
farming zones has become central to the industry’s 
long-term competitiveness. Enterprises with strong 
governance, vertically integrated value chains, and 
diversified export portfolios have been better positioned 
to sustain profitability amid policy and market volatility.
Within this selective yet fundamentally recovering 
environment, The PAN Group’s 2025 performance in 
the shrimp and pangasius segments demonstrates the 
effectiveness of its strategy centered on sustainable 
value chains, rigorous farming area management, and 
expansion into premium export markets. This strategic 
positioning has enabled the Group to capture the 
sector’s recovery momentum while improving margin 
quality and operational resilience.
The year 2025 marked a historic milestone for Vietnam’s 
seafood industry, with export turnover reaching a record 
USD 11.3 billion, representing growth of approximately 
12.4–13% compared to 2024. This achievement was 
realized amid heightened global trade volatility driven by 
geopolitical 
tensions 
and 
rising 
protectionism, 
underscoring the industry’s resilience and adaptability. 
Key growth drivers included stronger global demand for 
food security and stockpiling, proactive export market 
diversification, 
and 
effective 
utilization 
of 
tariff 
preferences under major free trade agreements such as 
the CPTPP, EVFTA, and RCEP.
Total seafood production in 2025 was estimated at 9,947.5 
thousand tons, up 3.0% year-on-year. Aquaculture 
remained the primary growth driver, reaching 6,116.8 
thousand tons, an increase of 5.1%, supported by 
favorable weather conditions and gradually stabilizing 
input costs. Shrimp and pangasius continued to anchor 
the sector’s export performance. Pangasius exports 
recovered strongly, exceeding USD 2 billion by November 
2025, while shrimp output surpassed 1.5 million tons. In 
contrast, capture fisheries declined marginally by 0.2% 
due to adverse weather patterns and stricter regulatory 
enforcement aimed at addressing the European 
Commission’s IUU “yellow card.”

U.S. Department of Commerce (DOC) announced the 
final anti-dumping duty rate for the POR19 review period

uncertainty created by the earlier preliminary rate of

shrimp exports to the U.S. market. The Group maintains

increasing ownership in existing ones) and developing

business activities take place, investments mainly involve 
building new factories, expanding production facilities, 
increasing capacity, and scaling up farming and processing 
operations. Additionally, M&A activities may also be 
carried out to expand market share and integrate the value 
chain, tailored to each business segment.

ENVIRONMENT
In 2025, the PAN Group continued to advance its sustainability 
roadmap, with a strong focus on greenhouse gas emissions 
reduction and energy transition. Despite capacity expansion 
and increased operational scale across several subsidiaries, 
CO2 emissions intensity per unit of revenue (tons CO2e per 
VND billion) decreased by 2.3% year-on-year. This 
improvement reflects the effectiveness of operational 
optimization measures and enhanced energy management 
practices implemented throughout the Group.
During the year, subsidiaries implemented a range of 
targeted initiatives. These included the installation of an 
additional 1.38 MWp of rooftop solar capacity and the 
conversion of diesel-fired boilers to biomass-based 
steam (rice husk) at Khang An Foods, resulting in an 
annual reduction of approximately 321,910 liters of diesel 
(DO) consumption.
At the same time, the PAN Group continued to scale up its 
low-emission rice cultivation model in the Mekong Delta, 
implemented by Vinaseed. The cultivated area reached 
20,517.8 hectares—twenty times higher than in 2024—
contributing to methane emission reductions and improved 
water-use efficiency.

Circular economy practices were further strengthened to 
optimize resource utilization and minimize environmental 
impacts. The sludge reuse initiative for vermiculture was 
expanded across approximately 80 hectares of pangasius 
farming ponds, generating economic value while improving 
pond environmental conditions.
Fimex VN currently operates more than 540 hectares of 
shrimp farming area under a proprietary microbial-
based farming protocol developed in-house, with an 
annual output of 30,000 tons of commercial shrimp. The 
farming area secures approximately 30% of its raw 
material demand, supporting supply stability and 
enhancing overall competitiveness.
In particular, 2025 marked a significant milestone as two 
subsidiaries, Aquatex Bentre and Fimex VN, successfully 
implemented the project “Whiteleg Shrimp Farming in 
Freshwater Areas” under a closed-loop production model.
The project has a designed capacity of approximately 1.6 
billion post-larvae per year and applies a recirculating 
water system throughout the nursery phase. Once meeting 
quality standards, the shrimp post-larvae are transferred to 
Fimex VN’s farming areas in Soc Trang. This model 
strengthens the Group’s ability to secure a stable supply of 
high-quality seed stock while enhancing resilience to 
environmental and water resource fluctuations.

OVERVIEW OF BUSINESS ACTIVITIES IN 2025
Overview
In 2025, the global economy continued to experience 
heightened volatility amid escalating trade tensions and 
geopolitical risks, which exerted widespread impacts 
on global production and supply chains. The year was 
characterized as a period of “weak recovery,” marked 
by elevated uncertainty and moderating growth 
momentum, with global GDP projected to decelerate to 
a range of 2.5%–3.1%. The global economy is confronting 
a “spiral” of challenges, including record-high public 
debt exceeding USD 324 trillion (equivalent to 325% of 
global GDP), persistent inflationary pressures, and the 
rising tide of trade protectionism—particularly the 
reciprocal tariff policies initiated by U.S. President 
Donald Trump. In parallel with ongoing geopolitical 
conflicts in Russia–Ukraine and the Middle East, global 
FDI inflows trended downward overall, albeit with a 
pronounced reallocation toward high-technology and 
renewable energy sectors. While advanced economies 
recorded subdued recovery, the Asia–Pacific region and 
ASEAN 
sustained 
comparatively 
robust 
growth. 
Concurrently, the global race in artificial intelligence 
emerged as a strategic growth driver, expected to 
enhance productivity gains in 2026.
In 2025, Vietnam’s economy faced considerable 
challenges. Severe storms and prolonged heavy rainfall 
resulted in widespread flooding, flash floods, and 
landslides 
across 
multiple 
localities, 
disrupting 
production and business operations and adversely 
affecting livelihoods.
Against this backdrop, Vietnam emerged as a regional 
bright spot in terms of resilience and adaptability, 
achieving GDP growth of 8.02% and expanding the size of 
the economy to USD 514 billion (ranking 32nd globally). 
Total import–export turnover reached a record high of 
USD 930 billion, generating a trade surplus of over USD 20 
billion. GDP per capita increased to USD 5,026, officially 
elevating Vietnam to upper-middle-income status.
In terms of sectoral contribution to total gross value 
added, the agriculture, forestry, and fisheries sector 
recorded growth of 3.78%, contributing 5.30% to the 
overall increase in value added. Despite adverse weather 
conditions, timely response measures and effective 
disaster remediation efforts enabled the sector to 
maintain stable production output.

KEY HIGHLIGHTS 
IN 2025
In 2025, the global economy 
continued to face pressures from 
persistent inflation, rising trade 
protectionism 
and

demand in several major markets. 
Despite these challenges, the 
Group maintained positive growth 
momentum.
Consolidated revenue increased

while 
profit 
after 
tax

These results reflect the Group’s 
strong 
governance 
capability, 
adaptability to market volatility 
and 
the 
effectiveness 
of 
its 
integrated 
agriculture–food 
ecosystem development model 
that PAN has consistently pursued 
over the years.
In 2025, the Group made significant progress in promoting science, 
technology and innovation. The Group signed cooperation agreements with 
the Beijing Academy of Agriculture and Forestry Sciences (BAAFS) and the 
Guangxi Academy of Agricultural Sciences (GXAAS), establishing a 
comprehensive framework for collaboration in crop breeding research and 
development, genetic material exchange, scientific training and the 
application of advanced technologies in sustainable agriculture.
In addition, the Group collaborated with the Vietnam National University of 
Agriculture to organize the international scientific conference titled 
“Technological Innovation in Crop Breeding within Enterprises and Research 
Organizations.” The conference attracted more than 100 scientists, experts 
and enterprises in the agricultural science and technology sector.
The conference introduced new research directions including accelerated 
breeding techniques, gene editing, artificial intelligence applications and 
biotechnology in crop improvement.
Alongside research collaboration, the Group also signed cooperation 
agreements with Agri Smile Co., Ltd. and the Mitsubishi Research Institute 
(MRI) to promote sustainable organic agriculture in Vietnam. Within this 
partnership, VFC and the Vinaseed Research Institute play a central role in 
testing the effectiveness of biological products, supporting regulatory 
registration and commercializing biostimulants, thereby developing 
integrated sustainable farming solutions for farmers.
Within the Group’s agricultural ecosystem, 2025 marked 
an important milestone for Vinaseed when Ms. Nguyen 
Thi Tra My, Group Chief Executive Officer, officially 
assumed the position of Chairwoman of Vinaseed’s 
Board of Directors in February 2025.
This transition opened a new phase of comprehensive 
transformation in governance and strategic development. 
Vinaseed implemented a restructuring of its operating 
model, enhanced governance standards and positioned 
research and development as a central pillar through the 
establishment of the Vinaseed Research Institute and a 
High-level Scientific Council.
At the same time, PAN continued to play a pioneering role in 
implementing low-emission agricultural models aligned 
with the Government’s program “Sustainable development 
of one million hectares of high-quality, low-emission rice 
associated with green growth in the Mekong Delta.”
The collaborative model among Vinaseed, VFC and Binh 
Dien II in building a sustainable rice value chain has 
completed three pilot seasons and demonstrated clear 
effectiveness by reducing input costs, improving farmers’ 
profitability and lowering greenhouse gas emissions.
Within the TRVC project, Vinarice emerged as the 
leading enterprise in emission reduction performance, 
expanding its participating farming area to 20,518 
hectares, accounting for approximately 62.5% of the 
project’s total area, and achieving an emission 
reduction of approximately 89,046 tCO2e, equivalent to 
4.34 tCO2e per hectare.
The year 2025 also marked the 50th anniversary of VFC. 
In the new development phase, the company continues 
to shift its product portfolio toward sustainability by 
increasing 
the 
share 
of 
biological 
products, 
biostimulants and soil improvement solutions, while 
developing integrated solution packages for low-
emission farming systems.
In the biotechnology sector, BioSpring further expanded 
its product portfolio by successfully developing and 
registering five new products, including three microbial 
products 
serving 
agriculture 
and 
environmental 
applications, thereby laying the foundation for product 
diversification in the coming years.

uncertainty compared to prior periods.

commodity prices weakening demand and tax policy 
implementation causing temporary disruptions in 
distribution channels, the agriculture segment is 
expected to recover in 2026 as the market gradually 
adapts, enterprises and distribution systems adjust, 
and the market positions of key subsidiaries continue to 
be reinforced.

protection, cost optimization, and revenue quality 
enhancement rather than purely scale-driven 
expansion.

The proposed plan is based on a prudent assessment by 
the BOD and Board of Management. Accordingly, 2026 
is anticipated to present many unpredictable variables 
in business operations, particularly in export and 
international trade. Pressures from freight costs, input 
prices, exchange rate fluctuations, and rising trade 
protectionism in certain major markets may continue to 
impact the performance of export-oriented businesses. 
Meanwhile, 
domestic 
and 
regional 
consumption 
demand is expected to improve but may vary across 
industries and customer segments.
Therefore, the 2026 business plans of both individual 
subsidiaries and the consolidated Group are designed 
to achieve reasonable, prudent yet proactive growth, 
with a focus on strengthening operational foundations, 
safeguarding profit margins, and selectively capturing 
market expansion opportunities in areas with clear 
competitive advantages.
In the optimistic scenario, the Board of Directors 
expects export markets may perform more favorably 
than expected, with improved control over freight and 
input costs and reduced policy uncertainties, potentially 
enabling certain business segments to outperform 
planned growth.
The packaged food segment is expected to continue 
growing through expansion in modern trade channels, 
better penetration of regional export markets, and 
acceleration of high value-added product lines. 
However, efficiency in this segment still requires tight 
management due to potential fluctuations in input 
material prices and selling expenses. Meanwhile, the 
nuts and dried fruit segment is oriented toward selective 
growth, focusing on deeply processed products, 
markets with stronger margins, and customers with 
higher stability, rather than pursuing expansion at all 
costs.
The aquaculture sector is expected to remain highly 
volatile in 2026, particularly in terms of consumer 
demand in major markets, price competition, and trade 
policies. However, the final U.S. anti-dumping duty rate 
of 4.58% for “separate rate” companies is significantly 
lower than the unfavorable levels feared last year. This 
outcome provides a more favorable basis for building 
proactive and well-founded export plans for shrimp.
	
Ï Shrimp segment: Revenue and profit are expected to 
grow at mid-single-digit levels, reflecting a cautious 
yet more positive outlook compared to the previous 
year; growth drivers include reduced uncertainty 
regarding anti-dumping duties, continued efficiency 
improvements 
in 
farming 
areas, 
increasing 
proportion of value-added products, and selective 
expansion of orders in key markets.
	
Ï Pangasius segment: The business plan continues to 
be developed cautiously, prioritizing margin protection, 
effective raw material management, and selective 
market engagement, in the context of export price 
levels and demand not yet showing clear recovery.
The agriculture sector including seeds, food grains, 
crop protection products, and fumigation—are expected 
to recover with stronger growth compared to the 
previous year. This outlook is supported by the Group’s 
leading domestic market position, proprietary product 
portfolio, and the gradual adaptation of its distribution 
system to policy changes. Following a period of negative 
impacts from low food prices and short-term distribution 
challenges, 2026 is anticipated to be a more stable year, 
creating favorable conditions for agricultural companies 
to enhance both revenue and efficiency. Packaged rice 
remains a key growth driver, underpinned by 
strengthened brand equity, raw material sourcing, 
processing capabilities, and distribution systems. At 
the same time, consumer demand for premium rice 
products with clear traceability continues to rise in both 
domestic and export markets.

regulations under Circular No. 96/2020/TT-BTC dated 
November 16, 2020 of the Ministry of Finance guiding 
information disclosure on the securities market, and 
Circular No. 68/2024/TT-BTC dated September 18, 2024

BTC, Decision No. 21/QĐ-SGDVN dated December 21,

for shareholders and investors.

or sanctions for violations related to information 
disclosure.

EQUAL TREATMENT OF SHAREHOLDERS
The Company recognizes and respects the rights of 
shareholders, the owners of the Company, including 
minority shareholders and foreign shareholders, by 
ensuring fair and appropriate treatment for each 
shareholder through accurate, transparent, and timely 
disclosure of information. The Company places emphasis 
on the completeness of disclosures so that shareholders 
can make informed decisions at the General Meeting of 
Shareholders, including voting and expressing opinions on 
significant changes and electing members of the Board of 
Directors based on accurate, complete, transparent 
information that is shared fairly. Shareholders’ rights are 
also clearly stipulated in the Company’s Charter and are 
protected by Vietnamese law.
In 2025, the Company successfully organized one Annual 
General Meeting of Shareholders in Hanoi. The Company 
provides shareholders with full meeting invitations, 
including attached documents containing comprehensive 
information related to the meeting. General Meetings of 
Shareholders are conducted in accordance with the 
agenda stated in the meeting invitation. The Chairman of 
the Board of Directors, the Group’s Executive Management, 
and representatives of member companies attended and 
answered questions and provided full information as 
requested by shareholders. The minutes of the General 
Meeting of Shareholders were recorded accurately, 
completely, and promptly in accordance with legal 
regulations and were disclosed together with the 
Resolution of the General Meeting of Shareholders to 
HOSE and published on the Company’s website within 24 
hours after the meeting.

consultations with shareholders to approve matters within 
its authority. The consultation documents were sent to all

146
INVESTOR RELATIONS 
ACTIVITIES 
ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING OF 
SHAREHOLDERS
2025 marks the first time The PAN Group organized its 
Annual Meeting of Shareholders in a hybrid format, 
combining online and in-person meetings. This is one of 
the efforts to raise the standards of the Group’s Investor 
Relations activities, closely following good governance 
practices and more fully meeting governance evaluation 
criteria. The meeting was successful with a total of 157 
shareholders in attendance, along with many guests 
including 
investors 
and 
experts 
from 
financial 
institutions interested in the Group. In particular, thanks 
to the advantage of electronic voting platforms, PAN’s 
2025 Annual General Meeting recorded the highest 
percentage of voting shares present at the meeting 
(62.27%), resulting in very high participation and 
approval rates on all meeting agenda items. With the 
above results, the 2025 Vietnam Listed Company 
Awards (VLCA) honored PAN in many major award 
categories, including the award for Best Annual General 
Meeting Organizer 2025.
INVESTOR NETWORKING AND SEARCH
In 2025, the Group continued to actively seek domestic 
and foreign investors through third-party investor 
networking events such as “SSI Earnings Call HY/FY”, 
“HSC Emerging Vietnam 2025”, etc. Dozens of large 
investment funds in the US, Europe, Japan, South 
Korea, Taiwan, and Hong Kong have been approached 
directly or online by the company, especially some 
investment funds have expressed particular interest 
and worked closely with the Group to promote 
investment opportunities.
Quarterly, the Group holds “Earnings Calls” with 
investors, investment funds, and securities companies 
online immediately after announcing business results. 
At these meetings, Group representatives share the 
latest information on production and business 
operations and answer questions from participants. In 
addition to the four quarterly Earnings Calls, the Group 
also facilitated 34 meetings with institutional investors 
throughout the year to introduce and update on 
production and business activities.
The results of these meetings were very positive, with 
many institutional investors disbursing funds to 
purchase PAN shares, increasing their holdings. In 
total for 2024, the stock grew by 16%, with a peak 
increase of 53% compared to the beginning of the 
year. Trading volume remained at an average of 1.4 
million shares per day, despite a volatile market year. 
Foreign investors continued to net buy VND 71.3 billion 
worth of PAN shares in 2025.
Investor Relations (IR) activities continue to be 
promoted in various forms and have achieved certain 
successes. In 2025, the number of shareholders is 
expected to concentrate in a positive direction, with 
growth in share price and trading volume, accompanied 
by increasing interest from domestic and foreign 
investors in PAN shares.
147
THIRD-PARTY REPORTS
The stock market in 2025 showed strong divergence, 
with only a few sectors and stocks rising to drive the 
index, along with many fluctuations stemming from 
global 
macroeconomic 
information. 
Therefore, 
maintaining investor interest is a challenging task. 
However, the Group has also attracted significant 
attention from investors and securities companies 
with its positive business results, as well as its 
proactive connection and cooperation with analytical 
departments at securities companies. 2025 also saw 
the emergence of many new stock analysis reports in 
the form of videos and chatbots about the Group, 
increasing the reach and accessibility of information 
for investors. Third-party analytical reports are 
collected and published on the website by the Group as 
an objective reference channel for investors.
IR AWARDS 2025
In October 2025, The PAN Group was honored for the 
second consecutive year to be recognized in the Top 3 
Mid-Cap Companies with the highest-rated Investor 
Relations activities by financial institutions. This is a 
well-deserved achievement after efforts to improve and 
raise the standards of IR activities, as well as active 
interaction 
and 
operations, 
creating 
a 
positive 
impression on the investment community.
REGULAR INFORMATION UPDATES ON 
WEBSITE AND FANPAGE
The Group regularly updates information, business 
performance, and other activities in the Investor Relations 
and Communications section on its Website and Fanpage 
for investors in particular and all interested parties in 
general. With a user-friendly interface, the Group’s 
official information channels ensure that investors 
receive accurate, transparent, and timely information.

The PAN Group Joint Stock Company (the “Company”) was established under the Business Registration Certificate 
No. 0301472704 issued by the Ho Chi Minh Authority for Planning and Investment on 31 August 2005, as amended, 
with the latest 24th amendment dated 02 October 2025.
The Company’s shares have been officially listed and traded on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (HOSE) with the 
stock symbol PAN since 18 November 2010.
The Company is headquartered at 81B, National Highway 62, Long An Ward, Tay Ninh Province, Vietnam. In addition, 
the Company has a branch at 15th Floor, ICON4 Building, 243A De La Thanh, Lang Ward, Hanoi, Vietnam.
The total number of employees of the Company and its subsidiaries as at 31 December 2025 is 10,349 (as at 31 
December 2024: 10,850).
On 02 April 2025, U.S. President Donald J. Trump signed an Executive Order imposing a 46% tariff on goods imported 
into the United States from Vietnam. From 05 April 2025 to 06 August 2025, President Trump and the U.S. Government 
implemented a temporary suspension of the reciprocal tariff application on goods imported into the United States 
from certain trading partners (including Vietnam), under which a tariff rate of 10% was applied.
On 31 July 2025, the United States Government issued a new Executive Order to further adjust the Reciprocal Tariff 
policy applied to certain trading partners (including Vietnam), increasing the tariff rate to 20%, effective from 07 
August 2025 until a Bilateral Trade Agreement between the United States and Vietnam is signed.
On 20 February 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled to invalidate the tariffs ranging from 10% to 50% imposed by 
President Donald Trump on all imported goods into the United States. Following this ruling, President Trump signed 
an Executive Order to revoke a series of tariff measures imposed on multiple countries under the IEEPA. However, 
he also announced a 10% tariff on most imported goods into the United States for a period of 150 days, with certain 
exemptions, including minerals, metals and essential energy products.
On 05 June 2025, the U.S. Department of Commerce issued the “Preliminary Results, Notice of Intent to Rescind in 
Part and Final Rescission in Part of the Administrative Review of the Anti-dumping Duty Order for 2023–2024” in 
respect of certain frozen warmwater shrimp products originating from Vietnam for the period from 1 February 2023 
to 31 January 2024 (“POR 19”). According to this announcement, the two mandatory respondents were subject to 
preliminary duty rates of 35.29% and 0%, respectively. Sao Ta Foods Joint Stock Company (“Sao Ta”), a subsidiary of 
the Company, was included in the group of companies eligible for a separate rate, with a preliminary rate of 35.29%.
On 17 February 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce announced the final results for the POR 19 review period. 
Accordingly, the two mandatory respondents were subject to a uniform duty rate of 25.76%. For companies eligible 
for a separate rate but not selected as mandatory respondents (including Sao Ta), the applicable duty rate was 4.58%.
The management of the Company and Sao Ta consider that the international trade environment, particularly the 
U.S. market, continues to involve significant uncertainties and tariff-related risks. Trade remedy policies may 
change in each review period and are heavily influenced by policy, legal factors, and global supply–demand 
developments, which could materially affect the Company’s operations, economic benefits, and obligations. 
Currently, the Board of Directors and management of the Company and Sao Ta are carefully monitoring and 
assessing the potential impacts of these matters on Sao Ta’s operations and are developing appropriate strategies 
to respond to changes in tariff policies.
The main activities of the Company and its subsidiaries are agricultural, food and other related activities, to carry out 
financial investment activities and other related services.
The Company’s normal production and business cycle is carried out for a time period of not more than 12 months.

The accompanying consolidated financial statements, expressed in Vietnam Dong (VND), are 
prepared under the historical cost convention and in accordance with Vietnamese Accounting 
Standards, accounting regime for enterprises and legal regulations relating to consolidated 
financial reporting.  
The consolidated financial statement is prepared based on consolidation of separate financial 
statement of the Company and its subsidiaries’ financial statements. 
The accompanying consolidated financial statements are not intended to present the consolidated 
financial position, consolidated results of operations and consolidated cash flows in accordance 
with accounting principles and practices generally accepted in countries and jurisdictions other 
than Vietnam.
The preparation of consolidated financial statements in conformity with Vietnamese Accounting 
Standards, accounting regime for enterprises and legal regulations relating to consolidated 
financial reporting requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the 
reported amounts of assets, liabilities and disclosures of contingent assets and liabilities at the 
date of the consolidated financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses 
during the financial year. Although these accounting estimates are based on the Chief Executive 
Officer’s best knowledge, actual results may differ from those estimates.
The consolidated financial statements incorporate the financial statements of the Company and 
enterprises controlled by the Company (its subsidiaries) up to 31 December each year. Control is 
achieved where the Company has the power to govern the financial and operating policies of an 
investee enterprise so as to obtain benefits from its activities.
Where necessary, adjustments are made to the financial statements of subsidiaries to bring the 
accounting policies used in line with those used by the Company.
Intragroup transactions and balances are eliminated in full on consolidation.
Non-controlling interests consist of the amount of those non-controlling interests at the date of 
the original business combination and the non-controlling interests’ share of changes in equity 
since the date of the combination. Losses in subsidiaries are respectively attributed to the non-
controlling interests even if this results in the non-controlling interests having a deficit balance. 
On acquisition, the assets and liabilities and contingent liabilities of a subsidiary are measured 
at their fair values at the date of acquisition. Any excess of the cost of acquisition over the fair 
values of the identifiable net assets acquired is recognized as goodwill. Any deficiency of the cost 
of acquisition below the fair values of the identifiable net assets acquired is credited to the 
consolidated profit and loss in the period of acquisition.
In case prior to the date that control was achieved by the Parent Company, a subsidiary is an

Goodwill
Goodwill represents the excess of the cost of acquisition over the Company’s interest in the net fair 
value of the identifiable assets, liabilities and contingent liabilities of a subsidiary, associate or jointly 
controlled entity at the date of acquisition. Goodwill is amortised on the straight-line basis over its 
estimated period of benefit of 10 years.
Goodwill arising on the acquisition of associates and jointly controlled entities is included in the 
carrying amount of the associates and jointly controlled entities. Goodwill arising on the acquisition 
of subsidiaries is presented separately as an asset in the consolidated balance sheet.
On disposal of a subsidiary, associate or jointly controlled entity, the attributable amount of 
unamortised goodwill is included in the determination of the profit or loss on disposal.

Cash and cash equivalents comprise cash on hand, demand deposits and short-term, highly 
liquid investments (not exceeding 3 months) that are readily convertible to known amounts of 
cash and which are subject to an insignificant risk of changes in value.
Receivables represent the amounts recoverable from customers or other debtors and are stated

Provision for doubtful debts is made for receivables that are overdue, or when the debtor is in 
dissolution, in bankruptcy, or is experiencing similar difficulties and so may be unable to repay 
the debt.
Inventories are stated at the lower of cost and net realizable value. 
The cost of inventories include:
	
Ï For manufacturing activities: direct materials, direct labour and overheads, if any, incurred in 
bringing the inventories to their present location and condition;
	
Ï For trading activities: purchase costs and other costs directly attributable to the purchase of 
inventories;
The Group applies the perpetual inventory method to account for inventories, except for Sao Ta 
Foods Joint Stock Company - a subsidiary of the Company, which applies the periodic inventory 
method to account for work-in-progress production costs. The cost of inventories is determined 
by the weighted average method. Net realizable value is determined by the estimated selling 
price less the estimated costs of completion and marketing, selling and distribution costs 
incurred.
The Group’s inventory allowance is made in accordance with current accounting regulations. 
Accordingly, the Company is allowed to make allowance for obsolete, damaged, or substandard 
inventories and in cases where the cost of inventories is higher than the net realizable value at 
the end of the financial year.
Trading securities
Trading securities are those the Company holds for trading purpose. Trading securities are 
recognised from the date the Company obtains the ownership of those securities and initially 
measured at the fair value of payments made at the transaction date plus directly attributable 
transaction costs. 
In subsequent years, investments in trading securities are measured at cost less provision for 
impairment of such investments.
Provision for impairment of investments in trading securities is made when there has been 
evidenced that their market prices are lower than their costs in accordance with prevailing 
accounting regulations.
Held-to-maturity investments
Held-to-maturity investments comprise investments that the Company has the positive intent or 
ability to hold to maturity. Held-to-maturity investments comprise term deposits and bonds to 
earn periodic interest.
Post-acquisition interest income from held-to-maturity investments is recognised in the 
consolidated income statement on accrual basis. 
Loan receivables
Loan receivables are measured at cost less provision for doubtful debts. Provision for doubtful 
debts relating to loan receivables is made in accordance with prevailing accounting regulations.
Equity investments in other entities
Equity investments in other entities represent the Group’s investments in ordinary shares of the 
entities over which the Group has no control, joint control, or significant influence. 
Equity investments in other entities are carried at cost less provision for impairment. Provision 
for impairment of equity investments in other entities are made when there has been evidenced 
that indicating impairment of these investments as of the end of the accounting year.
Tangible fixed assets are stated at cost less accumulated depreciation. 
The costs of purchased tangible fixed assets comprise their purchase prices and any directly

Bonds are issued as long-term borrowings. 
Carrying value of straight bonds is recorded on net basis, equal to bonds’ nominal amount 
less (-) Bond discount plus (+) Bond premium.
The Group accounts for the issued bonds’ discount and premiums individually and recognizes 
their amortization for the purpose of determining borrowing costs which are recorded as 
expenses or capitalized during each period, as follows:
	
Ï Bond discount is amortized gradually during bonds’ life, accounted for as borrowing costs;
	
Ï Bond premium is amortized gradually during bonds’ life, reducing borrowing costs;
The discount or premium is allocated using the straight-line method. The discount or premium 
is allocated evenly over the term of the bond.
The cost of issuing bonds is gradually allocated in accordance with the term of the bond using the 
straight-line method and recorded in financial expenses. At the time of initial recognition, the 
cost of issuing bonds is recorded as a reduction of the principal of the bond. Periodically, the cost 
of issuing bonds is allocated by recording an increase in the principal value and recorded in 
financial expenses in accordance with the recognition of the interest payable on the bond.

The severance allowance for employees is accrued at the end of each financial year for all 
employees having worked at the Group for full 12 months and above. Working time serving as the 
basis for calculating severance allowance shall be the total actual working time subtracting the 
time when the employees have made unemployment insurance contributions as prescribed by 
law, and the working time when severance allowance has been paid to the employees. The 
allowance made for each year of service equals to a half of an average monthly salary under the 
Vietnamese Labor Code, Social Insurance Code and relevant guiding documents. The average 
monthly salary used for calculation of severance allowance shall be adjusted to be the average 
of the 6 consecutive months nearest to the date of the consolidated financial statements at the 
end of each financial year. The increase or decrease in the accrued amount shall be recorded in

Revenue from sale of goods
Revenue from the sale of goods is recognised when all five (5) following conditions are satisfied:
(a) the Group has transferred to the buyer the significant risks and rewards of ownership of the goods;
(b) the Group retains neither continuing managerial involvement to the degree usually associated 
with; ownership nor effective control over the goods sold;
(c) the amount of revenue can be measured reliably;
(d) it is probable that the economic benefits associated with the transaction will flow to the Group; and
(e) the costs incurred or to be incurred in respect of the transaction can be measured reliably.
Revenue from service rendered
Revenue of a transaction involving the rendering of services is recognised when the outcome of 
such transactions can be measured reliably. Where a transaction involving the rendering of 
services is attributable to several years, revenue is recognised in each year by reference to the 
percentage of completion of the transaction at the balance sheet date of that period. The outcome 
of a transaction can be measured reliably when all four (4) following conditions are satisfied:
(a) the amount of revenue can be measured reliably;
(b) it is probable that the economic benefits associated with the transaction will flow to the Group;
(c) the percentage of completion of the transaction at the consolidated balance sheet date can be 
measured reliably; and
(d) the costs incurred for the transaction and the costs to complete the transaction can be 
measured reliably.
Interest on deposits and investments
Interest income from deposits is recognized on an accrual basis, based on the outstanding 
balances and the applicable interest rate.
Interest income from investments is recognized when the Group’s right to receive payment has 
been established.

Income tax expense represents the sum of the tax currently payable and deferred tax.
The tax currently payable is based on taxable profit for the period. Taxable profit differs from 
profit before tax as reported in the consolidated income statement because it excludes items of 
income or expense that are taxable or deductible in other years (including loss carried forward, 
if any) and it further excludes items that are never taxable or deductible. 
Deferred tax is recognised on significant differences between carrying amounts of assets and 
liabilities in the interim consolidated financial statements and the corresponding tax bases used 
in the computation of taxable profit and is accounted for using balance sheet liability method. 
Deferred tax liabilities are generally recognised for all temporary differences and deferred tax 
assets are recognised to the extent that it is probable that taxable profit will be available against 
which deductible temporary differences can be utilised. 
Taxation 
As at 31 December 2025, the Parent company, PAN-Hulic Joint Stock Company, PAN Farm Joint 
Stock Company and Golden Beans Coffee Joint Stock - subsidiaries of the Company - did not 
recognize deferred tax assets for tax losses that could be used to offset taxable profits in the 
future within a maximum period of 5 consecutive years following the year the tax loss was 
incurred due to uncertainty about future profits.
Deferred tax is calculated at the tax rates that are expected to apply in the period when the 
liability is settled or the asset realised. Deferred tax is charged or credited to profit or loss, 
except when it relates to items charged or credited directly to equity, in which case the deferred 
tax is also dealt with in equity.
Deferred tax assets and liabilities are offset when there is a legally enforceable right to set off 
current tax assets against current tax liabilities and when they relate to income taxes levied by 
the same tax authority and the Group intends to settle its current tax assets and liabilities on a 
net basis. 
The determination of the tax currently payable is based on the current interpretation of tax 
regulations. However, these regulations are subject to periodic variation and their ultimate 
determination depends on the results of the tax authorities’ examinations.
Other taxes are paid in accordance with the prevailing tax laws in Vietnam.

This represents anti-dumping tax expenses incurred when Sao Ta Foods Joint Stock Company - a subsidiary 
of the Company (“FMC”) – exports shrimp to the United States market in accordance with the anti-dumping 
regulations of the U.S. Department of Commerce. Such expenses are estimated and accrued by the Company 
and recognized in profit or loss during the respective periods in relation to shrimp export shipments to this 
market, as detailed below:
For the period from 01 February 2023 to 31 January 2024, FMC is setting aside a provision for anti-dumping tax at 
a rate of 4.58%, which is the rate according to the final results from the U.S. Department of Commerce for the 
review period from 01 February 2023 to 31 January 2024 (“POR 19”), published on 17 February 2026.
For the period from 01 February 2024 to the end of fiscal year, which falls under the anti-dumping tax review 
currently being conducted by the U.S. Department of Commerce for the period from 01 February 2024 to 31 January 
2025 (“POR 20”) and for which no final conclusion has been reached, as well as for the subsequent period up to 31 
December 2025, the U.S. Department of Commerce has not yet conducted a review. Based on the actual situation 
of tariff imposition by the U.S. authorities and the developments in the outcome of the anti-dumping tax case for 
POR 19, FMC assesses that the potential tariff situation carries a high level of risk, is continuously volatile, and 
unpredictable. The Company is currently setting aside an anti-dumping tax provision amounting to VND 
332,803,004,376 based on reference tax rates derived from the history of previous POR periods.
The Vietnamese seafood industry, especially the export of shrimp to the U.S. market, is frequently affected by 
trade remedy measures (anti-dumping) imposed by the U.S. Department of Commerce through each administrative 
review period. Therefore, FMC assesses that the tax rate currently applied for POR 20 as well as the subsequent 
period up to 31 December 2025, appropriately reflects the competitive pricing situation of frozen warm-water 
shrimp originating from Vietnam exported to the U.S. market and the international trade environment, particularly 
the U.S. market, which continues to be prone to fluctuations. The payable tax and related tax costs will be adjusted 
in accordance with the final decision of the U.S. Department of Commerce in the near future.

30. BUSINESS AND GEOGRAPHICAL SEGMENTS 
The Group chooses business segments as the main reporting ones because the Group’s risks and profitability are 
primarily impacted by the differences in products and services provided by the Group. Segments by geography are 
secondary reporting ones. The Group’s business activities are organized and managed according to the nature of the 
products and services provided by the Group with each division being a strategic business unit that provides different 
products and serves different markets.
The Group consists of segments divided by main business activities as follows:
	
Ï Agriculture;
	
Ï Food production and processing;
	
Ï Others.
The Group’s business activities include export and domestic activities.
Prices applied to transactions between segments are determined on the same basis as with third parties. Revenue, 
expenses, and business results of segments include transactions between them. These transactions are eliminated 
when preparing the consolidated financial statements.

In 2025, Vietnamese enterprises in general, and The PAN Group 
in particular, faced a convergence of multifaceted challenges: 
volatility in U.S. tariff policies, the increasingly extreme impacts 
of natural disasters and floods, and escalating global demands 
for quality, environmental stewardship, and social responsibility. 
These “giant waves” have become an unavoidable reality.
With the theme “Steadfast Heart – Bold Step,” The PAN Group’s 
2025 Sustainability Report demonstrates a long-term vision - 
remaining resolute in our commitment to sustainable 
development despite short-term fluctuations. Our “Go Global 
– Go Green” strategy continues to serve as our North Star, 
aimed at elevating the value and position of Vietnamese 
agricultural products in the global market, embodying the spirit 
of “embracing difficulties, not avoiding them.”

MESSAGE FROM THE CEO
The year 2025 concluded with unprecedented challenges 
for the Vietnamese business community. Global trade 
volatility, U.S. tariff policies, and the increasingly severe 
impacts of natural disasters created significant “waves” 
that tested the resilience and adaptability of every 
enterprise. In this context, The PAN Group chose a clear 
path: steadfast commitment to a long-term strategy – 
staying resilient amid short-term fluctuations.
The “Go Global – Go Green” strategy continues to serve as 
the guiding principle for all our activities. PAN remains 
committed to enhancing the value of Vietnamese agricultural 
products in international markets, while promoting green 
transformation and transparent governance, aiming for 
sustainable growth rather than growth at any cost.
For the PAN Group, we define the success of 2025 not 
merely by growth figures. The most valuable achievement 
of the Group is the breakthrough in cooperation and 
cohesion among the units within the agricultural ecosystem. 
And perhaps this is also the greatest foundation for jointly 
creating very proud accomplishments. PAN’s consolidated 
revenue in 2025 reached approximately 17.586 billion VND, 
profit nearly 1.165 billion VND, and contributions to the state 
budget amounted to 497.2 billion VND. Notably, in key 
agricultural sectors such as rice, aquaculture, packaged 
foods, fish sauce, and nuts, all have overcome difficulties to 
achieve strong growth, contributing to the overall 
development of the Group as well as bringing better income 
to farmers.
The past year was also one in which PAN focused on 
strengthening internal capabilities and improving 
governance quality. Member companies proactively 
restructured, 
innovated 
products, 
invested 
in 
technology, and advanced green transformation. The 
area of high-quality, low-emission rice models in the 
Mekong Delta was expanded to 47,520 hectares—an 
increase of 47 times compared to 2024. Units operating 
in the aquaculture sector successfully implemented for 
the first time the project “Farming whiteleg shrimp in 
freshwater areas” under a closed-loop model, this 
initiative enhances our control over high-quality seed 
supply 
and 
strengthens 
our 
resilience 
against 
environmental and water resource fluctuations. Green 
transformation efforts continued to be accelerated, 
with total rooftop solar power capacity increasing to 
5.53 MWp, while circular economy models and biological 
production continued to be expanded.
The Group currently has 10,349 employees working 
nationwide, of which 48% are female and 33% from ethnic 
minority groups—reflects our dedication to fostering 
diversity, equality, and inclusion in the workplace. 
Compensation and benefits policies are maintained 
steadily; the average income of direct workers reaches 
1.45 times higher than the regional minimum wage.
Alongside strengthening internal capabilities, PAN continued 
to expand value chain linkages by collaborating with 50,700 
farmers and 221 cooperatives under product off-take models, 
contributing to improved incomes and sustainable livelihoods 
in local communities. The Group contributed more than 7.48 
billion VND to community activities, affirming a consistent, 
long-term commitment to social responsibility.
In 2025, PAN continued to be recognized among the Top 
100 Sustainable Companies in Vietnam for the 6th 
consecutive year, the Top 20 listed companies with the 
best ESG practices, and the Top 50 Pioneering Enterprises 
committed to enhancing corporate governance standards 
in Vietnam (VNCG50). It is also among the 20 pioneering 
companies improving corporate governance quality 
under the ASEAN Corporate Governance Scorecard.
With the spirit of “Steadfast Heart – Bold Step”, The PAN 
Group remains committed to pursuing economic growth 
in parallel with sustainable development, contributing to 
elevating Vietnamese agriculture on the global map. We 
believe that only by maintaining resilience in the face of 
volatility and staying true to core values can a business 
create long-term impacts for society.
I would like to express my sincere gratitude to our shareholders, 
customers, and partners for your continued trust and 
companionship. In particular, I extend my appreciation to the 
PAN team—individuals who have continuously strived to turn 
challenges into opportunities. We are committed to ongoing 
innovation, transparency, and leadership in building 
sustainable values for today and future generations.
Sincerely,
Nguyen Thi Tra My

SUPPLY CHAIN
AGRICULTURE
PAN Group continuously promotes the integration of sustainable 
development factors into its procurement and supply chain 
management activities, with a focus on environmental, social, 
and business ethics issues. The Group has developed and 
implemented a set of criteria for evaluating suppliers and 
partners, serving as a basis for selection, collaboration, and 
periodic monitoring, with priority given to partners that comply 
with legal regulations and demonstrate stronger adherence to 
sustainable development standards.
In addition to evaluation activities, PAN emphasizes accompanying 
and enhancing the capacity of partners within the value chain, 
aiming to build a responsible, transparent, and resilient supply 
ecosystem with long-term adaptability.
The Group is currently collaborating with more than 
1,500 agents supplying seeds and agricultural inputs, 
over 220 cooperatives, and 50,453 farming households 
engaged in rice production linkages. Through its 
member companies such as Vinaseed and VFC, PAN 
regularly implements training programs, capacity-
building activities, and the transfer of sustainable 
farming 
solutions, 
contributing 
to 
improved 
productivity, optimized input use, and reduced 
environmental impact.
PACKAGED FOOD
AQUACULTURE
In the seafood sector, PAN Group collaborates with six agents and 
approximately 170 shrimp farming households, supplying key export markets 
such as the United States, Europe, and Japan.
The Group integrates environmental, social, and human rights 
criteria into supplier selection and evaluation through its 
Code of Conduct and periodic assessment system. At the 
same time, PAN implements training programs and works 
closely with agents and farming households to enhance 
sustainable aquaculture practices, ensure product quality, 
and strengthen transparency across the supply chain.
In the food sector, we collaborate with one coffee-
growing cooperative, one cashew-growing cooperative, 
and 38 farming households in raw material regions in 
Bình Phước and Gia Lai, contributing to the development 
of a stable and traceable supply source.
Our partners receive annual training and technology 
transfer on sustainable farming practices from the 
Group. We also provide partial support for input costs 
and commit to purchasing their products at prices at 
least 20% higher than the market rate.

In 2025, The PAN Group continued to maintain stable 
economic performance amid ongoing volatility in the 
agriculture–food and seafood markets due to the 
impacts of input costs, weather conditions, and global 
consumption trends. With sustainable development as 
its foundation, PAN focused on enhancing governance 
capacity, 
optimizing 
operational 
efficiency, 
and 
strengthening its core business areas.
According to consolidated business results, the Group’s 
net revenue reached VND 17,586 billion, an increase of 
8.7% compared to 2024 and achieving 102% of the annual 
plan. This result reflects a positive market recovery as 
well as the effectiveness of flexible management 
solutions, cost control, and market expansion.
In terms of profitability, consolidated profit after tax 
reached 1,165 billion VND, of which profit after tax 
attributable to the parent company’s shareholders was

Vietnam Context
In 2020, Vietnam committed to reducing greenhouse 
gas (GHG) emissions by 15.8% by 2030, and up to 43.5% 
with international support. This commitment was to be 
updated in 2022 to align with the ambition of achieving 
net-zero emissions by 2050. To realize these goals, the 
Government of Vietnam has issued a series of supporting 
policies. Under Decision No. 942/QĐ-TTg dated August 
5, 2022, Vietnam aims to reduce total methane emissions 
by at least 30% by 2030 compared to 2020 levels across 
sectors including crop production, livestock, solid waste 
management, wastewater treatment, oil and gas 
extraction, coal mining, and fossil fuel consumption. In 
2025, ministries and agencies also piloted a carbon 
trading exchange through 2028, with official operation 
expected from 2029.
On June 9, 2025, the Government issued Decree No. 
119/2025/NĐ-CP, amending and supplementing several 
articles of Decree No. 06/2022/NĐ-CP dated January 7, 
2022, on greenhouse gas emission mitigation and ozone 
layer protection.
Among them, Khang An Foods – a member company of 
PAN Group – is also subject to regulations on greenhouse 
gas emission reduction, GHG inventory, and disclosure 
of environmental and social information. This requires 
us to continuously improve production processes and 
reduce energy-related emissions to effectively meet 
emission reduction requirements while ensuring 
transparency in disclosures.
Notably, in 2025, two major government resolutions—
Resolution 68 on private sector development and 
Resolution 57 on science and technology—are expected 
to accelerate digital transformation, contributing to the 
realization of Vietnam’s Vision 2045 of becoming a 
developed, high-income country.
PAN Group’s products are currently present in more 
than 40 countries and territories, with key markets 
including the United States, Europe, and Vietnam. We 
position ourselves as an active and proactive player in 
the green transition across all the countries and 
territories where we operate. Sustainable development 
and the green economy are increasingly becoming 
mandatory standards in international markets, while 
the rise of trade protectionism and technical barriers is 
placing higher demands on exporting enterprises.
Although these requirements present challenges, they 
also open up significant opportunities for Vietnamese 
businesses. 
By 
proactively 
adapting, 
embracing 
innovation, and shifting business strategies toward 
green and sustainable models, companies can 
overcome barriers, enhance their market position, and 
create ESG value.

The identification of material topics serves as the foundation for developing 
and implementing PAN Group’s sustainable development strategy toward 
2030. We actively listen to and thoughtfully consider feedback and input 
from stakeholders who are directly and indirectly affected by the Group’s 
production and business activities. Accordingly, the Group’s approach is 
based on a double materiality principle, including:

OPERATIONS ON THE ECONOMY,

THE INFLUENCE OF ECONOMIC, SOCIAL, 
AND ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS ON THE

AND VALUE CREATION CAPACITY

conducted through the following key steps:
IDENTIFICATION OF

INTERNAL CONSULTATION 
AND REVIEW
PRIORITIZATION AND
IDENTIFICATION OF MATERIAL TOPICS
The initial list is compiled based on: the operational 
characteristics of PAN’s ecosystem in the 
agriculture, aquaculture, and food sectors; the 
Farm – Food – Family value chain; GRI Standards, 
legal 
requirements, 
market 
trends, 
and 
stakeholder expectations.
Each topic is evaluated against the following 
criteria: severity of impact (including scale, scope, 
and remediability); likelihood of occurrence, 
covering both actual and potential impacts; scope 
of impact, distinguishing between direct impacts 
within the Group’s operations and indirect impacts 
across the supply chain; and the level of impact on 
key stakeholders.
The assessment results are reviewed with the 
participation of the Management Board and 
representatives of member companies to ensure 
they fully reflect the operational context, level of 
control, and the Group’s risk management and 
governance capacity.
Issues are prioritized based on their overall level of 
impact and strategic significance to the Group, 
forming the basis for developing the materiality 
matrix and selecting key topics for disclosure in the 
Sustainability Report.
The results of this assessment will shape PAN Group’s 
long-term sustainable development strategy.

amount of packaging materials. These packages are 
optimally designed in terms of size and materials to suit 
the specific production characteristics of each region.

recycling of discarded packaging for purposes such as 
packing raw materials, agricultural by-products, or 
selling them for recycling.

Mekong Delta region. Under this initiative, participating 
farmers and distributors receive VND 8,000 for each 
returned used package. From June to December 2025, 
the program collected 20,000 PP bags, equivalent to 
approximately 4 tons of packaging. All collected

raw material packaging and by-product handling.

aquaculture to enhance the resilience of shrimp and fish, 
improve pond water quality, reduce the frequency of water

seasons, as reflected in low pond losses, high survival rates of

Animal Welfare
Marketing, and Labeling
Increasingly stringent animal welfare requirements are 
driving changes across farming, harvesting, and processing 
practices. Initially, compliance with ASC farming standards 
was required. These requirements have since been tightened, 
particularly regarding stocking density, which must not be 
excessive, and the need to strictly control environmental 
parameters such as dissolved oxygen and toxic gases… 
Further requirements mandate that shrimp, once harvested 
and brought to the surface, must be humanely killed and 
preserved by icing within 2 minutes. Subsequently, during net 
harvesting, the use of electrical stimulation to drive shrimp into 
nets is prohibited. More recently, customers have required 
faster and more humane slaughter methods, specifically by 
electrical stunning, as currently applied by Sao Ta. Looking 
ahead, a growing trend is the installation of underwater 
cameras in shrimp ponds to monitor animal behavior and 
welfare in real time.
